How do I clear an old mortgage from the Forsyth County record?

The lender or noteholder cancels it by recording a satisfaction, and the office charges nothing to record one.

The county explains that a deed of trust or mortgage is a security instrument that is canceled once the debt is paid, while a deed is title and is never canceled. Cancellation is the responsibility of the owner or noteholder in the county where the instrument was recorded. The county lists several forms that can do the job: a satisfaction of security instrument, a trustee's satisfaction, a notice of satisfaction, a certificate of satisfaction and an affidavit of satisfaction.

Do not assume the lender has acted. The office states that payoff papers and satisfactions are not mailed to the borrower automatically after the loan is paid in full. A borrower can call the register of deeds to check that the loan is marked satisfied before ordering a copy of the record.

Where do tax maps and deed lookups fit in Forsyth County?

The tax office's parcel maps show lot lines, but the deed is the legal description to rely on.

The county's tax FAQ warns that parcel dimensions on tax maps are calculated for tax purposes only, and the acreage on a tax record may not match the deeded or platted acreage. To find legal lot dimensions, open the Deeds tab on the parcel's property detail page or use the register of deeds lookup. That is the practical step before a sale where a fence, a split lot or an old boundary dispute is in play.

What other services and fees does the Forsyth County office list?

Besides land records, the office charges for notary work and vital records, and it waives fees for some military papers.

  • Notary public: $10, and notarial acts are $5 for each signature, except when performed with an act that already carries a fee.
  • Comparing a copy for certification: $5.
  • Recording a military discharge and getting a copy: no fee, and the Thank a Veteran photo ID is also free.
  • Certified birth or death certificate: $10; marriage license: $60.

Heirs who need a certified death certificate pay $10 for it according to the fee page. Call the office to confirm which of these documents can be issued the same day.

More questions about Forsyth County, NC Register of Deeds

How much does the Forsyth County office charge for filing a document?

Nothing is added for a satisfaction of a deed of trust, and the other charges follow the county's fee sheet, which G.S. 161-10 backs.

Will the Forsyth County office accept my personal check?

No. The fee page rules out personal checks, counter checks and e-checks. Business checks, official bank checks, money orders and credit or debit cards work.

What is the cutoff for an e-filed deed in Forsyth County?

E-filed items need to land by 4:30 p.m. on a business day. Counter and mail filings follow the regular weekday hours.

Who covers the excise tax on a Forsyth County sale?

The seller pays it to the register of deeds first. The rate is one dollar per $500 block of value, and a partial block is rounded up.

Can staff at the Forsyth County registry help draft my deed?

No. The office records papers only, and state law keeps staff from giving legal advice or showing how to draft an instrument, so see an attorney.

Franklin County by the numbers

Where is the Franklin County Register of Deeds?

The Franklin County Register of Deeds is at 283-B S. Bickett Boulevard in Louisburg, NC 27549, after a move made while the county courthouse is under construction. The mailing address is P.O. Box 545, Louisburg, NC 27549, the phone is 919-496-3500 and the fax is 919-496-1457.

The county describes the office as the custodian of real estate documents for Franklin County that reach back to 1776. For a sale anywhere in Franklin County, this is the office that holds the deed you received, the deed of trust on it and any plat or power of attorney tied to the parcel. Credit card payments are available. Because the office relocated recently, check the county page before you drive over with a document, and mail or e-record when you can.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Franklin County house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

What records does the Franklin County office keep?

Land records and vital records share one counter, and the land side matters most to a seller. For a home sale the land records matter most.

  • Deeds and deeds of trust, the documents that move title and secure a loan.
  • Powers of attorney, assumed names, maps and other papers connected to real property.
  • Military discharge records.
  • Birth and death certificates back to 1913 for events in Franklin County, and marriage certificates back to 1869, with a bond book that carries marriage information from 1779.

The office can also print birth and death certificates from the state system for North Carolina events, and it takes online orders for certified or regular copies of vital records through a county vendor. A seller dealing with an inherited house often needs a death certificate and the old deed from the same visit.

Does Franklin County require tax certification before a deed is recorded?

Yes. A deed moving real property is turned away unless the Tax Collector first certifies that no delinquent ad valorem or other administered tax is a lien on it. The county has applied this rule since April 1, 2015.

The Collections Department stamps deeds free of charge on weekdays between 8 am and 5 pm, excluding county holidays. There are three ways to get it done.

  • Walk the deed in to Collections before recording.
  • Mail it to the Franklin County Tax Collector, P.O. Box 503, Louisburg, NC 27549, Attention: Tax Certification.
  • Use eRecording, which forwards deeds to the tax office on its own.

Electronic recordings that need the stamp must reach the tax department by 4:30 pm, so a closing that wraps up late should send its package early.

For a seller with back taxes, this is where the problem surfaces. The deed waits until the balance is cleared or the closing agent pays it out of the proceeds.

Can I record a Franklin County deed electronically?

Yes. Title companies, banks, attorneys and private individuals can all submit electronically, and every document type is accepted except UCC filings.

The county names three authorized providers: CSC eRecording Solutions (866-652-0111), Simplifile (800-460-5657) and the ePN eRecording Partners Network (888-325-3365). Its stated benefits are quicker recording, lower postage and courier spending, fewer rejected documents and added security. Closing attorneys normally choose the provider, so a seller rarely sets this up personally. Ask which day your closing will be recorded.

What will a Franklin County closing pay at the Register of Deeds?

Two charges apply at the counter: a page-based recording fee and a tax tied to the sale price.

For the recording fee, the state tier is $26 for a general instrument through page 15, with $4 added for every page after that. A deed of trust is $64 through page 35. Recording the release of a paid-off loan is free. A certified copy starts at $5, and a document that does not meet the standard format costs $25 more.

The deed tax comes to a dollar for each $500 of price or value, and a leftover fraction counts as another $500. The party giving up the property pays it at the register of deeds window ahead of recording, and the proceeds are divided between the county and state revenue. Your settlement statement will carry the final number.

Who handles each step when I sell in Franklin County?

Four parties handle separate pieces of a sale, as the county's own pages describe them.

Franklin County offices and the part each plays in a sale
OfficeWhat it doesContact
Register of DeedsRecords the deed and deed of trust, keeps land records and collects the recording fees919-496-3500

Tax AdministrationSets values and handles real estate value appealsCounty Tax Office, through the Value Appeals page
eRecording providerSends the signed documents to the Register of Deeds electronicallyCSC, Simplifile or ePN

Sources for the table are the county Register of Deeds, Collections, Value Appeals and Electronic Recording pages listed below.

How do Franklin County tax bills affect a seller?

Real estate tax in the county is due each September 1, and the 2026 bills turn delinquent on January 6, 2027. The county mails bills in late July to early August, and money received before September 1 can earn a discount.

When a house sells after the bill arrives, the county tells the former owner to hand the bill to the buyer unless the former owner will pay it. Agreements between buyers, sellers and attorneys are not the tax office's concern, and because tax is a lien on real estate, the buyer wants everything settled at closing. A mortgage company that escrows tax still causes the bill to be mailed to the owner, and the county suggests checking in the second week of September that the lender paid. A Solid Waste Availability Fee is also billed per electrical connection. The commissioners set it each year, and part-time use of the home does not exempt you.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

What is the process to dispute a Franklin County assessed value?

An owner files the Board of Equalization and Review form between January 1 and the board's adjournment, which usually falls in May. A change-of-value notice opens a separate 30-day window.

Staff look at the file first. Anything they cannot settle goes to the board, which mails its decision. The current revaluation took effect January 1, 2024, so the county wants evidence tied to that date. Higher bills, fixed income and market drops after January 1, 2024 are not legal grounds. Comparable properties with lower values, comparable sales before that date, unrepaired fire or storm damage, a denied septic permit and documented cleanup costs are. The owner carries the burden of proof. If the worry is affordability, ask the tax office about relief programs.

Why does recording order matter on a Franklin County sale?

Registration time decides priority. Under G.S. 47-18, a deed, option, lease longer than three years and similar interests do not bind lien creditors or paying buyers until they are registered in the county where the land sits.

That explains why closings are timed around recording cutoffs, and why an unrecorded deed from a former owner can stall a new sale. If an inherited Franklin County house still shows the deceased relative as owner, check the index before you list and ask your closing attorney what must be recorded first.

More questions about Franklin County, NC Register of Deeds

Is the Franklin County Register of Deeds in the courthouse?

No, not at present. The office now sits at 283-B S. Bickett Boulevard in Louisburg while the courthouse is under construction. Mail goes to P.O. Box 545, Louisburg, NC 27549, and the phone is 919-496-3500.

Do I need a tax certification stamp to record a deed in Franklin County?

Yes, for any deed that transfers real property. The Tax Collector must certify there is no delinquent tax lien, free of charge on weekdays from 8 am to 5 pm. eRecording sends the deed to the tax office for you.

What does Franklin County charge to record?

The statewide tier applies: $26 through page 15 for a general instrument and $64 through page 35 for a deed of trust, plus $4 per extra page. Confirm with the office before mailing a long document.

Can a title company record electronically in Franklin County?

Yes. The office accepts all document types electronically except UCC filings, through CSC, Simplifile or the ePN network. The company or closing attorney normally handles the submission.

Who pays the North Carolina deed excise tax?

The seller pays it when the deed is brought in for recording. The rate is one dollar per $500 of value. The settlement statement shows the amount.

Where is the Gaston County Register of Deeds?

The office is on the first floor of the Gaston County Courthouse at 325 Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. Way, Gastonia, NC 28052. That address was formerly listed as 325 N. Marietta Street, so older deeds, letters and directions may still show the old street name.

Mail goes to P.O. Box 1578, Gastonia, NC 28053, and the phone is 704-862-7681. The office is open from 8:30 am to 5 pm. No appointment is needed to use the records or to take a notary oath.

What changed in Gaston County's online records search?

The office switched to a new records vendor on Thursday, May 28, 2026, and the old system has been retired. The county says every record from the old system is now in the new one, so bookmarks and links that pointed to the old site need updating.

The public search is the place to look for deeds, deeds of trust and other property records. Some older records are not online, and the county asks you to visit or call for help with those. Uncertified copies can be pulled online. For a certified copy you can use the county's Certified Copy Request Portal, call 704-862-7681, email rod@gastongov.com or go to the office. A seller who needs a prior deed to prove how the family took title will usually want a certified copy for the closing attorney.

What else does the Gaston County office do besides deeds?

The office records and indexes deeds, plats, maps, deeds of trust, mortgages and other personal property documents, and it also issues marriage licenses and keeps birth and death certificates. It runs a passport service as well, and most of the money from passport fees goes to the U.S. Department of State, with a portion kept for the county general fund.

Paper records are kept in vaults, and digital copies sit on secure servers in the courthouse. The fees the office takes in for recording are far larger than its operating budget, so they help fund the county and the state general funds. If the office ever has a vacancy, the Board of County Commissioners appoints someone to fill the unexpired term.

What do copies and counter payments cost at the Gaston office?

Per the office's FAQ, plain copies run $0.25 a page. Certified copies start at $5 for page one, and each added page is $2.

Accepted ways to pay Register of Deeds fees:

  • Cash.
  • Business check or money order, made out to Gaston County Register of Deeds.
  • Debit or credit card.

Staff will point you to the books and help with the computers, though state law bars them from doing title research, and they cannot run a lien check for you. A lost deed can be replaced with a copy bought in person or requested in writing at the P.O. Box. Changing names on a deed means drawing a new deed, and the office suggests an attorney, since it keeps no legal forms for deeds or powers of attorney.

How much does the Gaston office charge to file a closing package?

The county's FAQ sends you to the uniform fee schedule, which tracks G.S. 161-10.

  • A general instrument is $26 through page 15, and each page past 15 adds $4.
  • A mortgage or deed of trust is $64 through page 35, with the same $4 for each extra page.
  • Recording a satisfaction of a paid-off loan costs nothing.
  • A plat is $21 a sheet.
  • Each extra instrument inside one document adds $10.

Transfer tax is a separate line, set by G.S. 105-228.30 at a dollar per $500 of price (any remainder counts as another $500). The seller pays it when the deed is presented.

Can Gaston County help protect me from deed and lien fraud?

Yes. The office partners with the county's land records software provider to offer a free notification service. You sign up with a name and an email address, and you are alerted when a recording is filed in your name.

The county is clear that no system can prevent fraud. The alerts are meant to help you spot a bad filing quickly, which matters if you own a vacant, inherited or rental house in Gaston County and might not see the mail. Anyone who prepares a document for recording is also barred from including Social Security, bank account, card or similar numbers unless the law requires it. If one does appear, you can ask in writing for it to be removed from the online image under G.S. 132-1.10(g). There is no fee for that request, though the underlying filing stays in the public record.

How do Gaston County property values and appeals tie to a sale?

Gaston reappraises every four years. The most recent value date was January 1, 2023, and 2027 is the next one, preceded by an informal review before the Board of Equalization and Review sits.

Owners may file from January 1 until that board adjourns, typically the last week of April, or until 30 days after a Notice of Value Change if that is later. The Tax Office is at 128 West Main Avenue in Gastonia, phone 704-866-3158. Property tax is billed separately from anything the Register of Deeds collects and stays with the property until paid, so buyers expect it settled at closing. Our Gaston County property tax guide covers rates, relief programs and payment options in detail.

Why does the order of recording matter for a Gaston County seller?

Whoever registers first generally wins priority. G.S. 47-18 says a conveyance or lease over three years does not bind lien creditors or paying buyers until it is on record where the land lies.

So before a buyer's deed goes in, confirm that earlier deeds in the chain, any estate documents and the release of a paid-off loan are all indexed. Releases are free to record. Ask your closing attorney to search the index and send the satisfaction of your old mortgage ahead of the sale.

What should an heir of a Gaston County house record before selling?

Settle the estate paperwork first. A deed signed by someone who does not yet hold title will not clear. For a small estate without a will, the state allows a small estate affidavit under G.S. 28A-25-1, filed where the decedent lived.

That route covers up to $20,000 in personal property after liens, and the affidavit lists every tract of land owned. Whatever route fits your family, the paper that gives you authority to sell lands in the Gastonia index, so build in time before the closing date.

Mail them to Gaston County Register of Deeds, P.O. Box 1578, Gastonia, NC 28053. For overnight service the county suggests an express envelope with a prepaid return envelope enclosed.

Real estate recordings are accepted until 4:45 pm. The office itself is open from 8:30 am to 5 pm, and marriage applications stop at 4:30 pm.

Black and white copies are $0.25 a page. Certified copies are $5 for page one with $2 on each page after.

Is the Gaston County records search online?

Yes. The county moved to a new public search system on May 28, 2026, with the old system's records carried over. Some older records are not digitized, so call 704-862-7681 for help.

Who owes the deed tax on a Gaston County closing?

The seller owes it when the deed is handed in, at a dollar per $500 of price. The settlement statement shows the dollar figure.

The seller pays it at the office just before recording, and the receipts are divided between the county and the state. The settlement statement should show it as its own line. Ask your closing attorney how it will appear on your deed.

When does Graham County bill property tax?

Bills go out July 1, come due September 1 and can be paid through January 5 with no interest.

  • Interest of 2% begins January 6, then 0.75% a month until paid.
  • A second real estate notice goes out each February.
  • Delinquent taxes are published in the Graham Star every April, and advertising fees are added to each listed bill.
  • Enforced collection can start any time after January 5: wage garnishment, bank attachment, a state debt setoff against income tax returns and lottery winnings, levy on rents and foreclosure.

Call the collector to confirm the amount before you pay a delinquent bill, because it will differ from the printed figure. The tax office lists (828) 479-7962 for foreclosure questions.

How do I pay Graham County property tax?

Pay in person, by phone or online. The county takes cash, credit card, money order or check, made out to Graham County, and a locked drop box sits at the side entrance of the building.

Cards carry a processor charge of 2.5% with a $2.00 minimum, none of which the county sets or receives. Partial payments and prepayments are accepted when the parcel or account number is noted on the check. With an escrow account the bill still comes to the homeowner, so pass a copy to your mortgage company. A returned check costs $25.00 or 10 percent, whichever is more.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Graham County houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

What else does the Graham County tax office value and bill?

Besides land and buildings, the Graham County tax office values these items and takes exclusion applications.

  • Motor vehicles, boats, jet skis and houseboats.
  • Elderly, present-use value, religious and educational exclusions.
  • January listings of personal property and business personal property, improvements, business listing extensions and value appeals.

Motor vehicle tax is a separate bill payable to the NCDMV office at 74 S. Main Street in Robbinsville, phone (828) 479-4896. A houseboat sticker costs $5.00 and requires a copy of the pump out permit when you pay. A seller who owns a boat or houseboat should sort out those bills too, since a buyer will not want to inherit them.

What relief programs and reappraisal affect a Graham County sale?

The assessor and collector both hand out the elderly, disabled and veteran exclusion forms, and they go back to the assessor's office by June 1.

The county has a 2027 Schedule of Values, with market values set as of January 1, 2027, plus a present-use value schedule for farm and forest land. Under G.S. 105-277.1, a homeowner aged 65 or over, or totally and permanently disabled, may exclude whichever is greater, $25,000 or half of appraised value. G.S. 105-277.1C gives a disabled veteran a $45,000 exclusion with no age or income test. Personal property is listed from January 1 to January 31. The assessor's number is (828) 479-7963.

What happens in Graham County if property tax goes unpaid?

The lien runs with the parcel from the listing date. The county can pursue it with a foreclosure suit in the county of the land, modeled on a mortgage foreclosure, under G.S. 105-374.

The owner of record, a spouse and other lienholders receive service. Bidders compete at a courthouse-door auction, and the commissioner may ask for up to 20 percent down. A raised bid or exception must come within 10 days of the sale report, and redeeming before confirmation means paying the taxes with penalties, interest and costs. A seller who is behind should call the collector early, since newspaper advertising fees land on each listed bill.

What should a seller do before recording a Graham County deed?

Settle the tax bill, confirm that every old loan has a recorded satisfaction and have your closing attorney review the chain of title.

G.S. 47-18 ties priority to registration time, so the document recorded first in the county where the land lies generally takes precedence over later ones. Satisfactions record free in Graham County. If the person who held the deed has died, finish the estate paperwork first, because the buyer's lender will want proof of authority to sign in the index before funding.

More questions about Graham County, NC Register of Deeds

Can I pay Graham County recording fees by card?

No. The Register of Deeds page says only cash or checks are accepted for recording fees. Property tax payments are handled by the tax office, which accepts cards with a processor fee.

What if the Graham County office is closed when I need to record?

Call (828) 479-7971 first. The county says that when the office runs flex hours or closes, recordings are accepted in the Tax Office. Only cash or checks pay the recording fees.

What are the recording charges in Graham County?

The county sheet shows $26 up to page 15 for a land record instrument and $64 up to page 35 for a deed of trust, with $4 for each page beyond those points. Satisfactions are free.

When are Graham County property taxes due?

Bills mail July 1 and are due September 1. You can pay through January 5 without interest, and 2% interest starts January 6.

Is the Graham County transfer tax the same as the statewide rate?

Yes. The sheet prints $2 per thousand, which equals $1 for each $500 of price. The seller pays it before the deed is recorded.

Where is the Oxford recording office, and how do I phone it?

Go to the courthouse at 101 Main Street, Oxford, NC 27565, or call 919-693-6314. Letters go to P.O. Box 427 in the same city.

The county's online ordering page gives office hours as weekdays, 8:30 AM to 5 PM, and says a request sent after 4 PM waits until the next business day. For a sale, phone first and ask what the staff will need for your type of instrument, since they may not draft or repair documents.

The register of deeds is a countywide elected position, and G.S. 161-1 sets the term at two years.

Which documents does the Oxford office file?

Real estate records are the core of its work: deeds, deeds of trust, cancellations, plats, assumed names, powers of attorney and similar instruments. The county says each is recorded, indexed and scanned, and that deed records stretch back to 1746.

  • Land records: deeds, deeds of trust, plats and cancellations.
  • Personal records: births, deaths, marriages and marriage licenses.
  • Other filings: military discharges and notary commissions, plus the oath for Granville County notaries.

Staff run a recording counter, not a legal clinic. The office tells filers that state law bars it from practicing law, so it will not supply legal forms, coach you through filling one in, or say what a recorded document means legally. A North Carolina attorney can answer those questions.

Which fees apply when a Granville County deed is filed?

The tax is $1.00 per $500 of consideration or value, rounding any remainder up, and G.S. 105-228.30 puts it on the transferor, due before recording. The county keeps half. For a tract in several counties, the one with the most value collects it. Because the tax is figured from the stated consideration, make sure the deed reflects the real contract.

Why should a Granville County deed be recorded promptly?

An unrecorded deed does not bind later buyers or lien creditors. G.S. 47-18 gives priority to the instrument registered first, measured by time, in whichever county holds the land.

That rule covers leases over three years, options and rights of first refusal as well. Seller-financed deals fall under Chapter 47H, which tells the seller to record the contract or a Memorandum of a Contract for Deed inside five business days and gives the purchaser until midnight of the third business day to cancel.

Is there protection against property fraud in Granville County?

Yes. The register of deeds' office provides a free alert tool, PropertyCheck, through its software vendor. Owners can ask for an email or text whenever a document is recorded that matches a name, a street address or a parcel number.

  • Register on the vendor's website.
  • Create alerts for each version of your name and for your spouse.
  • Add the property address and parcel number.

The county describes the scheme it guards against: a forger moves title into another name and records the paperwork while the real owner stays unaware. An alert does not block a filing. It gives you the chance to call 919-693-6314 and consult a lawyer fast.

Who may collect a vital record in person at the Oxford office?

Anyone picking up a record must show valid state-issued photo ID, and the county limits who may collect it for someone else. Online requests are first come, first served, with no refunds, and all messages about an order arrive by email.

  • The person named on the record.
  • A spouse, brother or sister, parent or step-parent, grandparent, or child, step-child or grandchild.
  • A funeral director, for a death certificate only, with proof of license.
  • An authorized agent, attorney or legal representative, who may be asked for proof.

Inaccurate order details can stop a request from being processed. Requests are handled on business days during office hours, and the vendor's help address for the ordering tool is on the ordering page.

What should a Granville County seller check in the records before closing?

Look up your own parcel on the Register of Deeds' online records first. The county says documents are available online and that copies can be had on request, so a seller can pull the vesting deed and any old loan paperwork without a trip to the courthouse.

  • The deed that put the property in your name, matching spelling and legal description.
  • Any deed of trust that was paid off but never cancelled of record.
  • Plats or easements that affect the parcel.
  • Assumed-name filings, if a business ran from the house.

A cleanup before listing is usually faster than a cleanup under a closing deadline. Where a recorded instrument looks wrong, call the office at 919-693-6314 to find out how it can be corrected, and bring an attorney in for anything that needs legal drafting.

How does the Oxford recording counter connect to the county tax office?

They are separate offices with a shared subject. Recording moves title, while Granville County Tax Administration, at 919-693-4181, sets the value and bills the tax. Under G.S. 105-355 unpaid tax becomes a lien on the parcel as of the January 1 listing date, so the balance should be settled by the time a new deed is recorded.

The county offers a 1.5% discount on current taxes paid between July 1 and August 15, and the bill is due September 1. A seller who closes in that window can ask the tax office what a prompt payment would save. Oxford, Butner, Creedmoor, Stem and Stovall all sit in this one county, so a deed for land in any of them is recorded at the single courthouse counter in Oxford.

How many homes and households does Granville County have?

QuickFacts lists 25,685 housing units in 2025 and 22,474 households across 2020 to 2024, averaging 2.52 residents each.

The base is $26.00 for the first 15 pages and $4.00 for each page after, as G.S. 161-10 sets it. The seller adds the excise tax, which is $1.00 per $500 of value.

Can staff prepare my deed for me?

No. The office is a recording office, and North Carolina law keeps its staff from practicing law, so it cannot supply forms or advise on legal effect. Hire an attorney for drafting.

Is a loan payoff cancellation free to record?

Yes. The state fee schedule lists no charge for a satisfaction or cancellation of a deed of trust or mortgage.

Where do I file a deed for Greene County land?

File it at the Greene County Courthouse, 301 N. Greene Street, Snow Hill, NC 28580. The counter is staffed from 8:00 AM until 5:00 PM on weekdays, holidays excepted, and the phone is 252-747-3620. Letters go to PO Box 86.

The register of deeds describes the office as custodian of the county's real estate papers and vital records. On the land side it handles deeds, deeds of trust, maps, easements, leases, assignments and UCC fixture filings tied to real property. Notary commissions are logged there, and the office swears in notaries who reside in the county.

The county's rate page names three towns, Hookerton, Snow Hill and Walstonburg, and land in any of them is recorded at this single office.

Why does Greene County want a tax form before it records a deed?

The county ties recording to its tax records. Every deed submitted must carry a form signed off by the Greene County Tax Office, which the register of deeds' page calls the Deed Information form.

  • Who is giving and who is receiving the property, with addresses.
  • The street address and legal description, and buildings if the deed splits a parcel.
  • Any personal property that moves with the land, such as a mobile home.
  • Whether deferred tax value is involved, and how the two parties are related if so.
  • Unpaid prior-year tax and the current-year figure, filled in by the tax office.

The tax office also marks the document as a transfer, a split or a merge and assigns the parcel number. Instructions on the reverse of the form cover deeds where delinquent taxes exist, so phone the tax office at 252-747-3615 before heading to the courthouse if you owe back tax on the parcel.

Can a Greene County deed be e-recorded?

Yes, for nearly every deed. The office accepts electronic recording for all instruments except maps and highway rights-of-way, so a closing attorney can file from a distance.

The one difference involves the tax form. For electronic filings, the county says its tax office only approves Deed Information sheets inside the e-recording platform and asks filers not to deliver anything to the tax office by hand or mail. Paper filers get the signature first, then bring the packet to Snow Hill.

Index searches run from 1875 to the present on a site run by Courthouse Computer Systems. The register of deeds moved to that system in December 2025, and staff take questions at 252-747-3620.

What will the state fee schedule cost on a Greene County filing?

Recording a satisfaction of a deed of trust costs nothing, and plats run $21.00 a sheet. Items outside land records are priced separately by the county: a certified birth, death or marriage copy is $10.00 in cash, and a marriage license is $60, cash only.

Who owes the excise tax when a Greene County house is sold?

The seller does. The state levies $1.00 for each $500 of consideration or value, with a partial $500 counted whole (G.S. 105-228.30), and the transferor settles it with the register of deeds before the deed is filed.

The money is split between the county general fund and the state. Since the tax tracks the amount stated in the deed, check that figure against the sale contract. A deed bounced for a missing tax form or a wrong amount is not effective against later buyers and lien creditors until it is properly registered, according to G.S. 47-18.

The fee is $60, cash only, and licenses are issued between 9:00 AM and 4:00 PM.

The office also offers a Thank-A-Vet program, an assumed business name filing, and a link for protection from property and mortgage fraud on its main page.

What does deferred tax mean on the Greene County deed form?

Item six on the county form asks whether deferred value is involved and, if so, how the grantor is related to the grantee. Item seven lists deferred taxes due by year, and the form warns that deferred taxes have not been calculated unless that section is filled in.

The tax office completes the lines for prior-year and current-year tax. If your parcel carries deferred value, ask the office to calculate the amount before the deed is signed, since the form treats uncalculated deferred taxes as unknown. Sellers should not leave that question for the closing table.

The form also asks for Social Security numbers but says disclosure is voluntary, based on federal law and N.C.G.S. 105-309 for tax administration.

Guilford County by the numbers

Where can you reach Guilford County's recording office, and what are its hours?

There are two counters. Greensboro is at 201 W. Market St., with real estate and recording upstairs on the second floor. High Point is at 325 E. Russell Ave., Room 155. One number, 336-641-7556, serves both, and staff work weekdays from 8 until 5.

Mail can be addressed to P.O. Box 3427, Greensboro, NC 27402, or P.O. Box 1467, High Point, NC 27261. Rowan and Orange counties gave up land to form Guilford in 1771, and one set of land records now covers a Jamestown farmhouse, a Summerfield lot and a downtown Greensboro condo alike. General questions can go to guilforddeeds@guilfordcountync.gov, and the Census Bureau counted 562,234 residents in mid-2025.

What is the process for filing a deed with Guilford County?

Deliver a properly formatted deed with the recording fee and the excise tax, and the office puts it on record. Electronic submission works too, because Guilford accepts every real estate document sent through its approved e-recording vendors.

E-recording returns the book and page data plus a stamped image within minutes, and the system rejects a document immediately if it misses the state's recording standards. Paper filings must also show where to send the original after recording. The county's checklist for a standard document includes:

  • Letter or legal size paper, one-sided, black type on white stock.
  • Three blank inches above the text on page one, and a quarter inch of margin elsewhere.
  • Type no smaller than 9 point, with the instrument's title printed as a heading on the first sheet.
  • Pen entries for blanks and corrections are acceptable.

A document that fails any item draws the non-standard surcharge on top of the regular fee, so check the layout before you send it.

What fees does the Guilford County recording office collect?

Pricing starts at $26 for a general instrument of up to 15 pages, and a mortgage or deed of trust of up to 35 pages starts at $64. Each page beyond those limits adds $4. State law fixes those amounts, and the county's published table adds the smaller line items.

Guilford County Register of Deeds fee schedule, recording and copies

Source: the county's Recording and Real Estate page. An ordinary copy of a real estate record is 5 cents a page at the counter and $1 by mail. Under the statute these fees are the only ones allowed, and payment comes first.

The county's page lists a few extras that come up around a sale. A notary oath costs $10, and authenticating a notary costs $1 per notary per page. A map copy is 50 cents, and certified plats are $5 per copy. UCC filings run $38, or $45 above two pages plus $2 for each page past ten. The Guilford office takes only fixture-related UCC filings, and every other UCC filing goes to the Secretary of State in Raleigh.

Who pays the Guilford County deed excise tax?

The transferor does, handing it to the register before the deed goes on record. State law sets the rate at $1 per $500 of the price, counting any leftover fraction as a full $500, and the county's table shows deeds since August 1, 1991 at $2 per thousand, which is the same thing.

Half of the revenue stays in the county's general fund and the remainder is forwarded each month to the state revenue department. A closing statement lists the tax apart from the recording fee. The county's table also carries two older rate bands, $1 per thousand for 1968 through July 1991 and $1.10 per thousand before 1968, which matter only when you read an old deed. For your own sale, get the exact figure from the closing attorney.

What happens to a payoff after it is recorded in Guilford County?

The loan stays visible against the title until someone records a satisfaction. North Carolina gives an unrecorded deed, option or long lease no priority over lien creditors or later buyers who paid value, and ranks competing claims by when they were registered.

Guilford describes three recordable forms of satisfaction, none of which costs anything to file:

  • A satisfaction signed by the secured creditor and acknowledged before a notary.
  • A trustee's or substitute trustee's satisfaction of the deed of trust.
  • An affidavit by a North Carolina attorney serving as satisfaction agent, for use when a lender never provides one.

The office stopped taking the original deed of trust and note as proof of payment. If an old lender's loan still shows open on your parcel, a recorded satisfaction clears it, and your attorney or the lender can arrange that.

How should Guilford County owners protect against forged deeds?

Enroll in the Property Fraud Alert. It emails notice when a document appears under a name variation you registered. The register must record a deed that meets the legal form once fees and taxes are paid, and the office does not test whether a signature is real.

The county names vacant or distressed homes, older owners and low-income owners as frequent targets. Its warning signs include a transfer you never signed, tax bills that stop arriving, and a default notice on a home with no mortgage. An owner who finds a bad deed should assemble the paperwork and report it to the Sheriff's Office or Greensboro or High Point police, the District Attorney, a real estate attorney and the register. The register cannot pull a recorded document from the index, so ask an attorney how to challenge it.

The county also advises checking credentials, reading contracts and considering a title search and title insurance.

Can the Guilford County register correct a mistake in a recorded deed?

Only indexing mistakes. G.S. 132-1.10 bars the office from changing a recorded instrument, so a misspelled name, a faulty legal description or a wrong loan amount in the document itself needs a corrective instrument prepared by your attorney.

The Indexing Correction Request form handles cases where the index differs from the document. Call 336-641-7556 or use the office email with questions. The corrective instrument is recorded at the usual fees. The recording page also carries a Personal Information Redaction section and a Real Estate Document Request form for copies.

How does Guilford County's housing stock look in the Census data?

QuickFacts counts 246,403 housing units for July 2025. For 2020 through 2024, the survey puts a middle-priced owned home at $259,900, the owner share of occupied homes at 59.9%, and median gross rent at $1,163.

The county's middle household earns $68,642 in 2024 dollars, and builders pulled 2,876 permits in 2025. For the tax side of a sale, read our Guilford County property tax guide.

More questions about Guilford County, NC Register of Deeds

Which phone number reaches Guilford's register of deeds?

336-641-7556, for the Greensboro office at 201 W. Market St. and the High Point office at 325 E. Russell Ave., Room 155. Staff are available on weekdays, 8 a.m. until 5 p.m.

What does a Guilford deed filing cost?

Expect $26 for an instrument of up to 15 pages and $4 for each page past that, plus a $25 surcharge when the document is non-standard. The seller also pays the excise tax before recording.

Is e-recording available through the Guilford register?

Yes. The office takes all electronically submitted real estate documents via approved vendors, sends back the recording details and a stamped image within minutes, and flags documents that miss the state standards.

Does the Guilford register verify a deed's authenticity?

No. A deed that meets the format rules is recorded once fees and taxes are paid. Owners can sign up for the free Property Fraud Alert and report forgeries to law enforcement and the District Attorney.

Do satisfactions of a mortgage carry a Guilford recording fee?

No. Satisfactions, affidavits of satisfaction and trustee's satisfactions are filed free of charge. The office does not accept the original deed of trust and note in their place.

What services does Halifax County's recording office provide?

The office takes in, indexes and safeguards land records, and it also handles plats, UCC filings, vital records and assorted miscellaneous documents. The county says the elected register serves a 4-year term and leads a team of one assistant and four deputies.

Business runs from half past eight to five on weekdays, holidays excepted. An online Register of Deeds Index Search is linked from the county site. Halifax County was carved from Edgecombe in 1758 along the Roanoke River, and the town of Halifax is the seat. The North Carolina Provincial Congress met in the town on April 12, 1776 and passed the Halifax Resolves, and the county still marks April 12 as Halifax Day. Census estimates count 46,534 people in the county for July 2025, and the county's 2026-27 budget ordinance appropriates $516,743 for the Register of Deeds.

How far back do Halifax County land records go?

Paper indexes reach to 1732, which is older than the county itself. Online, the index search offers three layers, as described on the county's Real Estate Records page:

  • Indexes and images of recorded real property documents from 1976 forward.
  • Historical real estate indexes for 1934 through 1975.
  • Survey maps dating from 1818.

Other record sets start at different points. Marriage records begin in 1825, and birth and death records begin in October 1913. Anything on a parcel that predates 1976 means working from the historical or hard-copy indexes.

Why does the Tax Collector sign off before a Halifax County deed is recorded?

Under a commissioners' rule that took effect January 1, 2016, the register will not accept a deed conveying real property unless the Tax Collector certifies that no delinquent ad valorem tax, or other tax the collector must collect, encumbers the parcel.

Staff need time to research each parcel, so the collector stops taking deeds at 4:30 in the afternoon. The collector's office is Tax Administration, 357 Ferrell Lane in Halifax, phone 252-583-2121. Do this step before you go to the register, since a deed without the certification is turned away. Our Halifax County property tax guide covers rates, appeals and relief.

What does Halifax County charge for recording documents?

The county's 2026-27 fee schedule lists $26 for an instrument up to 15 pages and $64 for a deed of trust or mortgage up to 35 pages, adding $4 for each page past those limits. State law fixes the same base amounts.

What is the Halifax County deed stamp tax and who pays it?

On its fee schedule Halifax lists the excise stamp tax at $1.00 per $500 of consideration, with any remainder counted as another $500. State law matches that figure and places the duty on the party giving up title, who must pay before the deed is recorded.

Revenue is split in two. The county general fund keeps one portion, and the state revenue department receives the rest monthly after refunds and an allowance. The 2026-27 county budget ordinance shows $353,500 for the Register of Deeds among other taxes and licenses. A parcel split across county lines pays in the county holding the larger share. Ask your closing attorney for the exact amount before settlement.

Which recording rules affect Halifax County contracts for deed?

Registration is what gives a deed, option or long lease its force against lien creditors and later paying purchasers, and the order of registration sets priority among competing claims.

Seller financing falls under Chapter 47H when the buyer will make at least five payments besides the down payment, the seller keeps title, and the property is a principal dwelling of one to four families or a manufactured home with a price of $5,000 or more. Three features stand out:

  • The agreement must be written, signed and acknowledged.
  • The seller records it, or a Memorandum of a Contract for Deed, within five business days.
  • The buyer may cancel through midnight of the third business day, and a default notice must allow a cure date at least 30 days out.

Ask an attorney to draft any land contract and to confirm that it was recorded.

What else does the Halifax County register's office issue?

Beyond deeds, the county's 2026-27 fee schedule prices the vital records and notary services that run through the same counter:

  • Marriage license: $60, which includes the $35 state fee.
  • Certified copy of a birth certificate or a death certificate: $10 each.
  • Notary public oath administered: $10, and $5 to verify a commission.
  • Military service record: no charge.

The same schedule prices a certified plat copy at $5 for the first page and lists right-of-way plans at $21 for the first page and $5 for each added page.

How do Halifax County tax foreclosure sales connect to the land records?

A tax foreclosure auction ends with a deed, which the register records. The county publishes each sale notice on its Tax Foreclosures page, and bidding happens in the courthouse lobby at Halifax. A bid stays open to a higher one for 10 days, and the property goes as is.

The county cautions that purchasers take subject to taxes, assessments and liens held by parties who were not named defendants, and it suggests a title examination before bidding. If your own house faces a tax sale, selling before the auction keeps the price in your hands, and the register will record your deed once the tax certification is on file.

What housing figures does the Census report for Halifax County?

The Census Bureau's table counts 25,078 homes and apartments in July 2025 and 20,383 households between 2020 and 2024. Of occupied homes, 62.9% are owned. A middle-priced owned home carries a value of $106,200, and rent sits at a median of $813.

The middle household earns $45,590 in 2024 dollars, and seniors make up 25.2% of the population. Only 75 permits for new building were issued in 2025, a light year for construction in a county of 723.74 square miles of land.

More questions about Halifax County, NC Register of Deeds

When can I visit the Halifax County Register of Deeds?

Weekdays from half past eight to five, with holidays closed. The tax certification a deed needs is handled at the Tax Collector's office, which closes its deed window a half hour before the register's counter.

How much will a Halifax County filing run?

The 2026-27 county schedule shows $26 for up to 15 pages plus $4 for every added page, and $25 more for a non-standard form. The seller also owes the excise stamp tax of $1.00 per $500 of value.

What can make the Halifax County register reject a deed?

A missing certification from the Tax Collector is one reason. A county rule effective January 1, 2016 bars the register from accepting a deed until delinquent taxes are cleared and certified, so visit Tax Administration first.

How old are the land records the Halifax County register holds?

Paper indexes go back to 1732. Online search covers recorded documents from 1976 forward, historical indexes for 1934 through 1975, and survey maps from 1818.

Is recording a satisfaction of a mortgage free in Halifax County?

Yes. The county's fee schedule shows no charge for satisfactions, consistent with state law. A deed of trust itself starts at $64 for its first 35 pages.

A deed counts when the staff has keyed it in. Walk-ins face no set cutoff, yet anything that cannot be keyed by 5:00 p.m. waits for the following business day, and electronic submissions stop at 4:45 p.m.

The clock matters because priority runs in order of registration. G.S. 47-18 gives a conveyance, option, lease beyond three years or first-refusal right no force against lien creditors or paying buyers until the instrument is registered in the home county of the land.

Payment may be by check, cash, money order or card, and a card payment adds a vendor fee that goes to the vendor.

The Tax Department's Land Records section works from the same courthouse. It builds the county's official index of tax listings from the deeds the register records and from Clerk of Court files, so a deed that reaches the register soon shows up in the parcel data the county uses for billing.

Which documents sit in the Henderson County deed vault?

Land transactions in the county are archived here. Its published list of holdings:

  • Land transfers, easements, rights of way and surveys
  • Deeds of trust, mortgages and UCC filings
  • Separation agreements
  • Assumed business name (DBA) filings
  • Notary public oaths

Marriage licenses are by appointment only, between 10:00 AM and 3:00 PM on weekdays, and the county asks callers to phone rather than email. How can I search Henderson County deeds and plats online?

The county offers an online deed index that runs from 1979 to the present, hosted by a records vendor. Visitors accept a disclaimer first, and the site works best on a desktop or laptop with Chrome or Edge, cookies on and pop-up blocking off for the site.

To pull a plat, open the Register of Deeds system and choose View Images. Pick Plat as the book type, then enter the recording year or Cabinet A, B or C as the book, and the plat number as the page. Leading zeros are not needed. The county's guide lists slide ranges by year. Recent years run like this:

  • 2021: slides 12982 to 13869
  • 2022: slides 13870 to 14600
  • 2023: slides 14601 to 15329
  • 2024: slides 15330 to 16020
  • 2025: slides 16021 to 16768
  • 2026: slide 16769 onward

Older plats from 1988 forward follow the same numbering, with three early cabinets covering the oldest slides.

The site's own disclaimer says the register makes no guarantee about the accuracy of the online images and that the official records stay in the courthouse office, so confirm anything important at the counter. A privacy notice on the search page cites G.S. 132-1.8(g). A document filed for recording should leave out Social Security, driver license, bank account and card numbers unless the law requires them. Anyone can ask the register in writing to remove such a number from an online image, and no fee is charged for that request.

What are the statutory recording amounts in Henderson County?

What does the 2027 reappraisal mean for a Henderson County seller?

Values reset on January 1, 2027. Henderson County reappraises real property every four years, well ahead of the eight-year minimum set by G.S. 105-286, and the last reappraisal took effect in 2023.

The county says values follow market prices from recent qualified sales, and that a mass appraisal groups similar properties together. It weighs location, construction type, age, replacement cost and zoning. Buildings still under construction on January 1 are valued by their percentage of completion. Land enrolled in the Present-Use Value Program for agriculture, horticulture or forestry can carry an assessed value below market value.

The Tax Department counts about 71,500 parcels, and property taxes make up an estimated 50 percent of the county operating budget in fiscal year 2027. The Board of Commissioners sets the rate and the Assessor sets values. Its Tax Department page lists divisions for real property, personal property, exemptions and deferment, land records and collections. The county's programs cover elderly or disabled owners, disabled veterans, nonprofits, commercial farms and wildlife management. See the county reappraisal page.

How big is the Henderson County housing market?

QuickFacts puts Henderson County at 122,375 people in July 2025, which is 5.2 percent above the April 2020 base, spread over 372.95 square miles of land. There were 61,173 housing units, and builders pulled 1,093 permits during 2025.

Owners occupy 75.0 percent of homes, valued at $351,400 in the middle of the 2020 to 2024 range. Monthly owner costs are $1,608 with a mortgage and $482 without. Tenants face gross rent near $1,187, and household income sits at $68,187 across 51,067 households of 2.29 people.

Age shapes sales here. Adults past 65 are 29.1 percent of residents, and the survey counts 7,811 veterans. The property tax exclusions for older, disabled and veteran owners are worth a question to the Tax Department. See Census QuickFacts.

What should I prepare before recording a deed in Henderson County?

A short checklist keeps the document from being flagged or delayed at the counter.

  • Print on one side of letter or legal paper in black ink, using at least 10 point type.
  • State the instrument type across the head of page one and leave a three inch blank margin there.
  • Redact Social Security and account numbers unless the law requires them.
  • Put the drafter's name and the parcel number on page one.
  • Have your attorney file the satisfaction of any paid-off deed of trust.

If the deed fails the formatting standards, the register records it anyway after collecting an added nonstandard document fee. Staff can also issue a certified copy of anything the office recorded.

More questions about Henderson County, NC Register of Deeds

Do I need an appointment to record a deed in Henderson County?

The county lists appointments only for marriage licenses, which run 10:00 AM to 3:00 PM and are booked by phone. Recording is open during the regular weekday window, and the office takes questions at 828-697-4901.

How far back does the Henderson County online deed index go?

The online index covers 1979 to the present. Older plats are found by choosing Plat as the book type and entering a year or Cabinet A, B or C. Check the county's plat guide for the slide ranges.

Does Henderson County reappraise property every year?

No. The county reappraises real property every four years, last in 2023, with the next reappraisal effective January 1, 2027. State law requires one at least every eight years.

Can I pay by card at the Henderson County Register of Deeds?

Yes. Cards are accepted along with checks, cash and money orders. The vendor that processes the card adds a fee, and Henderson County does not charge it.

What does a certified vital record cost in Henderson County?

A certified copy of a birth, death or marriage certificate is $10.00 with proper ID and an acceptable relationship to the person named. Photocopies are $.25.

Where is the Hertford County Register of Deeds?

Go to the third floor of the Hertford County Courthouse, 119 Justice Drive, Suite 9, in Winton. The office phone is 252-358-7850, and hours run from 8:30 AM to 5:00 PM Monday through Friday except county holidays and closings.

The county says its staff maintain real estate documents going back as far as 1862, and its history page notes land deeds in the area dating to 1710. The office holds deeds, deeds of trust, maps, military discharge records, notary records, and birth, death and marriage records for events in Hertford County.

The county sits in northeastern North Carolina, bordering Virginia to the north. Farming remains its economic backbone, with tobacco, cotton, peanuts, corn and soybeans listed as staples, and the Chowan River crosses its land. QuickFacts lists 353.16 square miles of land.

How did Hertford County's land records begin?

The General Assembly formed the county in 1759 from land taken from Bertie, Northampton and Chowan counties. Before that the area was part of the Parish of Saint Barnabas. The first court met at Cotton's Ferry, and Winton, on the Chowan River, replaced it as seat of government when the town was incorporated in 1766. Ahoskie grew later into the commercial center of the county.

Two highways cross in the county, U.S. 13 running north and south and U.S. 158 running east and west. The county's records are indexed by name, which is how a lawyer follows an old farm tract back through its owners.

What does Hertford County post as its recording fees?

Plat copies are $3.00 a page. Copy requests made by fax or online cost $1.00 for page one, then $.25 for each page after.

Which formatting rules can trigger the Hertford County nonstandard fee?

The recording rules page repeats the paper standards of G.S. 161-14. A document that misses them is still recorded, with the $25.00 fee added.

  • Letter or legal size paper, one side only
  • Black type on white, 10 point or larger
  • Wide blank band across the head of page one

Session Law 2011-351 adds a drafter rule: page one of a deed or deed of trust must name the person or law firm that prepared it. The county also wants the tax parcel pin on each deed, plus either a tax department stamp showing no delinquent taxes or a sentence directing the closing attorney to pay any back taxes from closing proceeds. Electronic deeds must carry the sentence.

Can a Hertford County deed be e-recorded?

Yes. Everything except maps can be e-recorded, according to the county FAQ, and the e-recording page names Corporation Service Company and Simplifile as submitters. The recorded copy comes back electronically right after recording.

What can the Hertford County office not do for a seller?

The list matters more than people expect, because sellers often call the register for help it cannot give.

  • It cannot search a title, because state law bars register staff from doing so. An individual or a legal representative can run the search.
  • It cannot confirm whether a lien exists. A deed of trust recorded in the office is the sign that the property secured a loan.
  • It cannot change a recorded deed. A new deed must be prepared, and the office recommends seeing an attorney.
  • It cannot name an owner from a street address, since records are indexed by name. Land Records Mapping, at 252-358-7809, handles location questions.
  • It holds no estate, will or divorce records. Those sit with the Clerk of Superior Court, 252-358-7100.

Real estate documents are online, though older indexes and images may not be.

Who pays the deed excise tax in a Hertford County sale?

The seller. G.S. 105-228.30 puts the burden on the transferor, and the county prints $2.00 per $1000.00 of purchase price on its schedule.

Under G.S. 47-18 a conveyance reaches later purchasers and lien creditors only once it is registered, so recording should follow signing quickly. The statutes are at G.S. 105-228.30 and G.S. 47-18.

What else is handled at the Winton counter?

The same office issues licenses and certificates, and the fee schedule and FAQ list the details. Knowing them helps if a seller also needs paperwork for an estate or a move.

  • Marriage license: $60.00, issued from 8:30 AM until 4:30 PM, valid for sixty days. A couple can buy it in Hertford County and marry anywhere in North Carolina.
  • Magistrate wedding: $50.00, arranged through the magistrate at the sheriff's department.
  • Certified birth, death or marriage copy: $10.00 each, with a government photo ID. Only close relatives or an authorized agent can pick one up.
  • Online vital record requests: $3.50 added, through the county's Get Certificate Now program.
  • Notary oath: $10.00. The Secretary of State sends the notice and no appointment is needed.
  • Beer licenses: $5.00 off premises and $25.00 on premises. Wine licenses: $25.00.
  • Military discharge filing and certified copy: free, though discharges are not open to public viewing.

How small is the Hertford County housing market?

The head count dropped from 24,669 in 2010 to 21,552 in 2020 and is estimated at 19,015 for mid 2025. Housing stock stands at 9,873 units, and the county issued just 3 building permits in 2025.

  • Median home value among owners, 2020 to 2024: $119,200
  • Share of owner households: 67.4 percent
  • Rent at the midpoint: $844
  • Household income at the midpoint: $45,537
  • Seniors 65 or older: 27.1 percent

Values are modest, so fixed charges such as recording fees weigh more on a small sale. Ask your closing attorney for the full list of closing costs before you set a price. Source: Census QuickFacts.

How does the 2027 revaluation touch deeds recorded now?

The county's revaluation takes effect January 1, 2027, the first since 2019, and field measuring began in July 2025. Deeds recorded before and after that date use the same recording steps. What changes is the assessed value attached to the parcel.

The Tax Assessor and Tax Collector sit at 115 Justice Drive in Winton. Ask the collector about the current bill before you close. The county also warns the public about deed scams, with a fraud detection page linked from the Register of Deeds site.

The schedule lists $26.00 for a general instrument up to 15 pages, then $4.00 per page after that, and $64.00 for a deed of trust up to 35 pages. Call 252-358-7850 to check for changes.

The county lists $2.00 per $1000.00 of purchase price, and the seller pays it.

What happens if my Hertford County deed is formatted wrong?

It is recorded anyway, with a $25.00 non-standard fee added. Review the rules above first.

Can Hertford County staff search my title or find a lien?

No. State law keeps register staff from searching titles, and the office will not say whether a lien exists. An attorney or title professional can read the recorded instruments.

Can I get a copy of my recorded deed in Hertford County?

Yes, at the counter or on the county sites, though older indexes and images may be missing online. Certified copies are priced per page.

Which Iredell County offices take deeds for recording?

Two sites handle recording for Iredell County, one in Statesville and one in Mooresville, and staff there work weekdays from opening at eight in the morning until five in the afternoon, according to the county staff directory.

  • Shared fax line: 704-878-5426

The same staff issue certified birth and death certificates, marriage licenses and copies of military discharges, and they administer notary oaths. Nearly everything held there is open to any member of the public. The one stated exception is military discharges.

A seller in this county will mostly meet this office through your closing attorney, who delivers the signed deed and the buyer's deed of trust. Afterward, a call to either site confirms that both papers made the record and shows the order in which they were filed.

What role does recording play when a house sells?

Recording makes the transfer effective against outsiders. The staff index the deed and the lender's deed of trust under the names of the parties, and the filing time fixes who stands first in line.

North Carolina's recording statute says a conveyance does not bind lien creditors or purchasers for value until it is registered where the land lies. Priority then runs by time of registration. That explains why a closing is not finished when pens come down, and why attorneys wait for confirmation of recording before releasing funds.

Iredell staff are clear about what they cannot do. They may not draft a deed or assist in drafting one, and they may not search title or offer a title opinion. Taking a name on or off a deed takes a fresh deed that is drafted, notarized and recorded, so most owners bring in a lawyer.

Court judgments sit elsewhere. The county FAQ tells people to look for them with the Clerk of Court at 704-832-6600, and it explains that a judgment lasts ten years, can be renewed for ten more, and attaches to land you own or later acquire. Before you sign a sale contract, ask your attorney to check for any entry against you.

What are the Iredell County filing charges?

A routine instrument is $26.00 for pages one through fifteen, and each page past fifteen adds $4.00, while a loan security document runs $64.00 for its first thirty-five pages. Those amounts come from G.S. 161-10, which applies in all one hundred counties alike.

Source: North Carolina General Statutes, section 161-10, which calls the schedule complete and exclusive and collects it up front.

For copies of what is already recorded, the county posts its own prices on its FAQ page: a deed copy at $.25 per page and a printed copy of a recorded map at $1.00. Mailed copies carry an additional charge, so call before you send a request.

Which party owes transfer tax on an Iredell County deed?

The person transferring the property owes it, and it must be paid to the Register ahead of the deed reaching the record. The tax rate is $1.00 on every $500 of price, and a leftover fraction counts as a full $500.

Under the excise tax statute, half the receipts stay in the Iredell general fund and the rest travel to the state revenue department. The Iredell FAQ illustrates the rate with its own sample: a $2,000 land purchase carries $4.00 of tax at filing.

The figure is based on the price or value of the interest passing. Because the statute places the duty on the seller, read your settlement statement for this line and ask your attorney how the contract handles it. A seller who accepts a cash offer still sees the same tax, since it follows the deed and not the buyer.

Where can I look up Iredell County land records online?

The county Register page links to a records search covering deeds, deeds of trust, plats and powers of attorney. Iredell says land records run from December 1788 to the present and that state law requires indexing by party name.

Its Land Records page offers a search guide, indexing rules and a separate guide for property recorded before 1964. A notice on the online portal says the system is being tested during a software change, that results may be incomplete, and that the portal is not an official record. For a sale, request a certified copy from the office instead of printing from the screen.

  • Find an owner: use the tax office GIS maps, or call 704-878-3020 for help with them.
  • Proof a mortgage is paid: the lender files a certificate of satisfaction, and the staff will mail or email you a copy.
  • Replace a lost deed: give names and a purchase year, and a copy costs $.25 per page.

Two plain-language answers from the same FAQ help sellers. A deed moves ownership, usually from seller to buyer, while a deed of trust ties the borrower, the lender and a neutral trustee together to secure a loan. The office also explains that a lender's title policy protects the lender, while an owner's policy is optional and protects you against defects a title search missed, and it recommends carrying both.

Is property tax paid through the Register of Deeds?

No. Iredell County Tax Administration in Statesville bills and collects it, and the Register only records instruments. The two still meet at a sale, since a buyer's attorney expects the tax account to be current.

The collector tells owners that payoff at the closing table is available on request, and that a prepayment can be taken at last year's rate if the new bill is not out. The 2026 county rate is .50 per $100 on the county rates page, with towns such as Statesville and Mooresville adding theirs.

Ownership for tax purposes is fixed on January 1. A seller who closes later keeps the liability for that year's bill unless the contract moves it, so look at the proration line on the settlement statement.

Census QuickFacts puts Iredell County at 211,798 people as of mid-2025, spread across 574.41 square miles and roughly 93,711 housing units.

Jackson County by the numbers

Where does Jackson County keep its deed records?

The Jackson County Register works from Room 108 at 401 Grindstaff Cove Road in Sylva, NC 28779. The county's department page gives one weekday window for walk-in recording and e-recording alike, opening at 8 in the morning and closing at half past four.

Archives there cover real estate transactions, Jackson County births and deaths and marriage licenses issued locally. The office records DD214 military discharge forms and issues certified copies to veterans free of charge. Questions about recording go to 828-586-7530.

  • Records portal: deeds.jacksonnc.org
  • E-recording: the department page links an e-recording guide
  • Plat questions: Land Records and Mapping at 828-586-7539, or the Planning Department at 828-631-2261

Tax Administration shares the 401 Grindstaff Cove Road address, so one visit can cover both recording and the tax certification described below.

What format must a Jackson County deed follow?

Anything filed after July 1, 2002 has to satisfy G.S. 161-14(b), and the county spells the rules out on its recording requirements page. A document that misses them draws a $25 non-standard fee added to the usual recording charge.

  • Letter paper (8.5 by 11) or legal paper (8.5 by 14), with the original handed in
  • A three-inch blank band at the head of page one, and half an inch along its other edges and on every edge of later pages
  • Black ink on white stock, typeface of at least 10 points
  • Print on a single side
  • The name of the instrument printed beneath the top margin

The staff draft nothing, supply no forms and alter nothing on a submitted paper. If a legal description has an error, the drafter must correct it.

Land records review each deed too. The county asks for an individual's or law firm's name and address as preparer on the first page, the names and addresses of the grantors and grantees, either a metes and bounds description or a plat cabinet and slide reference, the grantor's back deed references, and a statement on whether any grantor lives on the parcel as a primary residence. A deed that divides a parcel must cite a recorded survey or bear approval from the Planning Department.

What are Jackson County's recording charges?

Ordinary instruments run $26 for the opening fifteen pages with $4 for each page past that, and a deed of trust is $64 for its opening thirty-five pages. The county prints these amounts, which agree with G.S. 161-10.

Charges posted by the Jackson County Register of Deeds

Source: the Register of Deeds recording requirements and plats pages. A UCC termination is $38, and pages after the tenth add $2 apiece.

Payment method matters. Attorney or law firm checks, cashier's checks and money orders are taken. Personal checks are refused.

What does the deed excise tax look like in Jackson County?

The county prints the tax as $2 against every $1,000 of sales price, collected when a deed that conveys an interest is filed. That matches the statute's wording of $1 on each $500.

The excise tax statute says the seller pays the register ahead of filing. Half of the money stays with the county's general fund and half goes to the state. A parcel that straddles county lines is taxed by whichever county holds the larger value.

Jackson County adds a tax check that surprises some sellers. Since March 7, 2011, every deed goes to the Tax Collector's Office for a certification that no delinquent property taxes are owed, and the collector asks for the Parcel Identification Number to speed things up. If back taxes might exist on your parcel, ask for a payoff before the day of closing so the certification does not hold up recording.

How do property tax dates affect a Jackson County sale?

Tax Administration, at the same Sylva address, bills real and personal property for the county and also collects for Dillsboro, Forest Hills, Highlands and Webster. Sylva sends its own bill and keeps its own collections.

The county's 2026 calendar shows bills mailed July 20, a September 1 due date, and January 5, 2027 as the final day to pay without interest. Starting January 6, unpaid balances pick up 2 percent, then 0.75 percent more each month. The window to apply for relief programs closed June 1, 2026, and the formal appeal period for real property ran from March 23 to April 24, and the county's review board first met April 7.

Useful numbers for a seller: Tax Collections at 828-586-7550, Real Property at 828-586-7549, and Exemptions, Present-Use Value and Property Tax Relief at 828-586-7542. The county also notes that its land borders the Eastern Band of Cherokee Indians, so a parcel missing from county records may sit on tribal land, which the tribe maps through its own viewer. Because a tax lien reaches a parcel as of the listing date under G.S. 105-355, ask the collector to confirm any open balance in writing.

What are the rules for plats in Jackson County?

A plat sheet is accepted at 18 by 24 inches or 24 by 36 inches, with a border of at least half an inch on every side. The staff look for the surveyor's original seal and wet-ink signature plus the statements G.S. 47-30 requires.

Plats sent electronically face the same requirements as those carried in, and whoever submits is responsible for collecting signatures first. In-office plats must be reproducible, black on white paper or Mylar, and the county says paper copies were accepted starting March 1, 2025.

Some plats go to Land Records or the Planning Department for review before they are filed. If your lot came from a recent split, ask the surveyor whether the plat is already on file, since the deed has to cite it. The charge is $21 per page.

What does the Jackson County housing picture show?

Census QuickFacts lists 45,039 residents for mid-2025, a rise of 4.4 percent since April 2020. Land area is 491.11 square miles, so density averages roughly 88 residents on each one.

  • 28,707 housing units
  • Homeowners hold 60.8 percent of occupied homes (2020-2024)
  • Typical owner-held house value: $284,700
  • Middle monthly rent: $904
  • Household income at the median: $55,815
  • Residents aged 65 or more: 21.5 percent
  • Poverty rate: 16.9 percent

Sylva, Dillsboro, Forest Hills, Highlands and Webster each appear in the county's tax collection notes, and Cullowhee has its own community planning council on the county meeting calendar. A seller should confirm which town's rate applies to the parcel, since municipal bills are handled differently in Sylva than in the other towns.

The tourism side shows in the 2022 receipts: accommodation and food services brought in $1,038,484 thousand, well above total retail sales of $609,571 thousand.

More questions about Jackson County, NC Register of Deeds

Which Jackson County office accepts a deed for filing?

The Register of Deeds in Room 108 at 401 Grindstaff Cove Road, Sylva. Walk-in and electronic recording share one weekday window that closes at 4:30 p.m.

What is the Jackson County fee to file a deed?

Fifteen pages cost $26 and each added page costs $4, while a deed of trust starts at $64 for thirty-five pages. Paper outside the format rules adds $25.

Are personal checks accepted at the Jackson County recording desk?

Does a Jackson County deed need a tax clearance?

The county posts it as $2 per $1,000 of the sales price. The seller pays ahead of recording.

Johnston County by the numbers

Which Johnston County office takes my deed?

The Johnston County Register of Deeds works from the ground floor of the courthouse in Smithfield, Suite 209 at 207 E. Johnston Street, near the 2nd and Market Street corner of Courthouse Square. Land records calls go to 919-989-5160.

The building is staffed on weekdays, except county holidays, and the real estate counter takes walk-ins with no appointment up to 4:45 p.m. Vital records run on their own line, 919-989-5161, so an heir who needs a death certificate for an estate sale should dial that number instead.

Recording matters because priority in North Carolina follows the time of registration in the county where the land lies. A deed still sitting in someone's briefcase gives the buyer no protection against a later purchaser or a lien creditor, so the usual plan is to record on the day the buyer funds.

What does the Johnston County Register of Deeds charge for recording?

In Johnston County a plain deed is a flat $26.00 up to page 15, and each page past that is another $4.00. A deed of trust or mortgage gets a longer base, running to page 35 for $64.00. The county's schedule page carries an August 30, 2024 update date.
