What is the transfer stamp on a Johnston County sale?

The county's schedule states the excise stamp as $2.00 per $1,000 of consideration, restating it as $1.00 per $500. Seller pays it. The statute puts the burden on the transferor, due at the register's counter before the deed is recorded.

Where the money lands is split down the middle: one half to the county general fund, one half to the Department of Revenue. The stamp sits on a different line than the per-page fee, and the closing company normally lists both in the seller column of the settlement statement.

Ask the office or your closing attorney for the exact stamp amount on your contract price before closing day, since the rate applies to each $500 or part of $500.

Can a Johnston County deed be recorded electronically?

Yes. The register says Johnston County was among the first North Carolina counties to e-record every document type and among the first anywhere to e-record plat maps, and most of what the office receives now arrives electronically.

Five submitters appear on the county's approved list:

  • CSC eRecording
  • EPN
  • Indecomm
  • NTC
  • Simplifile

A recorded document goes back to the submitter within seconds for review. Title companies and closing attorneys typically hold an account with one of these services, so a seller rarely logs in. If you are closing without a lawyer, ask the person handling your closing which service they use and when the file can go out.

The county also hosts an online search. Visitors can look up a grantor or grantee name, a reception number, a date range or a subdivision, and a find-related function pulls documents sharing a legal description.

What pushes a Johnston County recording bill higher?

Three things raise the bill, each with a line on the schedule.

  • Length. Every page past 15 on a deed adds $4.00.
  • Bundled instruments. A document holding two or more instruments with different legal effect adds $10.00 for each extra one.
  • Format. A paper that fails the state recording standards is billed a further $25.00.

Payoff paperwork is the inexpensive part. A satisfaction, trustee's satisfaction or affidavit of satisfaction carries no charge, so clearing an old loan costs nothing at the register. If your lender has not released its lien, ask it to send the satisfaction for recording right after payoff.

What should be ready before a deed goes to the Johnston County register?

Have the deed signed, notarized and complete before it leaves the closing table. The register records instruments and does not draft or repair them.

Run through these items before the signing appointment ends:

  • Match the grantor names to the way title is now held.
  • Carry over the parcel description from your own deed.
  • Line up the stamp amount for the seller to pay.
  • Ask your lender to record a satisfaction of the old deed of trust.
  • Ask the Johnston County tax office about any unpaid bill, since the property tax lien attaches to a parcel on the January 1 listing date.

Johnston County's office also offers a free fraud alert, which you join through the county website. Owners who rent out or leave a house empty during a sale may want it, as the office reports property fraud cases on the rise.

What kind of county is Johnston County for a seller?

East of Raleigh, Johnston County has added people quickly. Its population stood at 168,878 in the 2010 census and 215,999 in 2020, and the July 1, 2025 estimate of 256,448 is 18.7 percent over the 2020 base. The county tallies 99,408 housing units.

The survey years 2020 through 2024 show a typical owned home worth $305,600, with their owners living in 76.1 percent of homes. Median household income is $83,384 and the average commute is 32.2 minutes. Renters pay a median gross $1,146, a number a landlord can weigh against an offer on a rental.

Construction is brisk, with 3,002 permits recorded for 2025. New houses compete with resales, so buyers on older homes often press for repairs or credits. At 792.02 square miles, the county offers everything from town lots to farmland.

What if the house is inherited or has liens in Johnston County?

Start by getting the right paperwork on file. Estate paperwork belongs to the clerk of court, and the register only records the deeds that follow. Smaller estates have a shortcut: once 30 days have passed since death, an heir, creditor or public administrator can file an affidavit if personal property net of liens does not exceed $20,000.

On liens, the register keeps the index but removes nothing on its own. A mortgage or deed of trust leaves the record only when a satisfaction is recorded. Tax liens take a different route. They fasten to the parcel on its January 1 listing date, and collection is a court foreclosure.

A house with liens, back taxes, tenants or repair needs can still sell for cash without a listing or showings. The deed goes to this same register and carries the same recording fee and stamp as any sale.

What phone number reaches the Johnston County Register of Deeds?

Dial 919-989-5160 for land records, or 919-989-5161 for vital records and marriage licenses. The office is in Suite 209 at 207 E. Johnston Street, Smithfield.

How much does a standard Johnston County deed cost to record?

A plain deed runs $26.00 up to page 15, with $4.00 added for each later page. Loan paperwork is priced higher, $64.00 up to page 35. The stamp is a separate charge.

Is there a charge for recording a satisfaction in Johnston County?

No. The schedule lists satisfactions of a security instrument, trustee's satisfactions, notices, certificates and affidavits of satisfaction at no charge.

Is e-recording available for Johnston County deeds?

Yes, through an approved submitter. CSC eRecording, EPN, Indecomm, NTC and Simplifile are listed, and your closing company normally sends the file for you.

Whose job is it to pay the transfer stamp in Johnston County?

The seller pays it at the register's counter while the deed is still unrecorded. Johnston County's schedule gives the rate as $2.00 per $1,000 of consideration.

What we confirmed on the official page

Fees

Selling in Jones County?

Where do I take a deed in Trenton, and what are the hours?

The office is at 101 Market Street in Trenton, with a mailing address of PO Box 189, Trenton, NC 28585, and the phone number is 252-448-2551. Staff are at the counter Monday to Thursday from morning to late afternoon, though documents stop being accepted for recording at 4:30. Fridays are short: open from 8 a.m. to noon, with 11:30 as the recording cutoff.

That short Friday matters for a closing. A deed that reaches the counter after 11:30 on a Friday is not recorded until the next open day, which is Monday, so sellers in Jones County usually schedule signing early in the week.

The office describes its job as recording and keeping births, deaths, marriages, service discharges, notaries, assumed names, maps and real estate transactions. Its real estate indexes reach back to the late 1700s, and a search for records before 1978 has its own page on the county site.

How much will Jones County charge me to record the deed?

Trenton posts a deed at $26.00 covering page 15 and under, adding $4.00 for each later sheet; the county schedule is dated October 1, 2016. A deed of trust has a longer base of 35 pages at $64.00.

Real estate charges listed on the Jones County register's October 2016 schedule
What you are recording or requestingAmount shown
Loan security (deed of trust)$64.00 to page 35, $4.00 per page past that
Deeds and other instruments$26.00 to page 15, $4.00 per page past that

Plain copy25 cents

The schedule also lists the excise stamp, at $2.00 for each $1,000 of purchase price. Its information page says $1.00 per $500 of consideration, which comes to the same figure.

Does Jones County require tax office approval before a deed is recorded?

Yes. The register's page says every deed, together with a completed Tax Certification Form, must be presented to the Tax Office for approval before the document can be recorded. The form is also called the Tax Data Sheet or Tax Collection Form, and the register's site links to it.

Two more local rules sit alongside that step:

  • Under a Jones County ordinance, every deed must show the tax parcel ID number on its first page.
  • A resolution under G.S. 161-31, effective September 1, 2007, bars the register from accepting a deed for real property that is subject to delinquent taxes.

So an unpaid Jones County tax bill can stop a deed at the counter. A seller with back taxes should plan to pay them at or before closing, using the closing agent to settle the bill so the deed is accepted the same day.

Which recording standards apply to a Jones County deed?

Paper filed from July 1, 2002 forward must meet the layout standards in G.S. 161-14(b), and the Jones County register lists them on its site. A document that falls short triggers the $25.00 nonstandard document fee in addition to the usual recording fee.

  • Sheets sized 8 1/2 by 11 or by 14.
  • Three blank inches above the text on page one, half an inch on page one's other edges, and half an inch all around on the pages behind it.
  • Dark ink on white paper in a type size of at least 10 points.
  • Printing that appears on one side of the sheet only.
  • The kind of instrument named just under the top margin, and the preparer named on page one.

The register may waive the nonstandard fee if the print is smaller than 10 point but still legible once scanned. Maps and plats follow separate rules: they must be 18 by 24 inches, with one mylar and one paper copy, and a Jones County review officer must approve the map before it is recorded.

How do liens and satisfactions work in Jones County?

An old mortgage is cleared by recording a satisfaction, and the Jones County register charges nothing for it. Two kinds exist: a Satisfaction of Security Instrument signed by the secured creditor, and a Trustee's Satisfaction signed by a trustee or substitute trustee. The county notes that satisfaction by presentation ended October 1, 2011.

Wills are not recorded at the register. They go to the Jones County Clerk of Court in Trenton, which a seller handling an inherited house should know before heading to the wrong counter.

Under state law a tax lien reaches the parcel as of its January 1 listing date, bringing penalties, interest and costs with it, and an unpaid lien is enforced through a foreclosure action in court. Before you sign a sales contract, get a current payoff figure from the Jones County tax office.

What do I need to know about Jones County property tax before selling?

Jones County taxes are due September 1, and they are treated as delinquent on January 6, when interest of 2 percent for January applies, then 3/4 percent each month after. A mailed payment counts by its U.S. Postal postmark, and a postage meter date is not accepted.

Jones County last revalued on January 1, 2022, with the following revaluation set for January 1, 2030. Market changes between those dates are not counted. A seller who disagrees with an assessment can call 252-448-2546 to set up an informal appeal before March 1, and later appeals may need a formal hearing before the county review board.

Find the tax office at 418 Hwy 58 N in Trenton, where the counter shuts at five o'clock Monday through Thursday and at midday on Friday. Partial payments are taken at the Tax Collections Office, and a payment plan is available only if no enforced collection action has begun. Agricultural and forest tracts can qualify for use value taxation, and a new application goes to the assessor in the regular January listing period.

What does the Jones County housing market look like?

Few counties in the state are as thinly settled. The Census Bureau puts Jones County at 9,575 people for July 1, 2025, below the 10,153 counted in 2010, with 4,804 housing units over 471.37 square miles. In 2020 that meant 19.5 people per square mile.

Survey figures for 2020 through 2024 show a middle-of-the-market owned home at $130,300, and owners occupy 79.4 percent of them. Renters pay a median $747, and households earn a median $59,641. Residents 65 and older are 26.8 percent of the county, so many sales here involve an older owner or an estate.

Construction is slow, with 46 building permits shown for 2025. Fewer new homes on the market means a Jones County seller competes mostly with other resales, and a house that needs repairs can sit for a long time.

Does a cash sale change the recording steps in Jones County?

A cash buyer's deed travels the usual route. It clears the tax office, carries the parcel number on page one, has its stamp paid by the seller, and reaches the register ahead of the weekday or Friday cutoff.

The difference is pace and condition. A cash deal skips the lender appraisal, and the house is bought in its current state. That can help an owner who has liens, a vacant house, tenants or an estate to wind up. Overdue taxes must still be cleared at closing so the register will take the deed.

More questions about Jones County, NC Register of Deeds

What are the Jones County Register of Deeds hours?

Monday through Thursday it opens at 8 a.m. and closes at 5 p.m., but the last recording is taken at 4:30 p.m. Friday hours run from 8 a.m. to noon, with the last recording at 11:30 a.m. The phone is 252-448-2551.

Can Jones County record a deed if property taxes are unpaid?

No. A resolution under G.S. 161-31, effective September 1, 2007, bars the register from accepting a deed for property subject to delinquent taxes. Pay the bill first, then present the deed.

What must page one of a Jones County deed show?

The tax parcel ID number, as required by a county ordinance, plus the type of instrument and the preparer's name. A 3 inch top margin and 1/2 inch side margins also apply.

Does Jones County bill for recording a loan release?

No. The county lists a satisfaction of a deed of trust as free, and that holds for either type, the creditor's signed form or the trustee's.

Where are wills recorded in Jones County?

At the Jones County Clerk of Court in Trenton, phone 252-448-6220, not at the Register of Deeds. The register records the deeds that follow.

The schedule prints the state excise tax on real estate conveyances as $2.00 per thousand, with $1.00 up to $500. Under the statute the seller owes one dollar per $500 of value, counting any leftover part as a full unit, and pays the register first.

The county's sheet adds a note on where the money goes. One half stays with the county, and the other half, less a 2 percent handling fee, goes to the state. That fee split is the county's bookkeeping and does not change what the seller owes.

When you receive a settlement statement from the closing attorney, look for the excise line on the seller side next to the recording line. Ask the register's office if the amount does not match the sale price on your contract.

Which Lee County documents carry no recording charge?

Cancellations are free, which covers releasing an old deed of trust. A military discharge is also free to file, along with one certified copy of it.

Everything else follows the page-based fees. The following items commonly come up when a house in Lee County is sold:

  • The buyer's deed of trust, if there is a loan, charged at the higher base.

Can I be told when something is recorded against my Lee County property?

This helps owners who are away from a house, who own an inherited property, or who rent a home out. A filing under your name that you did not expect is a red flag for fraud, and the email gives you a chance to call the office quickly.

Deeds and other documents can also be searched through the Sanford and Lee County deeds online portal that the county links. Use it to confirm a deed from your closing has appeared and to read the book and page of earlier deeds.

The Lee County Tax Office, 106 Hillcrest Drive in Sanford, handles listing, appraisal and assessment of real estate, personal property and registered motor vehicles, and it collects both current and delinquent taxes. It keeps weekday hours from eight to five.

Three direct lines cover the main needs:

  • Collections: 919-718-4662
  • Listings: 919-718-4661
  • Appraisals: 919-718-4660

The department offers a comparable sales tool called Comper on its page, which sellers can use to see recorded sales near their address. State rules apply to the bill itself: the bill falls due on September 1 and carries no interest if paid ahead of January 6, with 2 percent interest added after that date and 3/4 percent a month from February 1.

Before saying yes to an offer, collect your own deed, a loan payoff statement if you owe on the house, and the newest tax bill. If a lien shows on the title, ask the lender to record its cancellation so the record is clear for the next owner.

Lenoir County by the numbers

Where in Kinston does Lenoir County keep its deed records?

The Register of Deeds sits at 101 North Queen Street, Kinston, ZIP 28501, and takes mail at PO Box 3289, Kinston, 28502. The front desk number is 252-559-6420, and the office lists lcrod@lenoircountync.gov for email.

Weekday counter and recording hours run 8:30am to 5:00pm. The same desk files maps, assumed names, notary oaths and military discharges, and it issues birth, death and marriage records, so a seller who also needs a certified family record can ask for it in the same stop.

County voters choose the register every two years, per G.S. 161-1. Whoever holds the job applies state recording law, which means a Lenoir County deed follows the same ground rules as one filed in Raleigh or Asheville.

How does a signed deed become a recorded Lenoir County deed?

Once the grantor signs before a notary, the paper goes to the Kinston office along with the money. The deputy stamps the date and time, indexes grantor and grantee names, and assigns the book and page that title searchers will use.

  • Have your closing attorney prepare and notarize the deed.
  • Send it with the page fee and excise tax, by hand, by post to the PO box, or electronically.
  • Collect the receipt and note the book and page.
  • Check the index a few days later to confirm your name shows as grantor.

The county says it now takes e-recordings and sends interested filers to Simplifile at (801) 223-1046. At the counter a debit or credit card works, though the county adds a small usage fee. Mail orders for vital records are different: the office wants cash or a money order, never a personal check, along with a stamped return envelope and a photocopy of the requester's picture ID.

What will recording cost at the Kinston counter?

Recording charges come from the state, and the Lenoir County office posts its own fee sheet as a link on its Register of Deeds page. Call the office to confirm the sheet in force when you file.

Selected statewide recording charges under G.S. 161-10
DocumentCharge
Standard instrument$26 buys the first 15 pages; each page beyond adds $4
Mortgage or deed of trust$64 runs through page 35; each page beyond adds $4
Paid-off loan releaseNo charge
Map or plat$21 a sheet
Certified copy$5 on page one plus $2 per added page
Nonstandard paper$25 on top of the usual fee

Clearing an old loan before a Kinston sale adds delay but no filing charge.

What does the state excise tax add to a Lenoir County deed?

The tax works out to $1 per $500 block of price or value, and a partial block is billed as a whole one. G.S. 105-228.30 puts payment on the transferor, so it is the seller's cost, due in Kinston before the deed goes on the books.

The county keeps one share for its general fund and forwards the other to the state each month, after refunds and the county's retained allowance.

Most sellers never hand over a separate check. The closing attorney deducts the tax at settlement and delivers it with the deed, so it shows up as a line on the seller's side of the closing statement.

Why should a Lenoir County seller care when the deed is recorded?

In North Carolina, G.S. 47-18 ranks competing claims by the moment they reach the county books. A buyer who holds only a signed deed can lose to a creditor or later purchaser whose paper was registered first.

That timing is why lenders want recording on closing day. A deed that sits in a briefcase over a weekend leaves a gap during which a new judgment or lien could attach ahead of it.

Options, leases longer than three years and first-refusal rights fall under the same rule. If your Kinston-area property has any such document, ask for a title search that looks for them before a closing date is fixed.

What does Lenoir County look like for sellers?

Lenoir County's seat is Kinston, and La Grange and Pink Hill are two other communities. The Census Bureau counts 55,837 people for July 1, 2025, a bit above the 55,122 of the 2020 count and well under the 59,495 of 2010.

  • Housing units: 27,402 as of July 2025.
  • Owner-occupied: 59.2% of homes (2020 to 2024), and renters hold the remainder.
  • Typical home value among owners: $120,500.
  • Typical gross rent: $861 a month.
  • Household income at the midpoint: $45,143, in 2024 dollars.
  • Land area: 399.09 square miles, and 131 building permits in 2025.

The county took shape in 1791 out of territory once governed through Bath, Craven, Johnston and Dobbs. Kinston dates to 1762 under the spelling Kingston, and the courthouse stands where a frame building first went up in 1779 at Queen and King Streets. With values near $120,500, a fixed recording fee takes a bigger bite of a modest sale, so price your net with it in mind.

How does the Lenoir County Tax Department connect to a sale?

The tax office shares the building at 101 North Queen Street and answers at 252-527-7174. It lists, appraises and bills property, and it maintains the records that follow transfers. Real estate sits on a permanent listing system, so owners file only when something about the property changes, while mobile homes, boats, aircraft and unlicensed vehicles must be listed in January or draw a 10 percent late penalty.

The county's page says values stayed fixed since the reappraisal effective January 1, 2017, and it describes a new reappraisal effective January 1, 2025. Real estate appeals for 2026 closed on April 23, 2026, when the review board adjourned, and the county announced that the 2027 window opens January 1, 2027.

The state calendar applies here. September 1 is the due date, and January 6 starts a 2 percent charge that is followed by monthly interest of three-fourths of one percent. Under G.S. 105-355 the tax lien is dated from the listing date, which keeps old balances on the parcel. Ask the tax office for a payoff number and have the attorney pay it out of proceeds at settlement.

What should a Kinston-area owner confirm before selling?

Begin with the index itself. Ask the Register of Deeds what appears under your surname and under the seller before you, then follow up on any loan, easement or plat you did not expect.

  • Names on the latest recorded deed, including heirs if a prior owner has died.
  • A recorded release for every paid-off loan.
  • Any unpaid county bill or present-use deferral.
  • Whether you will file by paper or sign up for e-recording.
  • Excise tax and filing charges, so your net number is realistic.

For an inherited house, call the clerk of superior court about the estate steps before anyone signs, and order a certified death certificate from the Register of Deeds, which keeps those records.

More questions about Lenoir County, NC Register of Deeds

What are the office hours at the Lenoir County Register of Deeds?

Weekdays from 8:30am to 5:00pm at 101 North Queen Street in Kinston. Call 252-559-6420 or write to PO Box 3289, Kinston, NC 28502.

Is e-recording available through Lenoir County?

Yes. The register's page says e-recording is available and lists Simplifile at (801) 223-1046 for enrollment. Ask your closing attorney whether the firm already files this way.

Who owes the excise tax on a Lenoir County deed?

The seller owes it, as transferor, before recording. The tax is $1 per $500 of value, with any part of a block counted whole, and the attorney normally subtracts it at settlement.

Do I pay to record a mortgage release in Lenoir County?

No. Recording a release of a mortgage or deed of trust is free under G.S. 161-10, so ask your lender to send it to the Kinston office after payoff.

How do I learn what property tax is due on a Lenoir County house?

Phone the tax department at 252-527-7174. Bills fall due September 1, interest begins January 6, and your attorney can pay the balance from sale proceeds.

Where is the Lincoln County Register of Deeds office?

The Lincoln County Register of Deeds is at 206 Gamble Drive, 2nd Floor, Lincolnton, NC 28092. The office phone is (704) 736-1744, the fax is (704) 736-8830, and questions can go by email to register@lincolncountync.gov.

Doors are open from 8:00am to 5:00pm Monday through Friday, except on county holidays. The county commissioners authorized the office to stop accepting real estate recordings and notary oaths at 4:30pm every day, so a deed that arrives at 4:45pm waits for the next business day. If you are driving in from Denver or Maiden on a closing day, plan to arrive well before that cutoff.

Payment is by cash, certified or business check, money order, or debit and credit card. Personal checks are not taken, and cards are not accepted for a recording that contains excise tax, which matters for deed filings since most sales carry that tax.

What records can I find at the Lincoln County Register of Deeds?

The office holds real estate records back to 1769, birth and death records from 1913, and marriage records from 1868. Real estate records back to 1769 and the birth, death and marriage indexes are also searchable online.

For a seller, the useful pieces are the grantor and grantee indexes, recorded deeds of trust, plats and maps, powers of attorney and assumed names. The office also keeps military records and notary public records. Since January 1, 2022 it no longer issues birth certificates for people born outside Lincoln County, so heirs closing out an estate should request those certificates from the county where the person was born.

  • Deeds and deeds of trust recorded against the parcel.
  • Plats and maps that show boundaries and lot numbers.
  • Powers of attorney used by a signer who is not present.
  • Death records for owners who have died.

How must a deed be formatted to be recorded in Lincoln County?

A paper deed must follow the state formatting standards in G.S. 161-14, which the Lincoln County office posts on its site. An instrument that misses them is still recorded, but the register collects a $25 fee for a nonstandard document.

Paper formatting standards listed by the Lincoln County Register of Deeds
ItemStandard
Sheet size8 1/2 x 11 or 8 1/2 x 14
Top margin, first pageAt least 3 inches
Other margins, first pageAt least 1/2 inch on three sides
Margins, later pagesAt least 1/2 inch on all sides
Ink and paperBlack on white
Smallest typeNo smaller than 9 points
Sides printedFront only
Instrument typeNamed at the head of page one, under the margin

Pen is allowed for filling blanks or making corrections. If the only defect is print smaller than 9 points, the register may waive the $25 charge when the page is still legible, but the office advises using 9 point type to avoid rejection. The standards cover instruments in general, deeds of trust and mortgages, UCC filings, Torrens registration and master forms.

What do recording fees and excise tax cost in Lincoln County?

State law fixes the fees. G.S. 161-10 sets a base of $26 for an ordinary instrument of up to 15 pages and $64 for a mortgage or deed of trust of up to 35 pages, with $4 for every page past those limits. Bundling a second instrument into the same document adds $10. Lenders pay nothing when they record a cancellation.

The excise tax is separate. Under G.S. 105-228.30 the rate is $1 per $500 of the price or value, with part of a $500 block rounded up, and the seller must deliver it to the register ahead of recording.

Because card payments are barred for recordings with excise tax, the closing attorney usually brings a firm or trust account check.

How does recording protect a seller in Lincoln County?

Recording fixes the order of claims. Under G.S. 47-18, a deed or sales contract has no force against lien creditors or paying buyers until the register of deeds in the land's county has it on file, and timing of that filing sets who comes first.

For a Lincoln County seller that means two practical points. First, confirm that old mortgages show a recorded cancellation before closing, since a lender's payoff letter alone does not clear the index. Second, options, long leases and first-refusal rights are governed by that statute too, so have the closing attorney look for them.

The county tax collector notes that property taxes are ordinarily prorated at closing by the closing attorney, so ask your attorney to show the proration on the settlement statement.

What does Lincoln County look like for home sellers?

Lincoln County is a growing county that runs its offices from Lincolnton and includes the town of Maiden and the Denver area. Census figures show 98,654 residents in July 2025, a 13.7 percent rise since the 2020 base, spread over 295.85 square miles of land.

  • Housing units: 41,865 in July 2025, with 785 building permits issued in 2025.
  • Owner-occupied rate: 78.9% for 2020 to 2024.
  • Typical home value: $321,000.
  • Median household income: $80,016 in 2024 dollars.
  • Median gross rent: $1,015.
  • Mean commute: 29.3 minutes each way.

The county's drinking water comes from Lake Norman, and the tax rate sheet lists fire districts including Alexis, Crouse, Denver, East Lincoln, High Shoals and North Brook. A buyer shopping in Denver or the east side pays a different fire district rate from one buying near Lincolnton, so the tax sheet is worth reading before you quote a net figure.

What should a seller carry to the Lincolnton counter?

Bring the signed, notarized deed, the excise tax, the page fee and a plan for the receipt. If a lender is paying off a loan, line up the cancellation so the old deed of trust comes off the index promptly.

  • A deed that meets the margin and type size standards, with the instrument type printed at the top.
  • Payment in an accepted form, remembering that cards are not taken when excise tax is due.
  • Arrival before 4:30pm, the daily cutoff for real estate recordings.
  • The full list of owners, spouses and heirs who must sign.
  • A look at the tax rate sheet: the county rate is 0.499 per $100 for 2026/2027, and the City of Lincolnton adds 0.5000 for a printed 0.9990 total.

Tax matters live in a different office. Collections are handled by the Lincoln County Tax Department, and the 2027 revaluation takes effect January 1, 2027, so ask that department about current-year balances. County voters elect the register of deeds, as G.S. 161-1 provides.

More questions about Lincoln County, NC Register of Deeds

What time does the Lincoln County Register of Deeds stop recording?

Real estate recordings and notary oaths stop at 4:30pm every day, even though the office stays open until 5:00pm. Arrive before 4:30pm on closing day.

Can I pay the Lincoln County recording fee with a credit card?

A card works for most services but not for a recording that contains excise tax. Use cash, a certified or business check, or a money order, and do not bring a personal check.

How far back do Lincoln County real estate records go?

Real estate records in the Lincoln County office go back to 1769, and the same years are searchable online. Birth and death indexes start in 1913 and marriage indexes in 1868.

What happens if my deed is not formatted correctly in Lincoln County?

The register will still record it, but it collects a $25 nonstandard document fee. Using black ink on white paper, correct margins and 9 point type avoids the charge.

Where do I get my Lincoln County property tax balance before I sell?

Call the Lincoln County Tax Department or use its online payment page. Taxes are due September 1 and become delinquent after January 5, and the closing attorney normally prorates the current year.

Which Franklin office files Macon County deeds?

Macon County deeds go on the record at the county Register of Deeds office in Franklin. Macon County government works from 5 West Main Street, Franklin, NC 28734, and the county switchboard at (828) 349-2000 can connect you to the Register of Deeds.

The county directory lists a vault line and several extensions for the office. Ask the office for its recording hours and its same-day cutoff before you plan a closing around it.

The Register of Deeds is elected by county voters for a two-year term under G.S. 161-1. The office applies the same statewide recording rules used in all North Carolina counties, so a Macon County deed follows the same format, fee and tax rules as a deed filed elsewhere.

What do recording fees and the excise tax cost in Macon County?

Fees come from G.S. 161-10, and the excise tax comes from G.S. 105-228.30. The register collects both before a deed is recorded.

  • Ordinary instruments: a $26 base for up to 15 pages, with $4 for each page past that.
  • Mortgages and deeds of trust: a $64 base for up to 35 pages, again $4 for each extra page.
  • Satisfactions and cancellations of mortgages and deeds of trust: no fee.
  • A second instrument in the same document: $10.
  • Excise tax: $1 per $500 of value, rounded up for any partial block.

The seller is the transferor and owes the excise tax. The money splits two ways: the county keeps half for its general fund, and the rest goes to state revenue officials monthly, net of refunds and the county's allowance. Closing attorneys in Franklin normally deduct the tax from the seller's proceeds and deliver it with the deed.

Why does filing order matter to a Macon County seller?

Filing sets priority. G.S. 47-18 withholds protection from deeds, sale contracts, options and leases over three years until they are registered where the land lies, and whoever registers first comes first.

A parcel that has passed through several families can carry old rights of way or boundary agreements. Have the closing attorney search the Macon County index for each prior owner, and ask the Land Records office for the parcel map so the legal description on the new deed matches the tax parcel.

Filing a deed does not itself clear the tax bill. The county assesses property as of January 1, so ask the tax office who is billed for the current year and plan the proration with your closing attorney.

What does the Macon County Land Records office do?

The Land Records office, also called the Mapping Office, is on the main level of the Macon County Courthouse on the Square in downtown Franklin. It is the place to get property cards, parcel maps and county maps, and it has public terminals for document searches, property searches, collection information and assessment data.

The tax office also links an address change form, property tax forms and a land records search from its page, so many owners can pull a map or a parcel record before they visit. A seller preparing a listing can print the parcel map to check the lot lines against the deed.

The Tax Department itself sits in the annex at 5 West Main Street. It posts a separate tax scroll for Highlands next to the county scroll.

Which Macon County dates matter after I record a deed?

The county tax calendar drives most of what follows a sale. The Macon County Tax Department lists these dates on its home page.

Important dates listed by the Macon County Tax Department
DateWhat happens
January 1Date of assessment; personal property ownership and place of taxation are set as of this date
January 1 to 31Listing period for personal property, except tagged motor vehicles, and for exemption and exclusion filing
January 5Last day to pay property taxes without interest
January 6Interest begins
AprilReview board hears appeals
April 15Last date to file listings with a prior approved extension
AugustCurrent-year tax bills processed and mailed

The 2026 board began meeting April 7, 2026 and adjourned April 17, 2026, and appeals had to be received or postmarked by that day. The tax office also notes a 2027 reappraisal and offers an online appeal portal, so check there after any new values are mailed.

How do Macon County owners pay a tax bill, and what scam warning applies?

The county moved to a new bill-pay platform, and owners must register their accounts again and re-enroll in paperless billing. The portal runs around the clock and offers AutoPay, text alerts with pay-by-text, and an automated pay-by-phone line. The collections office answers at (828) 349-2142.

The tax office also posts a warning about lookalike government scams. It says the Macon County Tax Office does not contact taxpayers asking to come to their homes to collect a debt, and it tells residents not to share personal information and to hang up at once. Sellers who owe back taxes are a likely target for calls like that, so route any demand through the official office and your closing attorney.

Businesses must list business personal property each January under G.S. 105-308, which covers furniture, fixtures, machinery and similar equipment. A rental owner who keeps furnishings in an income-producing unit should ask the Personal Property desk at (828) 349-2144 whether those items need listing.

What is Macon County like for home sellers?

Macon County is a county whose communities include Franklin, Highlands and Nantahala. County population reached 39,232 in July 2025, a 6.0 percent rise from the 2020 base, across 515.58 square miles of land.

  • Persons 65 and over: 31.7 percent.
  • Housing units: 27,700, against 18,406 households for 2020 to 2024.
  • Persons per household: 2.04.
  • Owner-occupied rate: 77.6 percent.
  • Typical owner-occupied home value: $251,900.
  • Typical rent: $803; household income at the midpoint: $59,061 in 2024 dollars.
  • Accommodation and food services sales: $205,516 thousand in 2022.

Those figures show more housing units than households. A buyer who plans a second home or a rental will want to see the recorded deed and any restrictions on file with the register.

What if the Macon County owner has died?

Call the clerk of superior court before the register of deeds. The directory lists the Estates and Special Proceedings line at (828) 349-7204, and that office can explain whether a small estate affidavit fits or whether the estate needs a personal representative.

For intestate estates, G.S. 28A-25-1 permits an affidavit filed with the clerk in the county of domicile when personal property less liens does not exceed $20,000, any time after 30 days from death. A surviving spouse who is the only heir may reach a limit up to $30,000 after the spousal allowance. The affidavit lists each tract of land the person owned.

When someone has authority to sign, the deed then goes to the Register of Deeds. Bring the certified death record if the register or the title company asks for it.

More questions about Macon County, NC Register of Deeds

Where is the Macon County Register of Deeds?

The office is part of Macon County government in Franklin, whose main address is 5 West Main Street, Franklin, NC 28734. Call (828) 349-2000 and ask for the Register of Deeds to confirm hours.

What do Macon County deed filings cost?

An ordinary instrument starts at $26 for up to 15 pages, with $4 per page after that, and the excise tax adds $1 per $500 of value. The office collects both before it records the deed.

Does Macon County have a separate tax scroll for Highlands?

Yes, the Macon County Tax Department posts a separate tax scroll for Highlands next to the main county scroll. Ask the tax office which scroll applies to your parcel.

When do Macon County property taxes become late?

January 5 is the last day to pay clear of interest, which starts January 6. Current-year bills are processed and mailed in August.

Where can I get a parcel map in Macon County?

Visit the Land Records office in the Macon County Courthouse on the Square in Franklin, or use the land records search linked from the tax office page. Property cards, parcel maps and county maps are available there.

What will the Madison County Register of Deeds do with my deed?

It files the signed deed in the county's permanent index, and that filing is the moment the transfer becomes visible to everyone else. The county's contact page gives 828-649-3131 for the office.

Valuation and yearly billing sit elsewhere, with Tax Administration in Marshall. The register is the keeper of paper. It checks the document, takes the fixed state fees and the seller's stamp tax, and notes the time.

Call before you travel and ask for the current counter hours, or let your closing attorney deal with the office from a distance.

Tax Administration, by contrast, posts weekday hours of 8:00am to 5:00pm at 5707 Highway 25/70, Room 25. Plan a call to each office, since a deed that is filed cleanly but left off the tax roll will keep sending the old owner a bill.

Why does the filing time on a Madison County deed matter?

Because North Carolina ranks competing claims by when each was registered. G.S. 47-18 says deeds, options, leases running beyond three years and rights of first refusal gain force against lien creditors and paying purchasers only on registration in the county where the land sits.

For a Madison County parcel, the Madison County office is therefore the only one that counts, wherever the seller lives. Excise tax on a parcel spanning two counties is paid where more of the value lies.

  • A buyer whose deed waits unfiled can lose out to a creditor who files first.
  • A new lender's deed of trust that is filed late may rank behind liens that were not meant to come first.
  • A deed filed in a neighboring county leaves the Madison County record unchanged.

This is why closings end with the deed and the loan documents going in on the same day, in the order the attorney planned.

What does the state charge at the Madison County counter?

One statute, G.S. 161-10, sets the fees for every North Carolina county alike, so Madison County has no separate schedule of its own to publish. A plain deed is $26.00 up to 15 pages, and a deed of trust is $64.00 up to 35 pages.

Madison County recording charges, taken from G.S. 161-10
Document or serviceCharge
General instrument, up to 15 pages$26.00
General instrument, each extra page$4.00
Mortgage or deed of trust, up to 35 pages$64.00
Mortgage or deed of trust, each extra page$4.00
Plat, each sheet$21.00
Certified copy, page one$5.00
Certified copy, later pages$2.00 each
Release or cancellation of a mortgageFree

Two surcharges exist: $25.00 for a document in nonstandard format and $10.00 for every extra instrument bundled into one filing. Payment comes before filing.

Does a Madison County land split need a recorded plat first?

Usually yes when the split counts as a subdivision. The county's subdivision ordinance, revised June 28, 2022, says no lot shown on a required subdivision plat may be sold or transferred until the final plat has been recorded by the Register of Deeds.

The same ordinance tells the register not to file a subdivision plat that has not been approved under its rules. It also bars a building permit or a septic permit until the Planning Board has approved the final plat and the register has recorded it. Buyers of a back lot are often caught here, because a lender will not close on a parcel that cannot be permitted.

  • Combining or recombining recorded lots without adding lots is carved out, as long as the results meet the county's standards.
  • A family subdivision has its own approval, and the final plat carries a title block that says so.
  • Plats must comply with G.S. 47-30 to be suitable for recording.

The ordinance also lets an owner sign contracts to sell by reference to an approved preliminary plat before the final plat exists, though the lot itself cannot transfer until the final plat is recorded. That sequencing is worth knowing when a buyer wants to sign early. If you plan to carve a lot off a Madison County tract before selling, ask the county's subdivision administrator whether your split needs a plat, and do it before you list.

Who pays the Madison County deed stamp tax?

The seller. G.S. 105-228.30 puts a levy of $1.00 per $500 of price, counting any fraction of $500 as a full unit, on whoever transfers the land. The register of deeds takes the money before the deed is entered.

Half stays in county hands. Monthly remittances carry the other half to the Department of Revenue, less a 2 percent county share of it.

Read the exact figure off your settlement statement, beside the loan payoff and any tax balance. A cash purchase works the same way.

Can Madison County owners get an alert when a document is filed?

A county newsletter dated March 2022 announced one. The register of deeds offered an email notice whenever a recorded document matched a name an owner had signed up to watch. The sign-up asks for your name, your email and the names to monitor, followed by a confirmation email that may land in a junk folder.

For anyone who owns land they rarely visit, or who is settling an estate, such an alert can catch a forged deed or a stray lien the day it reaches the index. Ask the office whether the service is still running.

Electronic filing is another question for the same counter. Your closing attorney knows which vendors the office accepts.

How do the two Marshall offices work together after a sale?

Filing the deed gives the assessor the new owner. The assessor's page says that office tracks ownership changes and keeps the property maps.

  • After recording, call Tax Administration at 828-649-0734 and confirm the owner name.
  • Have the year's September 1 bill paid or credited in the closing so the lien does not follow the house.
  • Where a circuit breaker deferral exists, give the tax office 10 days to prepare deferred bills, as its page requests of attorneys.
  • Take the parcel number from the tax bill and put it on the deed paperwork.

County housing data hints at the workload: 11,874 units in 2025, with 77.5 percent owner-occupied across 2020 to 2024 (Census Bureau). Ordinary sales and family transfers dominate.

What should a Madison County seller have ready before closing?

A title agent or attorney files the paperwork. Gather these items so nothing stalls.

  • The old deed, so names can be copied exactly.
  • Payoff statements for each deed of trust on the parcel. Lenders then file cancellations, and those carry no fee.
  • The parcel number, plus a survey if the acreage is uncertain.
  • For an inherited house, estate paperwork. Small estate affidavits go to the superior court clerk, and G.S. 28A-25-1 sets the dollar limits.

A cash buyer can take a house with a tangled history, yet every link still has to be recorded properly. Running the title early gives you time to chase a missing release.

More questions about Madison County, NC Register of Deeds

Which number reaches the Madison County Register of Deeds?

828-649-3131, per the county contact page. Ask about counter hours and recording options before you send anything.

What is the price of recording a deed in Madison County?

A deed of 15 pages or fewer costs $26.00, then $4.00 per added page. Mortgages and deeds of trust cost $64.00 through page 35. State law fixes both amounts.

Which side of the sale pays the Madison County excise tax?

The seller pays, at $1.00 per $500 of price, and the register takes it ahead of recording.

Does Madison County charge to file a mortgage release?

No. G.S. 161-10 sets no charge for filing a satisfaction or cancellation.

After recording, who updates the tax bill owner in Madison County?

The assessor tracks ownership changes, so confirm the new name with Tax Administration and settle the September 1 bill at closing.

What can the Williamston registrar's office do for me?

Easements, agreements, assignments, releases, plats, deeds and deeds of trust are all recorded at this counter, and an index tracks them, with a separate index for plats.

Uniform commercial code statements join the real estate books too, a practice the county dates to July 1, 2001. Other jobs include filing military discharge papers (DD-214), keeping assumed business name, partnership and incorporation instruments, and giving oaths to notaries. Vital records on hand begin in October 1913 for births and deaths and in 1883 for marriage licenses, with an index for 1872 to 1882.

A seller should remember that whatever sits in these books is what a title searcher will find. Look first, and ask the office about anything odd you see, such as an easement or an unreleased lien.

Can Martin County deeds be searched online?

Yes: the county points to martinrod.org for deeds, with records back to 1771. A separate online service takes vital record orders, and an index of births, deaths and marriages is posted too.

An hour in the index pays off for a house you inherited or have held for decades.

  • Search under your name and under the previous owner's name.
  • Match the legal description on the latest deed to the tax record.
  • Watch for old deeds of trust with no release after them.
  • Note any plat or state right of way plan that touches the lot.

What does Martin County list as its recording charges?

The county's fee sheet follows the statewide schedule and warns that amounts may change. Call about the total before you mail a payment, and write money orders to Martin County Register of Deeds.

How should a deed be formatted before it goes to Martin County?

Paper signed on or after July 1, 2002 has to meet the layout standard the county quotes from G.S. 161-10. Miss it and the office adds $25.00 to the recording charge.

  • Letter or legal paper, 8 1/2 inches wide.
  • Three inches left blank at the head of page one, with half an inch on the other edges.
  • Black on white, type no smaller than 9 points, printed on one face.
  • The words naming the instrument type, printed above everything else on page one.

Blanks and corrections may be inked by hand, and exhibits face the same standard. What counts is the day it was signed, not the day it arrives.

Who pays the excise tax at a Martin County closing?

The seller. Martin County's sheet gives $2.00 per $1000 of purchase price, and the statute expresses that as $1.00 for each $500 or part of $500.

The register takes it when the deed is filed, splitting it between the county general fund and the state. The county may retain 2 percent of the state portion.

The settlement statement prints the dollar amount, and it sits on the seller's side of the ledger beside the loan payoff and any tax balance. No deed gets filed until it is paid, so let the statement settle the number.

Why does filing sequence matter on a Williamston sale?

Under G.S. 47-18 a conveyance, an option, a lease over three years or a right of first refusal gains force over lien creditors and paying purchasers only through registration. Martin County land registers here whatever the owner's address.

If a creditor's judgment is filed ahead of your buyer's deed, the buyer can rank behind it. Attorneys avoid that by filing as soon as funds are confirmed.

What else does the Martin County office issue besides land records?

Marriage licenses and certified vital records are the other daily business, and heirs selling an inherited house often need the second kind. A certified copy of a birth, death or marriage record costs $10.00, and the county limits who may request one: the person named, a spouse, parents, siblings, children, grandchildren or grandparents, an authorized agent or attorney, or someone who needs it for a legal determination of a personal or property right and can prove it.

An executor or heir therefore usually brings proof of the relationship or a document showing legal authority. Uncertified copies are open to the public at $0.25 a page.

  • Marriage license fee: $60.00, issued between 8:00 AM and 5:00 PM, valid for 60 days from issue.
  • Both parties must appear with proof of age and proof of a Social Security number.

  • The county says a premarital physical is no longer required.

When does Martin County send tax bills, and when is interest charged?

A recorded deed leaves the tax bill alone. Bills for real and personal property go out in July or August, with a September 1 due date. Interest-free payment runs through January 5, with the deadline moving to the following business day if January 5 is a Saturday, Sunday or holiday.

A 2 percent penalty starts January 6, and interest of three-fourths of one percent accrues monthly after that. The collector must also advertise unpaid real estate tax in the local newspaper from March 1 to June 30, and the taxpayer pays extra for that notice.

Visit the collector at 305 East Main Street, Room 125, any weekday from 8 AM to 5 PM, or call 252-789-4360. A written payoff before closing lets the bill come out of your proceeds.

How does Martin County's housing stock look in Census data?

The mid-2025 estimate is 21,601 people, down 2.0 percent since April 2020, on the Census Bureau's estimates base, living among 11,071 housing units. The 2020 to 2024 owner-occupied rate was 66.8 percent and the median home value $109,700.

Household income at the median was $48,578 in 2024 dollars, and 19.7 percent of people live in poverty. Building permits for 2025 numbered zero. Seniors make up 26.9 percent of the population, and the median gross rent was $758.

With values this modest, deferred repairs can make a traditional lender balk. A cash buyer can purchase it where it stands, repairs untouched, and close once title is clear. Have your attorney run the land records early so any deed of trust still uncancelled is released before closing.

The seller, at $2.00 per $1000 of price by the county's wording, collected as the deed is filed.

What happens to the parcel map once a McDowell County deed is filed?

On the assessor's page, GIS mapping is the unit that processes deed transfers and updates the maps, and it doubles as plat review officer. That puts deed transfers and parcel maps in the same hands, so check the map after your deed is recorded.

The assessor sits at 60 E. Court Street, open the same weekday hours, with separate extensions for real property, mapping and land records. A 2027 real property reappraisal is announced on that page, and new values will land on whoever owns the house then.

  • Ask mapping whether your parcel shows the shape and acreage you expect.

Which relief programs on a McDowell County parcel affect a buyer?

  • Elderly or disabled exclusion: takes off the larger of $25,000 or half the assessed value of the home and up to one acre, without a lien. The owner must be 65 by January 1 or totally disabled, and the county asks you to phone for the yearly income cap.
  • Disabled veteran exclusion: removes $45,000 of assessed value on a one-time application, with no age or income test.
  • Circuit breaker: needs five preceding years of ownership and occupancy and an application each June 1. Three years of deferred tax sit as a lien, and a death, a transfer or leaving the home makes them payable.

How do McDowell County tax foreclosure auctions work?

Why does filing order matter on a McDowell County house?

The county has 2,760 veterans, some of whom may qualify for the exclusion in G.S. 105-277.1C.

Monday through Friday, 8:30am to 5:00pm, at 35 West Fort Street. The number is 828-652-4727.

  • The name on the latest deed. On an inherited property, the last recorded owner is often the person who died.
  • The property record card at Reval.MeckNC.gov, which lists bedrooms, bathrooms and other characteristics the county uses to value the house.
  • The county's no-cost alert service, so a later filing under your name reaches you.

A closing attorney will run a full title search in any event. Doing a light version first tells you whether a sale will be quick or whether an old lien, a missing release or an unprobated estate has to be cleared up before closing.

What steps carry a signed deed to the public record?

Four steps get a deed from signature to the public index. The state treats its fee list as complete and exclusive, so payment is due when you file.

  • Match the grantor's name and legal description to the prior deed.
  • Have the seller's side cover the excise tax.
  • Add the page-count fee and any surcharge.
  • Hand in the original and keep proof that it was recorded.

A lender's satisfaction after payoff is recorded free and will show up in the index afterward.

Where do veterans and homeowners go for other filings?

Discharge papers are recorded at this office, and the county has 44,881 veterans in Census survey data for 2020 through 2024. A property tax break for disabled veterans is another matter: applicants complete Form NCDVA-9 with a Veterans Service Officer and file with the county assessor. The exclusion covers $45,000 of value and has no age or income cutoff.

The register is an elected county officer, chosen every two years under G.S. 161-1. Questions about deed contents or title for a specific house belong with a closing attorney. Value and exemption questions go to Tax Administration.

How can I pay, and how do I guard my title?

At the counter the office takes cash, Mastercard, Visa and Discover, checks, money orders, and approved escrow accounts. Checks need a printed name and address and a phone number, and they go to the Mecklenburg County Register of Deeds. Starter and counter checks are turned away, and a bounced check may cost $35.

The office offers a no-cost Property Fraud Alert that notifies you when any document under your name reaches the records, which suits owners of vacant or inherited houses. Anyone buying on a contract for deed should know Chapter 47H obliges the seller to record the contract, or a memorandum of it, inside five business days.

If you own a Mecklenburg house burdened by back taxes, a title snag or a difficult tenant, a cash buyer can set a closing date that works and use a closing attorney for the recording.

More questions about Mecklenburg County, NC Register of Deeds

What does Mecklenburg County bill for filing a deed?

$26 covers the first fifteen pages, plus $4 for each page past that. A loan instrument costs $64 for thirty-five pages. Documents outside the format rules carry a $25 surcharge.

Which party pays the deed stamp tax in a Mecklenburg sale?

The seller owes it. The rate is one dollar per $500 of price, rounded up for a partial block, and it is due at the counter.

Does recording a mortgage satisfaction cost anything?

No charge applies. The fee schedule lists satisfaction instruments as free, so the burden is only to confirm your lender files one after payoff.

Can I look up Mecklenburg land records on my own?

Yes. A modern online database covers documents from March 1990 forward, a historic index covers 1763 through February 1990, and records can be inspected at the office from half past eight to half past four.

What happens to a deed that breaks the format rules?

It is still recorded, but you pay $25 on top of the usual fees. Margins, tiny type and two-sided pages cause most of those cases.

The staff acts only as a recording office. State law bars the register and employees from practicing law, so any question about what a deed should say goes to an attorney.

What can I search in Mitchell County's online records?

The search site at mitchelldeeds.com holds real estate indexes and images from 1994 to the present. Older material, from 1861 through 1993, sits in an Index Book Viewer under the search menu.

That 1994 line matters for sellers of long-held family land. A deed of trust from the early nineties, a right-of-way, or a division of a family tract may appear only in the older books.   • Median gross rent: $813.

Why does recording order matter in Mitchell County?

G.S. 47-18 says unrecorded transfers and options give way to lien creditors and paying purchasers, and that rank follows the time of registration. Registration happens at the county where the land sits, so Mitchell parcels are registered in Bakersville.

Which county offices touch a Mitchell County house sale?

The collector's calendar has bills going to the January 1 owner of record in August, so the closing papers need to say who covers the year.

What should veterans and older owners in Mitchell County know?

The Census Bureau counts 946 veterans in Mitchell County for 2020 to 2024, and 27.6 percent of residents are 65 or older. Both groups may qualify for property tax relief, and neither claim is filed with the Register of Deeds.

What does the Montgomery County Register of Deeds handle?

This office files the paper trail of land ownership in Montgomery County: deeds, deeds of trust, easements, plats, releases and the index that ties them together. The county's department page calls it the legal custodian of real estate and vital records.

The staff also handle veterans' discharge records (DD 214), assumed name and partnership filings, and UCC fixture filings. Residents go there for marriage licenses and certified copies of birth, death and marriage certificates, and newly commissioned notaries take their oath there.

A seller in Troy, Biscoe, Candor, Star or Mount Gilead meets this office at the very end of a sale. A buyer's title examiner searches its index before closing, and the new deed lands in its books afterward. A quick cash sale follows the same route as any other.

How large is Montgomery County, and what is a typical house worth?

Montgomery County is a small, rural county in the Uwharrie region, home to an estimated 26,403 people in mid-2025. Its 491.54 square miles of land work out to roughly 52 residents for each square mile, and the 2020 headcount of 25,751 was lower than the 27,798 counted in 2010.

Who owes the excise tax at a Montgomery County closing?

That falls on the seller. Under the statute, whoever transfers the property hands the tax to the county's land records office ahead of recording (G.S. 105-228.30).

The levy is $1.00 on each $500 block of value, and a partial block is counted as a whole one. Half of every payment stays in county hands and the other half goes to the State.

  • Your closing attorney normally carries the payment with the deed.
  • If a parcel spans two counties, the county with more of its value collects.

What do recording fees look like in Montgomery County?

No local price list exists here. G.S. 161-10 sets a single schedule for every register of deeds, calls it complete and exclusive, and requires payment before filing.

  • An ordinary deed is priced by page count, with a flat charge covering the opening pages and a smaller one for every sheet after those.
  • A mortgage or deed of trust costs more than a deed, with a longer first stretch of pages.
  • Plats are priced per sheet and certified copies per page.
  • Filing the lender's release after payoff is free.
  • A page that breaks the state formatting rules picks up its own add-on charge.

Read the statute for the exact dollar figures. If your payoff is part of the sale, the free release means the lender's cleanup step will not cost you anything extra.

How does the Montgomery County tax office use what is recorded?

The Tax Administrator keeps the ownership and parcel records that begin with recorded deeds, then lists, values and bills each property. According to the county tax department page, the office oversees about 30,000 parcels of real property.

Which office sends your bill depends on the address. The county collects its own tax plus the real estate tax for Biscoe, Star, Candor and Mount Gilead. Troy collects for itself. Lake Tillery, Badin Lake and Wadeville fire district charges ride along on the county bill.

The state tax lien reaches the parcel on the listing date (G.S. 105-355), so request a payoff statement from the tax office or Troy before any fall or winter closing.

What if a Montgomery County deed is signed and left unrecorded?

A buyer holding an unrecorded deed is exposed. G.S. 47-18 says a conveyance, an option or a lease running past three years gives no protection against creditors holding liens, or buyers who paid value, until it is entered in the land records of the parcel's own county.

Registration order sets priority. If a creditor records a judgment before the deed is filed, the creditor may win. Families sometimes keep a signed deed in a drawer for years, and that habit is the surest way to create the problem.

The cure is quick. Carry the signed, notarized deed in along with the excise payment and filing fee, and hold on to the recording details the staff give back.

  • Gather payoff letters for each mortgage or lien, and confirm each lender will file its release.
  • Find out whether the county or the Town of Troy collects the tax on your parcel.
  • Have the excise payment and the recording fee ready as separate amounts.
  • Keep the notarized original with the recording stamp once the deed is filed.

Call the Montgomery County Register of Deeds for current hours and ask how it accepts documents before you make the trip.

Which other Montgomery County offices touch a home sale?

The register of deeds is one stop among several. The county's department list includes Inspections, Planning, Environmental Health, Public Utilities, Veteran Services and the Tax Department, and each can come up during a sale.

The county's website also has a how-do-I menu with a real estate and GIS search, a permit link and an occupancy tax payment link. Starting there often saves a phone call.

The seller owes it. The transferor pays the county office ahead of filing, at $1.00 per $500 block of value.

Read G.S. 161-10, the one price list that every North Carolina register of deeds follows. Pages drive the charge for a deed, a mortgage costs more, and a release after payoff is free.

Will the office draft my deed for me?

No. Staff file deeds but do not write them or offer legal advice. A closing attorney or other lawyer prepares the deed, and the office records it after it is signed and notarized.

When is a Montgomery County tax bill late?

The county lists September 1 as the due date and January 5 as the point where a bill is past due. Interest then starts at 2%, and each month from February adds another 3/4 of 1%.

Does the county collect tax on a house inside Troy?

Troy collects its own real estate tax. The county office handles the county bill plus the bills for Biscoe, Star, Candor and Mount Gilead, so a Troy owner can expect a town bill and a county bill.

The same page carries a notice sellers and researchers should read. Staff are back-filling the index for records dated January 1, 1888 through June 30, 1988, and adding parties as they go, so a name may be missing from the online search for those years. The notice tells researchers to confirm in the paper index books at the office.

What does a deed need on its first page to be accepted in Carthage?

A deed arrives finished, signed and notarized, either on paper at the Carthage counter or electronically through a filer. Staff are barred by statute from drafting deeds or advising on them, so a lawyer prepares it first.

The recording requirements page lists what page one of a North Carolina deed or deed of trust has to carry.

  • The name of the person who drafted the document.

  • The grantee's mailing address, which the Tax Department needs for the next bill.

The stamp is paid along with the filing fee. The county's page does the math as $2 for every $1,000 of price, which equals $1 per $500 block. The seller carries that cost as the transferor (G.S. 105-228.30).

Which formatting slips add a charge in Moore County?

Can a law firm or lender e-record in Moore County?

Moore County also runs a free Real Estate Recording Notification Service. Once you subscribe, an email arrives whenever a document is recorded under a name you listed. One address can watch up to 10 names or spellings, and the alert covers only filings made after you subscribe.

What do the 2020-2024 housing figures look like in Moore County?

The federal estimate for mid-2025 is 110,619 people, an increase of 10.9% since its 2020 base. The land area is 697.68 square miles, which gave a 2020 density near 143 residents for each square mile.

One resident in four is past 65, and permits topped a thousand in one year, so the Carthage office sees estate transfers and new construction side by side. A clean chain of recorded documents keeps a sale moving, especially when a house has passed within a family.

What happens at the Moore County Tax Department after recording?

After recording, the Land Records Section at the county Tax Department updates ownership from what the Register of Deeds or the Clerk of Court received. The Tax page lists 1 Courthouse Square in Carthage, 910-947-2255, with weekday service from 8 am to 5 pm.

The latest revaluation became effective January 1, 2023, and the next is scheduled for 2027, followed by four-year rounds. A recorded sale does not reset the assessed value, though a price far outside the assessment can bring an appraiser to the property, per the county's FAQ.

Request the current bill and any past-due balance before closing so the settlement statement shows the payoff.

How do Moore County appraisers find out about changes to a house?

The Tax Department learns about new work mostly through permits. The Appraisal page says the Commercial and Residential Section receives permit data from the county and from Aberdeen, Pinebluff, Pinehurst and Southern Pines, then schedules a site visit to record what was added.

Anything that adds heated floor area counts, and so do decks, porches, patios, sheds, pools and barns. The county still expects owners to report improvements themselves. A seller who finished a garage conversion without telling anyone may find the buyer's inspection and the tax record disagree.

  • Every parcel has an ID, sometimes called the PARID or land record key, that appears on the GIS site and on the bill.
  • The GIS site also shows the field review document and a condensed property record card for each parcel.
  • Customer service at 910-947-2255 can walk an owner through the record.

Checking that card before listing the house catches errors in square footage or features that a buyer's agent will notice.

What are the visiting hours in Carthage?

Weekdays, opening at 8 am and closing at 5 pm, at 26 Courthouse Square in Carthage. Call 910-947-6370, and marriage licenses are by appointment once the application is complete.

Which items belong on the first sheet of a Moore County deed?

Page one needs the drafter's name, a return name and address with an envelope, the grantee's mailing address, the excise stamp and the instrument type. It also needs 3 blank inches at the top.

How much is the non-standard document fee in Moore County?

It is $25, added to the recording fee when a document misses the state formatting standards. The register may skip it for small type when the scanned image reads clearly.

Can I be alerted when something is recorded under my name?

Yes. The county's free Real Estate Recording Notification Service sends an email when a document is filed under a name you list, up to 10 names per address, for filings made after you subscribe.

Who handles my tax bill after the sale?

The Moore County Tax Department in Carthage lists, values and collects, and its Land Records Section updates the owner record from recorded deeds. Call 910-947-2255.

Nash County by the numbers

What does the Nash County Register of Deeds keep on file?

Real estate books here start in 1777, the year Nash County was formed from the western part of Edgecombe County. Marriage records start in 1862, and birth and death records begin in October 1913.

Deeds from 1777 through 1969 are searchable online. Anything newer is available as a hard copy, so a seller hunting for an old deed of trust or a plat should ring the office at (252) 459-9836, the number shown on the county's e-recording page. A Nash County deed of trust or deed that predates 1970 can often be found without leaving home.

Is a house in Rocky Mount recorded in Nash County?

Sometimes, and sometimes in Edgecombe County. The county's health report says Rocky Mount straddles the Nash and Edgecombe line, while the rest of Nash County is largely rural. Check the tax parcel record for the lot before a deed is drafted.

Nash County sits in the northeast part of the state and borders Edgecombe, Wilson, Johnston, Franklin and Halifax Counties. Its eleven municipalities fall into five areas:

  • County seat: Nashville
  • East: Rocky Mount and Sharpsburg
  • North: Dortches, Castalia, Red Oak and Whitakers
  • South: Middlesex and Bailey
  • West: Momeyer and Spring Hope

A seller in Spring Hope and a seller in Sharpsburg record at the same county office, even though the towns lie at opposite ends of the county.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Nash County house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

How should a deed be printed for Nash County?

For documents recorded on or after July 1, 2002, the county's filing standards page condenses the state paper rules into this checklist. A deed that fails the checklist is still recorded, though the office tacks on a $25.00 nonstandard fee.

  • Paper cut to letter (8 1/2 x 11) or legal (8 1/2 x 14) size.
  • A clear 3 inch band at the head of page one.
  • Black characters on a white sheet, no smaller than 10 point.
  • Text on one face of each sheet only.
  • The kind of document named right under that band.

Blanks can be filled by pen. The county's note says the margin on the other edges of page one shrank to one quarter inch on October 1, 2011. Where the type is under 10 points but still readable, the Register may waive the extra charge.

What fees does the Nash County Register of Deeds list for real estate?

The county's 2025-2026 fee schedule prints the real estate charges below. The first four match the statewide amounts in G.S. 161-10. The remaining lines are items that a seller or closing attorney can run into in the course of a sale.

Real estate fees from the Nash County 2025-2026 fee schedule, Register of Deeds section

Who pays the excise stamps when a Nash County house sells?

The seller does. Nash County lists stamps at $1.00 per $500, and G.S. 105-228.30 says the transferor owes the tax at the register before the deed goes on record. A leftover amount under $500 is charged as a full unit.

Expect the stamp to appear among the seller's charges at closing. It is unrelated to income tax on any profit, and its size follows the price recited in the deed.

How do you e-record a deed in Nash County?

A filer signs a Memorandum of Understanding and then receives a filing number. The county's phone for that step is (252) 459-9836.

The office receives electronic filings on weekdays from 8:00 am until 4:30 pm, holidays excepted. Closing attorneys and title firms are the usual filers, so a seller's job is mostly to sign on time and ask which day the deed was submitted.

What if a Nash County lot has to be split before a sale?

The county's planning fees show how much that adds. A recombination or exempt plat costs $25, a minor final plat of two lots or fewer with no road, water, sewer or drainage work costs $50 plus $10 per lot, and a zoning permit is $10. The schedule adds that recording fees for plats are paid to the Register of Deeds when the plat is approved.

New construction or additions inside Bailey, Castalia, Dortches, Middlesex, Momeyer, Nashville, Red Oak, Sharpsburg, Spring Hope or Whitakers also need a zoning permit from that town's office before the county issues construction permits. A buyer who wants to add a room should know that before closing.

A recorded plat sheet costs $21.00 to file, and the county's tax office sells recorded plat copies at $4.00 for a full-size sheet and $1.00 for a reduced one.

Which other Nash County Register of Deeds services touch a sale?

Sellers closing an estate or a move often need a few small items from the same counter. The schedule lists them with their prices.

  • Certified birth or death certificate: $10.00 each.
  • Marriage license: $60.00, and a certified marriage copy is $10.00.
  • Notary oath: $10.00, and authentication of a notary: $5.00.
  • Genealogy copy: $1.00 by mail or $0.10 in the office.

Ask the office which of these an estate sale needs, since the right papers depend on how title passed to the seller.

Why record a deed promptly?

Under G.S. 47-18, paperwork that never reached the register can lose to a later claimant. A deed, option or long lease that was never registered cannot be used against lien creditors or purchasers who paid value, and whoever registers first comes first. A parent's old deed that was signed but never filed is the classic example.

The schedule above lists no fee to record the release of a paid-off deed of trust. When a lender has merged or vanished, ask a North Carolina attorney to guide the cleanup before the listing goes live.

What does Nash County housing look like in the Census?

Nash County's mid-2025 estimate is 99,365 people, 4.6% over the 2020 base, with 175.7 people per square mile in 2020. Owners occupied 63.6% of its 45,068 housing units across 2020 to 2024.

The middle owner-occupied house was worth $191,000, while renters paid a median of $953 a month and the median household brought in $62,426. Builders pulled 483 permits in 2025. Residents aged 65 and up make up 21.7% of the county, and 5,784 are veterans. Median monthly owner costs were $1,367 with a mortgage and $501 without one, and the median gross rent is the $953 noted above.

More questions about Nash County, NC Register of Deeds

Who do I call about Nash County land records?

Call (252) 459-9836, the Register of Deeds number on the county filing standards page. Staff can explain e-recording sign-up and where older books are held.

What will the Register charge to file my Nash County deed?

Expect $26.00 up to 15 pages, then $4.00 more per page. Add $25.00 if the paper breaks the printing rules.

Is there a charge to file a loan payoff release in Nash County?

No. The fee schedule shows satisfaction instruments at no fee.

Which Nash County town offices issue zoning permits before building?

Bailey, Castalia, Dortches, Middlesex, Momeyer, Nashville, Red Oak, Sharpsburg, Spring Hope and Whitakers. The county issues its construction permits only after the town permit.

What are Nash County excise stamps on a deed?

They are the transfer tax receipt, priced at $1.00 per $500 of value and owed by the seller.

Where in Wilmington do you take a deed to be recorded?

Real estate recording for New Hanover County is handled in Land Records, Suite 102, at 320 Chestnut Street in Wilmington. A second counter on Government Center Drive takes recordings in the afternoon only.
