What information does New Hanover County want on page one?

Quite a bit. Beyond the statewide format rules, the county requires the following on its recordings:

  • A return name and address for the original document.
  • The drafter's name, on every deed and deed of trust.
  • The parcel's tax ID number, on any document that conveys land.
  • The grantee's address, again on conveyances of land.

Tax ID numbers come from Land Records in the county Tax Department, at 910-798-7300. Pull the number early, since it has to be typed onto the deed before anyone signs.

How does the county treat paper that is not standard?

New Hanover County will still record it, for an extra $25.00 under G.S. 161-10(a)(19) on top of ordinary fees. Follow the county's own list below when you file in Wilmington.

  • Page sizes: 8 1/2 by 11 or 8 1/2 by 14 inches.
  • Margins: three inches blank at the top of page one, half an inch elsewhere on that page, and half an inch on every side of later pages.
  • Ink and font: black on white, with 9 points counted as the smallest legible size.
  • Sides: text on the front of the sheet only.
  • Label: the instrument type at the top of page one, outside the blank margin.

Blanks may be inked in by hand, and fixes must use black ink. Releases of deeds of trust or mortgages, in every form, and UCC filings do not have to meet these standards.

What does the county charge to record and copy real estate documents?

The fee schedule for fiscal year 2026-27, revised July 1, 2026, lists the charges below. Plats and maps have their own lines, and a deed that must be re-indexed under later instruments can draw extra index fees.

What does the county say about excise stamps?

The county prints the rate as $1.00 per $500.00 of price, which it says works out to $2.00 per $1,000.00, and it adds that state law makes the seller pay. G.S. 105-228.30 requires payment at the register before recording.

A caller who asks what a house sold for will be told only the stamp amount. The Register does not search titles or report on liens.

The county's fee schedule also prints the stamp rate by era: $2 per $1,000 from 1991 to the present, $1 per $1,000 from 1968 to 1991, and $1.10 per $1,000 before 1968. That history matters if you read an old deed and wonder what its stamp meant.

What can the New Hanover County register do, and what is off limits?

The office keeps the public record and does not advise. The county's FAQ draws the lines clearly.

  • Off limits: legal advice, attorney referrals and title searches.
  • Public: every filed record except DD-214 discharges, open to viewing and copying at the office.
  • Name changes on title: a new deed is needed to add or drop a name.
  • Wills: filed with the Estate division of the Clerk of Superior Court.
  • Maps: subdivision and condominium plats only, not lot surveys.
  • House size and age: ask the Tax Department.

There is also a free fraud alert. Once you enroll, any document recorded under your name triggers an email with a copy. Owners of a vacant or inherited house may find that worth setting up.

Why does the order of recording matter in New Hanover County?

Under G.S. 47-18, whichever instrument is registered first takes priority, and a deed that was never registered gives no protection against lien creditors or buyers who paid value. A deed signed on Friday but filed the following week can lose to something registered in between.

Because the office does not run title searches, ask an attorney or title company to check for open liens before anything is signed.

What other services does the Wilmington office run?

Besides land records, the staff issue certified vital records, passport services and military discharge filings, and they take e-filed assumed business name certificates. Marriage licenses need an appointment, while notary oaths do not.

The county's page also links a public records search and a guide called "Don't Overpay for a Copy of Your House Deed," useful when a closing needs a copy of the vesting deed. The fee schedule lists first-time adult passport books at $165 and passport cards at $65, and certified birth, death and marriage copies at $10 each. A marriage license is $60, and a minor's passport book is $135. Mailed requests for uncertified vital record copies carry a $1.25 fee on the same schedule. For a business-name form, the office keeps printed copies of the Secretary of State form as a courtesy.

What do the Census numbers say about New Hanover housing?

New Hanover County has 128,402 housing units, with 104,856 households averaging 2.19 people. Owners live in 61.4% of occupied homes, which leaves nearly 39% for renters paying a median of $1,417 a month.

Residents who stayed in the same house for a full year make up 83.8%, and 45.4% of adults aged 25 or older finished a bachelor's degree. The county saw 2,332 building permits in 2025. For a seller, the lesson from the recording rules is to arrive with a deed showing the drafter, tax ID and grantee address on page one.

What is the street address for recording a deed in Wilmington?

Go to 320 Chestnut Street, Suite 102, in Wilmington (ZIP 28401). A satellite counter at 230 Government Center Drive takes recordings from 2 pm to 5 pm on weekdays.

Will New Hanover County accept a deed by mail?

Yes, but only to the Suite 102 address on Chestnut Street. The county says mailed recordings should not go to the satellite office.

Who owes the New Hanover County excise tax?

The seller owes it. The county prints the rate as $1.00 per $500.00, and the register can later tell you only the stamp amount on the recorded deed.

Where can I find my parcel's tax ID for a New Hanover County deed?

Ask Land Records at the county Tax Department, 910-798-7300. The number belongs on page one next to the grantee's address.

Are wills filed with the New Hanover County register?

No. They go to the Estate division of the Clerk of Superior Court. The register handles deeds and other property records.

What happens at the Northampton Register of Deeds?

Permanent county records live here: land instruments, plats, UCC filings and vital records. Sellers come in contact with it because the deed to the buyer, and the buyer's loan security, get filed here.

The county says its land books start in 1741, marriage entries in 1863, and birth and death entries in December 1913. Older entries are located through paper indexes. Staff also issue marriage licenses and certified vital records, so say you are calling about a deed.

The county office page gives 252-534-2511 for questions. Ask there for the street address, hours and holiday closings.

How do I search Northampton County land records online?

Free online access sits at northamptonrod.org, where the computerized index starts January 1, 1991. The county describes it as the first time these records were on the internet.

  • Search from 1991 forward on the website for deeds, deeds of trust and releases.
  • For older records, plan on the hard-copy indexes at the office.
  • Search under the owner's name exactly as the latest recorded deed spells it, because the index follows document names.

The title history of a family farm or inherited lot may start before 1991. If your parcel passed through several generations, phone the office before assuming the website shows everything.

What does Northampton County's housing market look like?

Population is sparse. A mid-2025 estimate of 16,491 people sits on 536.70 square miles of land, which is 5.6 percent fewer than the 2020 base and well short of 2010's 22,099. Density in 2020: 32.6 per square mile.

Of 7,857 households, 74.6 percent own. Owned homes are valued around $114,500 at the midpoint, and rents land near $758. About 31.5 percent of residents are past 65. Builders took out 15 permits in 2025, and 91.9 percent of people stayed at one address across a year.

For a long-held house, a clean recorded chain of title matters most, and a gap in the index is easier to fix before a buyer's title search finds it. These numbers are from Census QuickFacts.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Northampton County house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

How does Northampton's local economy affect a home sale?

Buyers follow jobs and paychecks, and this is a small economy. In 2023 the county counted 255 employers, 4,427 jobs and about $212 million in payroll. Stores sold roughly $251.7 million in 2022, or $14,961 per person.

  • Midpoint household income is $50,086, with $32,746 per person.
  • Poverty touches 22.5 percent of residents.
  • High school completion is 85.1 percent among adults, and 17.9 percent hold a four year degree.
  • Drive to work averages 29.9 minutes.
  • 1,017 veterans live here.
  • 74.3 percent of households subscribe to broadband.

These income levels and the shrinking population fit the modest home values, and a fast cash closing may suit someone holding an inherited house or a property needing repairs.

What do filings cost at the Northampton office?

Fees are uniform statewide, so Northampton charges what neighboring counties charge. The table follows the list posted by the state association of registers of deeds, whose latest update is dated February 5, 2024.

Register of deeds fee list for real estate filings

G.S. 161-10 is the legal basis, calling the fees complete and exclusive and collectible before filing.

Who covers the deed tax at a sale?

The seller. Each deed carries a tax of $1 per $500 of consideration, with a leftover under $500 counted as a full $500, and G.S. 105-228.30 makes the transferor deliver it to the register ahead of filing. The county general fund keeps half; the other half travels to the state revenue department in a monthly remittance.

The office page also links a Deed Tax Certification form, a deed of trust fee change notice and a public records redaction request. Ask which, if any, your closing needs.

Which other filings touch a sale?

The office also files loan security instruments, releases and plats. Satisfactions cost nothing, which means an old paid-off loan can be released for free, and the buyer's lender will expect that.

  • A plat is $21 a sheet, which applies if a lot is split before sale.
  • A nonstandard document adds $25.
  • Assignments add $10 for each extra index reference, and a party beyond the twentieth adds $2 a name.
  • A UCC record runs $38 for one or two pages.

Owners of several parcels, or of older estate property, can ask the office to look through the index for liens, releases and earlier deeds ahead of closing. Anything older than 1991 requires a phone call.

What should be checked before listing?

A sale touches the register, the tax department and, with an estate, the clerk of court. Work through this list before closing.

  • Locate the latest recorded deed and compare its names to the people signing.
  • Search 1991 forward for any deed of trust never released, and call about older ones.
  • Ask the tax department what is owed for every open year, including bills from earlier years.
  • Download the parcel's property tax card and GIS map from the tax page so the acreage and description agree with the deed.
  • After an owner's death, confirm with the clerk of court who may sign and whether a will has been probated.

The tax page also links a room occupancy tax return, so a lodging operator at the property should ask the tax department about closing that account.

How is a deed submitted?

Every filing should travel with a self-addressed stamped envelope, the county's page says, along with the signed deed and payment.

  • Compare the deed against the recording standards the state association of registers publishes.
  • Enclose the filing fee and the seller's deed tax.
  • Phone to learn whether mail, couriers or drop-off are accepted.
  • Keep the confirmation, because under G.S. 47-18 a deed binds creditors and later buyers only after it is registered.

Filing order sets priority, so a deed that arrives late can rank behind an earlier lien.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

Who sends the property tax bill?

The Tax Department, at 126 E. Jefferson St. in Jackson, bills Northampton parcels. Its page sets September 1, 2026 for 2026 bills and holds interest until after January 5, 2027. Listed numbers: 252-534-4461 (main), 252-534-5941 (land records) and 252-534-3431 (listing).

The tax page links appeal forms and a list of county property for sale. Before fixing a closing date, ask what balance clears the parcel. An owner who prefers no repairs or showings can ask Cash Home Buyers for a cash offer and set it beside the payoff and recording costs.

More questions about Northampton County, NC Register of Deeds

Which office records deeds for Northampton parcels?

The Northampton County Register of Deeds records it. A deed takes effect against creditors and later buyers once registered in the county where the parcel lies, per G.S. 47-18. Phone 252-534-2511 for the street address and hours.

What is the filing fee for a deed here?

A deed runs $26 for the first 15 pages with $4 added per extra page, and a deed of trust $64 for 35 pages with the same $4 add-on. The seller's deed tax, $1 per $500 of price, is a separate payment.

Is there a free online index?

Yes, from 1991 forward. The county says land records from January 1, 1991 to the present are free at northamptonrod.org, while older records are searched in paper indexes at the office.

Is the seller or buyer responsible for deed tax?

The seller. G.S. 105-228.30 puts the payment on the transferor, due at the register of deeds before filing, at $1 per $500 of consideration.

When is the property tax deadline?

September 1. The Tax Department says interest on 2026 bills starts only after January 5, 2027. State law then adds 2 percent through January and 0.75 percent per month afterward.

The counter opens at 8 in the morning and the last recording goes in at 5:30 in the afternoon, Monday to Friday. Marriage licenses stop a quarter hour earlier. A call before a long drive is a sensible habit if the weather or a holiday could change the schedule.

How far back do Onslow County real estate records go?

The office holds land records going back to 1734. Its Real Estate Records page lists conveyances, deeds of trust, cancellations of deeds of trust, powers of attorney, assumed names, separation agreements and road maintenance agreements.

Anything filed there is open to view at the counter. Staff will not complete forms or search a title for you. The county explains that doing so would amount to practicing law without a license, so owners who want a title check should hire a closing attorney or order one through a title company.

An owner can also ask in writing to have a Social Security, bank or card number blacked out of an image on the county website. The county charges nothing for that request.

What does Onslow County want on a deed before it is filed?

Three things stand out on the county's pages: an excise tax statement, a tax certification form and clean personal data. Check each one before you present a deed.

  • Page one must show the excise tax, including a line for zero when nothing is due.
  • A tax-exempt transfer needs the legal reason for the exemption on page one.
  • A Tax Certification Form must be attached to the back of the original deed. That rule dates from July 1, 2013 and came from a decision of the Onslow County Tax Office.
  • Identity and account numbers stay out of the document unless the law or a court order requires them, or unless only the last four digits show.

Closing attorneys know these rules. A seller who prepares paperwork alone should phone 910-347-3451 first.

What does the Onslow County office charge, besides the state fees?

Payment and filing rules on the Onslow County Recording Information page
ItemWhat the county page says

When it holds two or more papers with different legal consequences or intent, each signed and acknowledged on its own and able to be recorded alone. The county charges $10 for each instrument after the first.

Each paper that could stand by itself is treated as its own instrument. If you are unsure how many instruments your package holds, ask the closing attorney or the office at 910-347-3451 before presenting it, because the extra charge is collected at the counter along with the base fee.

Who pays the excise tax on an Onslow County house sale?

The seller does. The county page prints the tax as $1 per $500, or part of $500, of the price or value conveyed, and it refers readers to G.S. 105-228.

Payment goes to the register of deeds ahead of filing, and page one of the paper has to state the figure. Ask your closing attorney to add this tax to your payoff and other seller charges so your net sheet matches the check you receive.

Why does the filing time matter for an Onslow County sale?

Priority follows the clock. Under G.S. 47-18, a deed, mortgage, option or lease longer than three years has no force against lien creditors or later buyers for value until it is registered where the land lies.

A deed in a desk drawer protects nobody. In Onslow County, a judgment filed against a seller on Monday can beat a buyer whose deed reaches the office on Tuesday. Ask the closing agent for the recording time plus the book and page, and keep that confirmation with your sale papers.

How do mail-in and plat recordings work in Onslow County?

Send an addressed, stamped return envelope with any mailed package so the original comes back to you. Checks are written to Onslow County Register of Deeds for the full amount.

Electronic plat submission through approved vendors began May 1, 2021, and plats can still be brought in. The county keeps the 18 by 24 inch statutory size. Sticky notes over wet-ink seals confuse the scanner, and residue gets a plat rejected. Anyone dividing a lot ahead of a sale should hand over a clean original.

Who lives in Onslow County, and how does that shape a home sale?

Onslow County added residents quickly. Between the 2020 census count and July 2025 its population rose 6.2%, ending at 217,175. Land area is 762.08 square miles, and the housing stock stands at 91,470 units.

Households skew young: 23.8% of people are under 18 and 12.8% are 65 or older. Median household income for 2020 to 2024 is $68,148, and 11.5% of people live in poverty. Owners hold 63.7% of homes, with a typical owner-occupied value of $236,400 and typical rent of $1,265. Workers report a 22.4 minute average commute, and 25,185 residents are veterans. The county issued 1,372 building permits in 2025, so new construction competes with resale houses in many parts of the county. A seller near a new subdivision should expect buyers to compare the two.

What should a seller do about liens before the deed goes in?

Clear them first. Filing a lender's release costs nothing at this counter, so the only variable is how fast the lender sends it.

Property tax attaches to the parcel as of the January listing date, which means an unpaid bill follows the house to the buyer's closing. Ask the Onslow County Tax Office for the balance owed and have it paid from your proceeds. A seller whose debts exceed the likely price should talk to a closing attorney before choosing a date, since a recorded lien blocks a clean transfer.

602 Anne Street, Jacksonville, NC. Mail is sent to 109 Old Bridge Street, Jacksonville, NC 28540, and the phone is 910-347-3451.

Weekday recordings are accepted until half past five. The marriage license desk shuts 15 minutes sooner.

Will the Onslow County office help me fill in a deed?

A Tax Certification Form goes on the back of the original deed. Page one must also show the excise tax amount, or the reason for any exemption.

What extras does the Orange County fee schedule list?

Older rates appear only for reading history: $1 per thousand from January 1, 1968 through July 31, 1991, and $1.10 per thousand earlier. The seller owes the tax at the counter before filing. For the exact stamp amount on your price, ask your closing attorney rather than guessing.

What will Orange County staff do, and what will they send you elsewhere for?

They issue certified copies of deeds recorded in the county and help owners find a plat by book and page. They send title searches to attorneys.

The county FAQ says a title search must come from an attorney, or a paralegal under an attorney's supervision. It adds that changing a name on a recorded deed takes a new deed, and it suggests legal counsel for anyone not used to drafting one. Whichever county holds the land. Registration there fixes the deed's rank against rival claims, whatever city the buyer or lender calls home.

What should you bring to the Orange County Register of Deeds?

Someone collecting a certificate for another person, such as an agent or attorney, must show papers proving authority. For deeds that run long, list many parties or use an odd page size, phone the office first. Added-page, non-standard document and extra-name charges can apply to those.

Where does Roxboro file its deeds?

The courthouse-area office is 21 Abbitt Street in Roxboro (ZIP 27573). Its listed number is (336) 597-1733. The Tax Office, which you will also need, is at 13 Abbitt.

County materials describe the department as the custodian of Person County's most important records. Visitors come for:

  • plats, cemetery records, grave removals, military discharges and genealogy files

Sellers mostly want the first item and the filing of the deed. Phone before you go to learn counter hours and whether electronic filing is offered.

How many properties does the Person County deed office serve?

Roughly 19,000 homes and apartments (19,023 housing units, per QuickFacts for July 2025) fall under this office, on 392.34 square miles of land. Of the homes lived in during 2020 to 2024, 77.3% were occupied by their owners, and those owner homes had a median value of $213,900.

The county counted 16,063 households and about 40,636 people, a 4.0% rise over the 2020 base. Builders pulled just 145 permits in 2025, so most deeds record a resale of an existing house rather than a new build.

  • Owners with a mortgage: $1,393 a month at the median.
  • Median gross rent: $864.
  • Share of residents 65 or older: 23.4%.

On a house in that value range, a flat filing fee and a tax of $1.00 per $500.00 are small pieces of the closing statement. Your title and tax payoff matter far more.

Who is the register, and why does filing order matter?

An elected officer holds the post, with a two-year term (G.S. 161-1). The office takes in conveyances, applies the uniform charges, and collects excise tax before anything goes on record (G.S. 161-10).

Ranking is by time stamp. Under G.S. 47-18, a deed or a lease of more than three years binds neither lien creditors nor purchasers for value until it is registered in the land's own county.

Clerks will not draft a deed or settle who owns what. An unfiled deed gives you no protection, which is why your attorney should file it the moment funds are released.

What will recording a Person County deed cost me?

Every figure is fixed by the legislature, so the Roxboro counter has no discretion.

Charges set by G.S. 161-10 and collected at the Person County counter

Who pays the excise stamp tax on a Roxboro deed?

Whoever gives up title pays, which in a sale is the seller. The tax is due before the deed is filed, and G.S. 105-228.30 sets it at $1.00 for each $500.00 or part of it in price or value.

The county retains half. The state receives the remainder monthly, after refunds and an allowance. A tract that spans counties pays where more of its value lies.

  • Put it on your net sheet, since it reduces what you take home.
  • It tracks the price in your contract.
  • If a gift or family transfer has little stated value, ask the office how it handles that.

Get the figure from your attorney in writing ahead of closing day.

What should I look for in Person County land records before listing?

Take an hour in the index, or pay an attorney to, and hunt for anything that blocks a clean transfer. Old unreleased loans, judgments and forgotten options are the usual finds.

  • Seller names should match the last recorded deed.
  • The contract's legal description should match that deed's.
  • Every earlier deed of trust needs a recorded release.
  • Ask the Tax Office for the balance so the lien clears at closing.

If you financed a buyer yourself, Chapter 47H has you record the contract or a brief memorandum within five business days.

One call to the old lender usually fixes a missing release. Title held by a deceased owner is a bigger job. A cash buyer can move fast, though insurable title still comes first.

How should I prepare a deed for filing?

Bring the signed, notarized original with the tax payment and fee, and check the page count, since each extra page adds four dollars.

Order of events counts. The buyer's lender normally files its deed of trust right after the deed, and your own payoff releases should already be in motion.

  • Look over the notary block for a full date and signature.
  • Add the parcel number to page one if your attorney does.
  • Keep a copy with the registration time on it.

Ask whether the office takes electronic filing, and confirm counter hours before driving over.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

Can I order a certified copy of an old deed or a plat?

Yes, the office searches and copies land records, and the statewide schedule sets the price for certified copies and for filing a plat. Ask the staff whether a copy can be requested by mail or phone, since this page does not list that.

An older deed is useful for three reasons when you plan a sale:

  • It shows the exact words used for the boundary, which a buyer's surveyor will compare against the ground.
  • It names the people who held title before you, which confirms the chain.
  • It may refer to an easement, a road right, or a restriction that survives to the new owner.

Copies are priced per page (see the table), and a plat is filed per sheet. If you ordered a new survey as part of dividing land, the plat is recorded here before lots are sold separately.

Bring the tax parcel number and the names of recent owners to speed up the search, and ask staff which index years cover the period you need. Staff cannot interpret what a deed means, so take any unclear wording to an attorney or surveyor.

What do I do if the owner of record has died?

A deed signed by someone who has died cannot be treated as a normal conveyance, so an estate attorney should say who may sign for the owner. State law lets small estates collect personal property by affidavit, with a cap of $20,000 in G.S. 28A-25-1, and that affidavit lists each tract of land the person owned.

  • Gather a death certificate, which the deed office keeps among its vital records.
  • Search the land records for the last recorded deed to confirm what the person actually owned.
  • Speak with an estate attorney before anyone signs a deed.

An heir who wants a quick sale should know that title company and lender requirements usually decide the timeline, not the filing counter.

The seller does, to the register, before filing. The statute's rate is $1.00 per $500.00 or part of the value.

Do I pay to record the release of my old mortgage?

No. The fee schedule lists no charge for releases of deeds of trust or mortgages.

Because the first paper on file wins. According to the state recording statute, an unfiled deed or option has no force against creditors with liens or buyers who paid value, and ranking among claims follows filing time.

Greenville is where that time stamp gets set, which is why every closing ends with a filing step. A signed deed left in a drawer protects nobody. Hold an old deed from a family transfer that never reached the office? File it, or talk to an attorney, before you advertise the house.

What will Pitt County charge to file a deed?

The General Assembly sets the fees, and the county page says they match in every county. The Pitt summary lists these items:

  • A general instrument such as a deed or easement starts at $26 and adds $4 per page after page 15.
  • A plat costs $21 per sheet, and a non-standard document adds $25.
  • A certified copy costs $5 for page one plus $2 per extra page.
  • Releasing a mortgage costs nothing.

The county's summary lists mortgages and deeds of trust at $56 for the first 15 pages, while the statute text, G.S. 161-10, prints $64 with a 35-page allowance. Call before sending a lender document so the check matches. Cash, check, money order and card payments are accepted.

How is the Pitt County deed stamp tax figured?

The excise tax runs a dollar for every $500 of price, with a leftover part of $500 counting as a full one. Pitt's records page says it follows the sale price.

The seller carries the duty, according to the excise tax statute, and it has to be paid before the register will accept the deed. Pitt keeps half the money and the State receives the other half. Look for the line on your settlement statement.

Does Pitt County accept electronic filing?

Yes. The county takes electronic filings through several vendors and tells filers to call each one to compare prices. Four vendors are listed, each with its own phone number on the county FAQ.

Most sellers never touch this step, since the closing office sends the deed and the buyer's loan papers together. A family transfer with no lender is different: ask whoever prepared the deed whether they file electronically or in person, and who covers the vendor charge.

How can a Pitt County owner watch for deed fraud and check records?

Pitt County has an alert sign-up that notifies owners whenever a filing matches their name or property. The county also runs an online search for recorded documents from September 1762 to the present, searchable by grantor, grantee, document type, book and page, or date range.

  • Search the grantor index for your name to see every recorded deed or lien tied to you.
  • Use book and page numbers from an old deed to pull the full document.
  • Use the county's Online Parcel Information System, run by Tax Administration and GIS, to view parcel boundaries, assessed values, tax districts and flood zones.
  • Older index books can be used on site at the Greenville office.

Do this before listing, especially with an inherited house. A loan that was never released, or a missing link in the ownership record, takes less effort to fix while no buyer is waiting.

What other papers might a Pitt County sale involve?

A Pitt County closing, apart from the deed, can include a deed of trust for the buyer's loan, a recorded release of the seller's old loan, and sometimes a plat or easement. Each one is filed separately and priced under the fee list above.

  • Old loan: confirm the lender recorded a satisfaction.
  • New loan: the buyer's lender records its own deed of trust.
  • Seller financing: see the contract for deed rules in Chapter 47H, which call for recording within five business days.

The county's FAQ lists agreements, assignments, assumed names, leases and subdivision maps among the land-related documents the office records.

What else does the Pitt County register's office keep?

The office is more than a deed counter. It holds birth and death certificates for events in the county, issues marriage licenses, files notary commissions and gives the oath to every notary public. Veterans can file military discharge records here, and the county waives the charge for filing or copying them.

It also takes Uniform Commercial Code financing statements on personal property, listed at $38 for one or two pages. The overlap that helps sellers is notary service. The county lists a $10 notarial act fee tied to a filing, so someone who has not yet signed a deed can ask about doing it at the counter. Call 252-902-1650 first, and bring photo identification.

What does Pitt County's history mean for old deeds?

Pitt County was formed in 1760, and the county says its oldest records include land grants, indentures and property agreements from the 1700s. Online search reaches back to September 1762, and index books for older records are kept on site: look up the grantor or grantee in the alphabetical index, note the book and page, then pull the full document with that reference.

For a seller, an old farm or family tract can have a chain of deeds that runs back generations. If a deed in that chain was never filed, or a name is spelled differently from one deed to the next, a buyer's title search will flag it. Start the search early, and keep every book and page number you find.

What should a Pitt County seller do before closing?

Begin with a title check. Pull the deed that put the house in your name, confirm each old loan has a filed release, and ask the tax office what is owed.

Property tax lives in a different office. According to the collection statute, each bill falls due on September 1, and interest begins after January 5. Pitt County Tax Administration, not this page, gives the balance on your parcel.

Repairs, tenants and estate delays do not block a quick sale to a direct cash buyer. The filing steps stay the same: the deed goes to Greenville.

At 100 E. 1st Street, Greenville, NC 27834. Weekdays only, 8:00 to 5:00, and the county lists 252-902-1650 for questions.

Who covers the deed stamp tax in a Pitt County sale?

Sellers do. The statute names the transferor, and the office takes the payment at the counter. Your settlement statement should show the line.

Is there a charge to file a mortgage release in Pitt County?

No. The county lists satisfactions and cancellations as free. The lender is the one that files the release, so ask yours to do it.

Is there an online deed search for Pitt County?

Yes. The county says documents recorded from September 1762 forward can be searched online by name, type, book and page, or dates.

What is the base fee for a Pitt County deed?

$26 buys a general instrument of up to 15 pages, then each extra page adds $4. Plats are $21 a sheet. Get the final total for your own document by phone, extras included.

They go to the Register of Deeds in the Polk County courthouse complex at 40 Courthouse St., Columbus, NC 28722. Postal mail uses PO Box 308. Weekday hours are 8:30 to 5:00 on the county site, which gives (828) 894-8450 as the number.

The county sums up the office's work as filing deeds, powers of attorney, cancellations of deeds of trust and plats. It also keeps marriage, birth and death records, issues marriage licenses and handles assumed business name certificates. The county site notes that marriage licenses are by appointment only. A home sale reaches this counter at the very end, once the deed is signed.

How does a recorded deed reach Polk County tax records?

The county updates its tax records after a deed is recorded. A recorded plat also prompts an update, with the tax side working alongside the GIS department on mapping.

Sellers often miss the January 1 rule. Polk County treats whoever held title on that date as the taxpayer for the year, even if the house sells in March. Splitting the bill with a buyer is, in the county's words, a private agreement, and it sends those questions to the closing attorney or the agent. What if the Polk County GIS map shows the old owner?

Give it time. The Register of Deeds page says parcel data refreshes every one to two months, so a name can lag behind a fresh deed.

  • Recording comes first; the map follows.
  • If a sale closed in the last two months, wait before worrying.
  • Past two months, call the tax office at (828) 894-8954.
  • For general ownership and transfer questions, the county's transfer page lists (828) 894-8500.

Write down the book and page of your recorded deed. The tax office may want it if a name needs correcting.

What do recording fees look like for a Polk County deed?

One fee schedule applies to every register of deeds in the state, and it is printed in G.S. 161-10. Polk's own page prints no fee list, so phone Columbus for the final amount before mailing anything. These are the statute's figures:

Why record a Polk County deed right away?

Two practical points follow. A deed from an earlier family transfer that never reached the office should be recorded before the house is sold. And a paid-off loan clears title only when the lender files its release. The county's Property Check sign-up emails an alert if anything new is filed against your name, which suits a house nobody lives in.

Does a contract for deed have to be recorded in North Carolina?

Yes. Chapter 47H governs seller-financed deals on homes of up to four families. Within five business days the seller must file the contract itself or a brief memorandum describing it. The buyer may back out until midnight on the third business day.

If either side of a Polk County deal works this way, record promptly and have an attorney read the papers. A forfeiture needs a written notice that gives at least 30 days to cure.

Who else touches a Polk County home sale?

Beyond the register, a sale usually involves the county tax office, which values the parcel and prints the bill, and the settlement agent, who runs the title search and the closing.   • Property Check: a sign-up that warns you about new filings under your name.
  • Powers of attorney: the register records them along with deeds.

A seller who runs a small business from the house or who holds a recorded power of attorney for a parent should ask about these items before closing, so the paperwork lines up with the deed.

What should you bring or send to the Columbus office?

Phone first at (828) 894-8450, since the county page gives no payment or mail-in details. Then gather the items below so the clerk has everything in one visit.

  • The signed deed, or the plat if you are splitting a parcel.
  • Payment for the excise tax, plus the recording fee quoted by the office.
  • The parcel number printed on your last tax bill.
  • The buyer's mailing address, so later notices arrive.

A month or two after recording, check the parcel on the county GIS site. A plat is the one paper that also reshapes the map: the county says the tax office and GIS department work together to update mapping after a plat is filed.

How should a Polk County seller treat the tax bill?

Get the current balance from the Polk County tax office, then tell the closing attorney who owes that year's bill. Tax is due September 1 and can be paid at face value through January 5, according to the collection statute.

A direct cash purchase can shorten the timeline for an inherited, vacant, rented or run-down house. The recording work described above stays the same either way.

What hours does the Polk County Register of Deeds keep?

The Columbus office at 40 Courthouse St. keeps weekday hours of 8:30 to 5:00 per the county site. Phone (828) 894-8450 to confirm, especially around holidays.

If I sell in spring, who owes that year's Polk County tax?

The January 1 owner carries the liability under the county's rule. Whether the buyer reimburses you is settled privately at closing.

How big is the state's deed excise tax?

A dollar for each $500 of price or value. The selling side pays it at the register's counter.

Can I buy Polk County birth and death records online?

Yes, with one limit. The county site says only vital records recorded in Polk County can be bought online, so a certificate from another county must be requested there.

Are old assumed business names in Polk County still valid?

Not if they were filed before December 1, 2017 and never refiled. The county says those expired on December 1, 2022, and the owner must refile at the local register's office.

The county lists the office's duties as real estate recording (deeds, deeds of trust, powers of attorney, releases and real property UCCs), plats and condominium maps, partnerships and assumed names, military discharges, and the satisfaction of deeds of trust.

Staff there also issue marriage licenses, hold certified birth, death and marriage records for events in Randolph County, and swear in notaries. Only the real estate side touches a sale, but a notary oath or a certified copy you need for closing paperwork may be handled at the same counter.

Recording matters because of G.S. 47-18: a conveyance carries no weight against lien creditors or later buyers for value until it is on the record where the land sits.

What is the 4:30 cutoff, and which days is the office closed?

Staff are on hand from eight in the morning until five on weekdays, yet real estate recording ends at 4:30 pm. County commissioners passed a resolution letting the office stop taking real estate documents, notary oaths and marriage licenses at that hour every day.

Closing attorneys know to send deeds before the cutoff. If a signing runs long, expect the filing to slide to the following business day. The register follows the holiday schedule used by Randolph County government, and the county posts the list each year.

Parking, a map and an email link to the office sit on the county website. Questions about records can be sent there, which saves a trip when you only need to know whether something was recorded.

The statute makes the schedule exclusive and requires payment before filing.

A book and page ending in E means the record is with the Clerk of Court, not this office. To add or drop a name, someone must prepare and record a new deed. The office offers no deed forms and no drafting help.

What else is recorded in a Randolph County sale besides the deed?

A deed is the headline filing, but the buyer's lender files a deed of trust, and your old loan is cleared by a certificate of satisfaction. That certificate is how an owner who paid off a mortgage confirms the lien is gone, and the county tells homeowners to check it online by name.

Options, contracts to convey, leases over three years and rights of first refusal also need registration to bind later buyers. A seller-financed contract for deed under Chapter 47H must be recorded, or a short memorandum of it recorded, within five business days.

Mobile homes are a separate matter. The county sends owners to the state motor vehicle office for those titles.

Where do estates and tax liens fit in Randolph County?

Wills are filed with the Randolph County Clerk of Court, and probate proceeds there. For a small estate, a statutory affidavit may suffice when personal property after liens is $20,000 or less, and it lists each tract of real estate owned.

Property tax runs on its own track. The lien attaches on the listing date and can be enforced by a foreclosure action in the nature of a mortgage foreclosure, with a courthouse-door sale. Before drafting a deed for an inherited or tax-troubled house, ask the Randolph County tax office what is owed.

To the Randolph County Clerk of Court, not the register of deeds. The register's FAQ page lists the clerk's phone number for questions about wills and estate filings.

Situations where this comes up before a sale include:

Because the whole file is public, you can also look up your own mortgage cancellation after a payoff to confirm that the lien came off.

What else gets filed with a Richmond County sale?

A deed is rarely the only paper. Per G.S. 47-18, an option, a contract to sell, a long lease (over three years) or a right of first refusal takes effect against outsiders only once registered, in order of time.

  • Owner-financed sales under Chapter 47H need the contract, or a memorandum of it, on record inside five business days.
  • A buyer's mortgage is filed as a deed of trust.
  • Surveys come in as plats.

Ask your attorney to list each document that will be filed, so none is held back.

What if the Richmond County house is in foreclosure or an inherited estate?

These go through the Richmond clerk of superior court instead. In a power-of-sale case the clerk holds the hearing, and notice must be served 10 or more days beforehand, see G.S. 45-21.16.

Once a foreclosure sale is reported, anyone can submit an upset bid during the next ten days. It needs to beat the last figure by 5 percent and at least $750, and every new bid starts the ten days over.

For a modest estate, an affidavit can replace full administration when personal property net of liens stays at $20,000 or under. The deed that follows is recorded in Rockingham.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

What questions are worth asking the Rockingham office before closing?

A short call to 910-997-8250 can head off delays. The staff are used to questions from attorneys, title searchers and owners, and everything they hold is public, so there is no reason to hold back.

  • Has the deed been indexed yet, and what book and page does it carry?
  • Did the cancellation of my old deed of trust record?
  • What is the total of fees for the page count of my filing?
  • Can my attorney's e-Recording submission still go in today?

Write down the answers with the date and the name of the person who gave them. Staff cannot interpret a document, but they can confirm what has been recorded and when.

What should Richmond County sellers do before recording?

Anyone may obtain copies from the office once the proper fees are paid, and the FAQ invites phone calls during working hours with questions about a filing.

Get from the closing attorney the day the deed should be recorded and proof that your old loan was cancelled. After closing, search the county records for both and keep the recorded copies.

Property tax becomes a lien on the listing date, so the current bill stays with the parcel until paid. Ask the Richmond County tax office for the balance. Fees and excise tax are paid at the filing, and the return address you give should be one where the recorded original will reach you.

More questions about Richmond County, NC Register of Deeds

What hours does the Richmond County Register of Deeds record documents?

Staff remain until 5:00 PM, yet counter recording ends half an hour sooner and electronic filing ends at 4:00. Papers that come after 4:30 are recorded first the next morning, so a late closing can push your recording date back.

Where is the Richmond County Register of Deeds?

At 114 E. Franklin Street, Room 101, Rockingham, NC 28379, which is also its mailing address. The county lists 910-997-8250 for questions, and the FAQ invites callers during business hours.

How much is a photocopy of a recorded deed in Rockingham?

The FAQ lists 35 cents a copy when you ask in person. Certified copies are priced under the state table instead, starting at $5 for page one.

Is a booking needed to record a deed in Richmond County?

Nothing on the county page asks for an appointment. Bring the signed, notarized deed during recording hours, or have an eligible submitter e-record it before 4:00 PM.

Can staff draft my deed for me?

No. An attorney or the owner has to prepare the deed, and it must be signed and notarized before it is brought in. The office records the paper and gives no advice on its wording.

What does the Robeson County Register of Deeds record in Lumberton?

Anything that transfers or encumbers land in Robeson County ends up here: the deed to your buyer, the buyer's deed of trust, the cancellation of your old loan, plats and similar papers. The county lists 910-671-3040 for questions about recordings.

The office is barred by state statute from giving legal advice or preparing deeds, and it keeps no forms. Its recording page tells filers to see an attorney for any legal question and for drafting.

Why bother with the record at all? The recording rule in G.S. 47-18 works like a queue: a deed protects its holder against outside claims from the moment of registration locally, and earlier registration wins.

Why does Robeson County require tax certification before a deed is recorded?

Per the register's recording page, every deed needs tax certification before recording, unless it is accompanied by the delinquent tax statement under G.S. 161-31. A deed mailed without either one is returned to the sender.

The certification comes from the county tax department rather than the register. That makes the tax office the first stop for a Robeson deed, and it is the step sellers most often forget.

Ways to get a Robeson County deed certified by the tax office
MethodWhat the county says

What else must be in place when a deed is recorded in person in Robeson County?

Every document recorded in person must show a return name and mailing address. No stamped, self-addressed envelope? A $1.00 mailing fee is added.

The paper must be drafted, signed and notarized before it arrives. Staff cannot repair a bad acknowledgment or write in missing terms.

  • Tax certification or the delinquent tax statement attached.
  • A return name and address on the document.
  • An envelope addressed to you with postage, or a dollar for the office to mail it.
  • The signed, notarized original.

Mailed packages follow the same rules, so include certification at the start. A call to 910-671-3040 can settle questions about a specific filing, and the county also hosts online deed search tools through its records page.

How are Robeson County recording fees set?

These are the statewide figures from G.S. 161-10, identical across North Carolina. Fifteen pages of an ordinary instrument cost $26 and each added page $4. Loan documents get 35 pages for $64. Recording a loan cancellation is free.

Plats cost $21 per sheet, a certified copy starts at $5 with $2 for each added page, and a document in nonstandard form adds $25. Each extra instrument in the same packet adds $10. These are paid before filing, so budget for them at closing, together with the mailing fee mentioned above if it applies.

Which side owes the deed excise tax in Robeson County?

The seller carries it. Under G.S. 105-228.30.

the transferor pays the register ahead of filing, at a dollar for each $500 of value with any fraction counted whole. Half remains with Robeson County. The remainder goes to the state revenue department every month after refunds, and the county may retain 2 percent of that state half. A parcel split between counties is taxed where more of its value sits.

The closing attorney should print the amount on your statement. If you want a figure early, tell the register's staff the sale price.

How do Robeson County property taxes affect a sale?

Whoever owns the parcel on January 1 owes for the year, and a sale later does not clear the seller's liability, the county tax office explains. Proration is a private agreement between buyer and seller, and the seller is mailed the bill for the year of transfer.

To be safe, ask for payment to the tax collector at closing. If the new bill is not yet due, the collector takes a prepayment based on the previous year's rate. A past-due bill on a property that sold during the year can result in both names being advertised.

The tax office that issues the certification is the same one to ask about your balance, so a single call can cover both.

Where do Robeson County parcel numbers and online payments come from?

The county tax administrator's Land Records and Mapping section assigns each tract a parcel identification number, which other county departments use for owner, acreage, value and zoning. The GIS and Addressing section sits in the same division. Quote the parcel number when you contact the tax office about certification, so staff can pull the right record.

The tax office also accepts online and phone payments. The county gives 1-866-249-0705 for the phone option and notes that a convenience fee applies.

  • Parcel number: ask the mapping section or find it on your tax bill.

Before closing, make sure the tax figure the buyer's attorney requests matches what the collector tells you, since the seller is mailed the bill for the year of transfer. Keep the confirmation with your closing file, along with the certification the tax office gave for the deed.

What other filings can accompany a Robeson County sale?

A satisfaction clears your mortgage, and the office charges nothing to record it. Under G.S. 47-18, options, contracts to convey, leases past three years and rights of first refusal bind later buyers only when registered. Under Chapter 47H, an owner-financed contract for deed or a memorandum of it must be recorded within five business days.

  • Check that your payoff results in a recorded satisfaction.
  • Keep copies of every recorded paper.
  • Ask whether a plat or easement affects the lot.

A closing attorney can list every document headed to the register before the day arrives.

What can a Robeson County seller do now to speed recording?

Contact the tax office for certification as soon as the deed is drafted, not on closing day, because the certification has to be in hand before the register will accept the paper. Confirm that the deed carries a return address and that an envelope or postage is ready.

Then follow up with the register to confirm the book and page after filing, and ask the title company or attorney for a copy of the recorded deed for your own files. Keep the receipt for fees and the excise tax, and file it with your closing papers. If anything is returned to you, read the reason first, because the usual causes are missing tax certification or a missing return address.

More questions about Robeson County, NC Register of Deeds

Can Robeson County register of deeds staff advise me on a deed?

No. State statute bars the office from giving legal advice or preparing deeds, and the office has no forms. Take drafting questions, including how to word a conveyance, to an attorney before the signing.

What if a deed is mailed to Robeson County without certification?

The office returns it to the sender. Every deed needs tax certification or the delinquent tax statement before it can be recorded.

What is the route to tax certification for a Robeson deed?

Email deeds@robesoncountync.gov, mail the document to the Tax Department at 550 North Chestnut Street, 2nd Floor, Lumberton, or phone 910-671-3060 for instructions.

Does Robeson County charge for mailing back a recorded deed?

Yes, $1.00, when you record in person and provide no addressed, stamped return envelope. The document must also carry a return name and mailing address.

Does the seller or the buyer owe the excise tax in Robeson County?

It is the seller's. The tax is $1.00 per $500 of value and is paid to the register before the deed is recorded.

Where is the Rockingham County Register of Deeds?

Find it at 170 NC Hwy 65, Suite 150, Reidsville, NC 27320, phone 336-342-8820, fax 336-342-6209. The office is open on weekdays, and its recording policy takes documents until the 4:30 cutoff on days the county is open.

What does a deed need before the Rockingham County office will record it?

The office posts a checklist, and a deed that skips an item can be refused or hit with an added fee. Several items matter most in a house sale:

  • Page one names whoever drafted the deed, a person or a law firm.
  • Page one also carries the buyer's mailing address, because the tax office uses it for billing.
  • Notarized papers show the acknowledgment, the notary's official seal and the date that commission ends.
  • Conveyances show the excise stamp amount on their face. If nothing is owed, the signer writes NTC, short for no taxable consideration.
  • No Social Security, bank account, card, passport or license numbers may appear, except the final four digits where the law demands an identifier.
  • Mail-ins need a check or money order to the Rockingham County Register of Deeds and a return envelope with a stamp. A bounced check costs $25.

None of this has to be sorted out alone on closing day. It matters most for a family deed, a deed into a trust, or a sale with no attorney.

What formatting rules does Rockingham County enforce?

Rockingham County enforces the statewide standard in G.S. 161-14, and a document that misses it picks up a $25 surcharge. Its printed standards list paper size (letter or legal), black ink on white, a clear three-inch strip across the top of the first sheet and a quarter inch of white space around everything else.

Beneath that strip, page one states what kind of instrument it is. Print has to be nine points or larger and appear on a single side. Pen may fill blanks or make corrections. Satisfactions, cancellations, military discharges and separately recorded plats (governed by G.S. 47-30) are exempt. The register may overlook a slightly small font if it copies cleanly, though the county urges sellers to stay above nine points.

Which fees does the Rockingham County office list?

The county's fee page tracks the state statute and adds practical items such as copies. A few lines from it matter to a house seller:

Selected lines from the Rockingham County Register of Deeds fee page

How is the excise tax figured on a Rockingham County deed?

Divide the price into $500 slices and charge $1 per slice, counting a partial slice as whole. The county checklist works two cases: $27,900 climbs to $28,000 for $56 of tax, and $32,200 climbs to $32,500 for $65.

The grantor reports and pays it at the register before the deed is accepted, so it normally appears among the seller's charges at settlement. The county keeps half of the revenue in its general fund and passes the rest to the state.

How are Rockingham County recordings processed, and when is the cutoff?

The office processes in-person filings first, then e-recordings, then priority mail such as UPS or FedEx, then regular mail. Each item has to be opened, reviewed and found acceptable before it is recorded.

The 4:30 p.m. cutoff applies to paper and electronic filings alike. Anyone already in line at 4:30 is served that day. Later arrivals are turned away until another day. If the exact recording date carries real weight, the county advises handing the instrument over at the counter and staying until it is recorded.

E-recording is accepted during business hours. The county lists three benefits: the recorded document comes back right away, nobody has to travel, and a rejection is flagged immediately. Ask the office for its list of approved e-recording vendors.

How do I look up Rockingham County land records and mortgage releases?

The E-Vault is the county's public search site for land records. The county explains that for 1789 through 1995 the official index is the paper index inside the office, with scanned copies under an Old Index Books tab, and that from 1996 on the electronic database in the office is the official index. Vital records are not in the E-Vault, and the county says its website records are unofficial, so the office holds the official set.

Fresh filings appear first in a temporary index shown in red entries and move to the permanent index, in blue, after full indexing. Use fewer characters in the search fields for better results.

For mortgage releases, the lender holds the duty of filing a satisfaction when a loan is paid off. Recording a satisfaction is free, and the county says to reference only one original instrument per satisfaction to avoid a $25 charge for each extra reference. A payoff does not create a new deed. A copy of the satisfaction can be pulled from the E-Vault or at the office.

What should a Rockingham County seller confirm before closing?

Confirm that every old loan shows a recorded satisfaction and that the vesting deed matches the name on the contract. A missing release is the most common snag, and a buyer's title insurer will ask for it.

  • Search the E-Vault for the last deed and any deed of trust on the parcel.
  • Ask the lender about any loan paid off years ago with no release showing.
  • Confirm that the grantee's mailing address and the drafter's name are on the deed.
  • Ask the attorney whether the deed goes by e-recording or in person at Reidsville.

Under North Carolina law a deed carries no weight against later buyers or lien creditors until it is on the record of the county holding the parcel, and rank follows registration time. That is why buyers push for same-day recording after funds move.

More questions about Rockingham County, NC Register of Deeds

When should I arrive to record a deed in Rockingham County?

Arrive before 4:30 p.m. on a weekday. That is when the office stops taking documents for recording, and a later arrival is not recorded that day.

Is there a fee to record a mortgage satisfaction in Rockingham County?

No, recording a satisfaction is free. The county charges $25 for each extra reference when one satisfaction document points to more than one original instrument, so list only one.

Does Rockingham County accept recording by mail?

Yes, send the original with a check or money order to the Rockingham County Register of Deeds plus a stamped return envelope, never cash. Regular mail is handled after in-person, electronic and priority-mail items.

How is the deed excise tax calculated in Rockingham County?

The seller pays $1 per $500 of price, rounding up to the next $500. The county's example turns a $27,900 price into $28,000 and a $56 tax.

Does the Rockingham County register of deeds search title for me?

No. The office says it is a recording agency and cannot help complete forms or run a title search. Hire an attorney or title agent for that, and use the E-Vault for your own look at the record.

What does the Rowan County Register of Deeds office do?

The county describes the register's duty as the integrity, completeness, accuracy and safekeeping of every public record recorded in the office. For a house seller, that means the deed that moves title to the buyer and the deed of trust that secures a loan both live there.

The office offers more than land records. It lists online certified copies of birth, death and marriage certificates, where identity is verified through an online system and a vendor adds a small convenience fee, and it serves as a passport acceptance facility. Those services help families settling an estate, who often need death certificates to support a deed or probate filing. The office also says it is committed to every citizen of the county, which in practice means the same counter serves buyers, lenders and heirs.

How does e-recording work in Rowan County?

Rowan County started electronic recording in August 2010 and accepts electronically submitted documents, maps included. The county says this helps banks, title companies, law firms and other businesses in real estate deals.

The county lists these benefits of e-recording:

  • No travel time or travel cost to reach the counter
  • No check writing, since fees are handled electronically
  • Document security
  • Real-time tracking of document status
  • A quick return of the recording information and a stamped image
  • An easy start for new users

An individual seller does not usually sign up for this. The closing attorney or title company that handles the Rowan County sale will already use a vendor from the county's vendor list.

How does Property Check protect a Rowan County owner?

It emails or texts you when a filing appears under a name or parcel number you register. The county is direct about why: the register does not decide whether a document is genuine, so a fraudulent paper that meets statutory recording requirements and has the fees paid can still enter the record.

Property Check is free, runs around the clock and sends alerts through the contact method you pick. The county admits it cannot block a bad filing, only warn you quickly. If you suspect fraud, call local law enforcement. Owners of vacant or inherited houses in Rowan County gain the most, because nobody is otherwise looking at the record. Questions on the system go to 704-216-8636.

How do I record a map or survey in Rowan County?

Have the Rowan County Review Officer sign the map first, then bring it to the register on one of three sizes: 18 by 24 inches, 21 by 30 inches or 24 by 36 inches. Review Officers work in the Planning Office and the Tax Assessor's office on the second floor at 402 N Main Street in Salisbury.

You get the original back after recording, and the office keeps a digital copy. The county says to ask about electronic map recording. If your lot sits in a recorded subdivision or you hold a recorded survey, a copy costs $2 at the register's counter. Sellers sometimes order one to settle a boundary question before a buyer orders a survey.

What does North Carolina charge on a Rowan County deed?

The state sets one fee schedule for every county, so the amounts below apply in Rowan County as they do elsewhere, and the seller covers the excise tax. The statute prints these figures:

Statutory charges at the Rowan County register
ItemStatute amount
General instrument$26.00 up to 15 pages

The tax is collected up front, ahead of recording. Half goes to the county general fund and half to the state, and a parcel that spans two counties is taxed in the county holding the greater value. The statute calls the recording fees complete and exclusive.

Why does the order of recording matter when I sell?

A conveyance, option or long lease has no force against lien creditors or purchasers for value until it reaches the public record of the county that holds the parcel. Time of registration sets the ranking between competing instruments.

Closing attorneys therefore hold funds until the deed is ready to go on the record. Ask yours to confirm that earlier mortgages were released and that any transfer from an heir or ex-spouse already appears in the Rowan County record.

What if I inherited a Rowan County house?

A death transfer starts with the court clerk, not the register. When a small estate has no will, an heir may file an affidavit with the superior court clerk of the person's home county once 30 days have passed. The statute's limit is $20,000 of personal property, or up to $30,000 when a surviving spouse is the sole heir, and the affidavit lists each tract of real property owned.

Estates above those limits need a personal representative named by the court. After that, the paper that shows who can sign the deed is what the register records, so ask a probate attorney before listing. A buyer's title insurer will want the right authority on record, and Property Check can watch the parcel while the house sits empty.

What happens after a Rowan County deed is recorded?

The Tax Assessor's office updates ownership for billing, and the register's office keeps the recorded image. The Tax Assessor page lists a separate land records contact, so a new owner who does not get a tax bill should reach out there. Rowan County Tax Administration also publishes a parcel map tool for checking boundaries and parcel numbers.

For the seller, recording is the moment the deed becomes public. After that, the real work is the tax proration at closing and any bill for the year that arrives in the buyer's name. The county's tax pages describe the assessor's job as listing, assessing and billing all taxable property, so the register and assessor each handle half of the paper trail.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

What should a Rowan County seller check at the register before listing?

Pull the recorded deed that put the property in your name, then confirm that the names, the legal description and the parcel number match your sale contract. Rowan County offers an online document search for land records, so you can check this before you call anyone.

  • Search for the vesting deed and read the names exactly as recorded.
  • Look for each deed of trust and confirm a satisfaction was recorded after payoff.
  • Check for easements, rights of way or an old recorded map that affects the lot.
  • Sign up for Property Check if the house will sit empty during the sale.
  • Ask the attorney whether the deed will go in by e-recording or by hand.

Fix problems early. A gap such as a deed from a deceased owner or an unreleased lien can add weeks to a closing, and cash buyers value a clean record as much as any other buyer.

More questions about Rowan County, NC Register of Deeds

When did Rowan County start electronic recording?

The Rowan County Register of Deeds began electronic recording in August 2010, and the office accepts electronically submitted documents including maps.

Is Property Check free?

Yes. You create an account, list a name or parcel number and choose how to be alerted when a filing is recorded.

Which map sizes can be recorded in Rowan County?

The county accepts 18 by 24, 21 by 30 and 24 by 36 inches. The Rowan County Review Officer must sign before the map goes to the register.

Who pays the excise tax on a Rowan County deed?

The seller, as transferor, pays it to the register before recording at $1.00 for each $500 or fractional part of the price.

How much does a copy of a recorded survey cost?

The county says a copy of a recorded subdivision map or survey costs $2 at the Register of Deeds.

Rutherford County by the numbers

Which office in Rutherfordton files Rutherford County deeds?

The Rutherford County Register of Deeds works from 229 North Main Street in Rutherfordton. Postal mail goes to Post Office Box 551, Rutherfordton, NC 28139. Per the county, the counter is staffed from half past eight to five on weekdays, holidays excepted.

Two phone lines are published: 828-287-6155 for the main desk and 828-287-6195 for the record room. The county says its holdings reach back into the 1700s, which is useful context for anyone selling a family tract that has passed through many hands in the foothills.

Most sellers never visit in person, because the attorney or title agent delivers the deed. Still, a rejected deed delays the closing and the payout, so the rules are worth knowing.

What papers does Rutherford County keep besides deeds?

The county lists a wide range of public records in its Rutherford register collection:

  • Real estate conveyances and deeds of trust, with their cancellations
  • Assumed names and powers of attorney
  • Road maintenance agreements and plats
  • Separation agreements and similar filings

An online index lets you search by name. A separate alert tool named Property Check emails you when something new is filed against a name or parcel you choose. Heirs watching a house that sits empty can use it to spot an unexpected lien or a forged transfer early.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Rutherford County house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

How must a deed be formatted for the Rutherford County clerk?

Under section 161-14, the county lists layout rules that a deed must meet on the page. Hold your draft up against each one:

  • Page one of a deed or deed of trust carries the preparer's name.
  • Paper is 8.5 inches wide and either 11 or 14 inches long.
  • Page one keeps its upper three inches empty, and every other edge needs at least half an inch of white space.
  • Text prints black on white, at 9 points or larger, on one side of each sheet.
  • The kind of instrument is spelled out across the head of page one.

Blanks and corrections may be inked in by hand. Having your attorney read the draft before signing is the least costly way to dodge a rejected filing.

Will late property tax stop a Rutherford County deed from recording?

It will. The register of deeds cites section 161-10(a)(19), effective October 1, 2011, which makes payment of delinquent taxes a condition of recording.

A tax lien explains the rule. Under section 105-355 it fastens to the property on the listing date, and penalties, interest and costs fasten with it. If the debt goes unpaid, a foreclosure auction can follow, and a person who redeems before confirmation must pay all of it (section 105-374).

Request a written balance for every parcel from the Rutherford County revenue office before you sign a contract, so your attorney can clear it from the sale money.

What fees does the Rutherford County recorder collect?

The statewide schedule in section 161-10 governs. On top of that, the county says military discharges are recorded free and satisfactions of deeds of trust carry no charge.

Recording charges at the Rutherford County desk
ItemPrinted figureSource
Standard instrument, pages 1 to 15$26.00 flatSection 161-10
Standard instrument, each page after 15$4.00Section 161-10
Mortgage or deed of trust, pages 1 to 35$64.00 flatSection 161-10
Mortgage or deed of trust, each page after 35$4.00Section 161-10
Deed of trust satisfactionNoneCounty page
Military dischargeNoneCounty page
Plat sheet$21.00Section 161-10

Under the statute these are the only charges, and they are due before anything is filed.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Rutherford County houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

What excise tax rides on a Rutherford County deed?

The charge is one dollar per $500 of price or value, with leftover dollars rounded up to the next $500 block, and sellers settle it before the deed is filed (section 105-228.30). The county keeps one half and the state receives the other.

A sale for cash is a transfer for value, so the tax is owed. Your attorney can show it as a separate line item.

Land that spans two counties is taxed in whichever county holds more of the value. If your Rutherford tract crosses a county line, raise it with your attorney early.

The statute lets the county retain a small slice of the state half as an allowance, which is bookkeeping between governments.

Where does a Rutherford County seller get a tax balance?

The county revenue department answers tax bill questions at 828-287-6000 and sits at 145 College Avenue, Suite A, Rutherfordton, NC 28139, and the counter hours there match, half past eight to five A collections email address is posted on the same department page.

The department page says all tax bills are due September 1 each year, and that payment by January 5 avoids interest and enforced collection. Mailed payments are honored by postmark through that date. Cash or check payments are taken at the tax office, while online payment runs through a third-party service that adds its own fees, whose amounts the vendor determines.

The page also shows a search for tax bill information, a link to registered vehicle tax receipts, and a list of delinquent tax bills. Pull your parcel's bill and ask for a payoff before your closing attorney orders the deed.

The department also posts a tax rate document. Because the total bill depends on the fire district and town where the house sits, ask the office which rates apply to your parcel instead of assuming a countywide figure. Phone 828-287-6000 and have the parcel number ready.

Does the Rutherford County office file business name certificates?

Yes. The register of deeds records assumed business name certificates, the doing-business-as forms that tell the public a person or firm trades under a particular name in one county or in all 100 North Carolina counties. The recording fee printed on the county page is $26.00.

An online option exists for businesses located in Rutherford County, with a $15.00 service fee added to the recording fee. The county also notes that certificates recorded before December 1, 2017 expired on December 1, 2022, so an older DBA for a rental or landlord business needs a fresh filing. Landlords with rentals should make sure a business name used on leases is still on file.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

Does Rutherford County accept electronic filing?

Yes. The county notes that e-recording through Simplifile began in the office on April 24, 2018, with plats added on February 1, 2022. It also states that microfilming began January 1, 2017.

Speed matters because registration time sets rank. A deed or long lease binds lien creditors and later purchasers for value only from the moment it is registered, and the earlier filing wins (section 47-18). When a buyer's lender and a seller's lender both file on closing day, a same-day electronic filing keeps your deal clean.

Anyone unsure about a particular document can call the main desk at 828-287-6155 before sending it.

More questions about Rutherford County, NC Register of Deeds

What days is the Rutherford County recorder open?

Half past eight to five on weekdays, holidays excepted, per the county. The main line is 828-287-6155. Calling first avoids a wasted trip on a holiday week.

Is filing a deed of trust satisfaction free in Rutherford County?

Yes. The county page says no charge applies to satisfactions, and state law agrees. Make sure your lender files one after payoff.

Who owes deed excise tax when a Rutherford County house sells?

The seller does. Section 105-228.30 sets one dollar per $500, collected ahead of filing, and the settlement statement should show it as its own entry.

Can overdue taxes hold up my Rutherford County deed?

Yes. Under section 161-10(a)(19), as the county explains, back taxes come first. Obtain the balance from the revenue office and pay it at closing.

Does Rutherford County take electronic recordings?

Yes. E-recording via Simplifile started April 24, 2018, and plat e-recording started February 1, 2022. Title companies and attorneys generally use it.
