Sampson County by the numbers

What is on file at the Sampson County Register of Deeds?

Sampson County calls its Register of Deeds the official custodian of records for county residents, keeping a permanent, standardized record of who owns real estate and how it changed hands. The office files deeds, deeds of trust, cancellations, plats, assumed names, powers of attorney and miscellaneous real estate papers.

Vital records share the same counter: birth, death and marriage certificates, marriage licenses, military discharges, and the commission records of notaries public. The office also swears in notaries.

The county site points to online access for these records. Start there for the index search before you phone anyone, and write down the book and page of each deed you find. A homeowner who inherited a Sampson County house can trace each recorded deed back through the chain of owners and confirm every name is spelled the same way, which saves trouble when a title company runs its search.

Will the Sampson County office explain how to fill out a deed?

No. Per the county, this is a recording office alone, and state law forbids the register of deeds and staff from practicing law. They will not provide legal forms, walk you through completing one, or comment on what a filed paper does legally.

That divides the work on a Sampson County sale:

  • An attorney drafts the deed and answers wording questions.
  • A title agent or closing attorney searches the chain of title and arranges loan payoffs.
  • The register of deeds checks each paper against recording rules, takes the charge, and indexes it.

When a house came to you through a family arrangement, see an attorney first. A recorder cannot repair a deed that was written wrongly.

Errors an attorney tends to catch include a misspelled seller name, a missing preparer line on page one, and a land description at odds with the mapped parcel. Sorting those out before closing costs far less than a corrective deed afterward, and it keeps your buyer's lender from pausing the funding.

What does Sampson County charge on a deed filing?

Section 161-10 sets the schedule the register applies, and the statute treats it as the whole list. Payment comes first, so request a combined total when several papers go in together.

Statewide filing charges applied in Sampson County

After closing, request a certified copy of the recorded deed, because lenders, heirs and later buyers tend to ask for it.

Who pays excise tax on a Sampson County deed?

Sellers pay. A deed conveying an interest in land carries a levy of $1.00 per $500 of consideration or value, with a partial $500 block counted whole, and the transferor remits it to the recorder ahead of filing (section 105-228.30).

One half goes to Sampson County's general fund. The rest flows to the state, after refunds and a small collection allowance. For land in more than one county, the county with the greater value collects.

Check that the tax shows on its own line of your closing statement, so your net proceeds are no surprise. If you split costs with the buyer by contract, put the allocation in writing, since the statute assigns the tax to the transferor by default.

How does recording order protect a Sampson County buyer?

Section 47-18 ties a deed, option, first refusal right or lease over three years to the moment of registration: until then it does not bind lien creditors or later buyers who paid value. Order of registration sets rank. That is why closing instructions usually call for same-day filing, and why delay can cost a buyer first position.

Filing the buyer's deed and the new lender's deed of trust together gives that buyer first position. For the seller, a recorded cancellation of the old mortgage clears the index. Forgotten, uncancelled liens can resurface and slow a later sale.

What happens to a Sampson County parcel with unpaid property tax?

Section 105-355 makes unpaid tax a lien as of the listing date, together with penalties, interest and costs. The county may pursue it through a court action patterned on a mortgage foreclosure (section 105-374).

If it comes to that, the parcel is auctioned at the courthouse door. The sale is reported within three days, exceptions or a raised bid can be filed for ten days after that, and anyone redeeming before confirmation pays the tax along with penalties, interest and costs.

Which other Sampson County tools help a seller around recording?

The county runs several web tools next to the recorder's index, each useful before listing:

  • The GIS Data Viewer searches by owner name, address or parcel ID and shows property layers, maps and reports.
  • The Property Record Search draws on the Tax Department's database for the parcel.
  • The Tax Bills site lets you search, view and pay a bill.
  • The Development Services Portal covers building inspection, planning and zoning and environmental health, with permit applications and status checks.

Use the GIS viewer to confirm the parcel ID and acreage match your deed. Check the permit portal for open permits or unfinished work tied to the address, which an inspector for the buyer could uncover.

The county also states that it handles public record requests under Chapter 132 of the General Statutes. Anything the register keeps is public, so assume anyone, a title examiner included, can read what you recorded.

Which Sampson County towns bill tax on a sale?

The county tax office collects for the county, fire and school districts and, at present, for the municipalities of Clinton, Autryville, Harrells, Newton Grove, Salemburg, Turkey and Garland. The address is PO Box 1082, Clinton, NC 28329, and the phone is (910) 592-8146.

The office says county bills fall due on September 1, and it allows a 2 percent discount for payment by August 31, and that parcels still unpaid are listed in a newspaper notice, normally early in April. Your closing attorney needs the current balance for the parcel before anything is sent to the recorder, so request it as soon as you have a contract.

More questions about Sampson County, NC Register of Deeds

Can the Sampson County Register of Deeds give legal advice about a deed?

No. As the county puts it, the office exists to record documents, and the law bars staff from practicing law. They cannot supply forms, explain how to complete them or discuss what a filing means.

What excise tax applies to a Sampson County deed?

It is $1.00 per $500 of consideration or value, paid by the transferor ahead of filing under section 105-228.30. The county general fund gets half, and the state gets the rest.

What is the standard filing charge in Sampson County?

Under section 161-10, $26.00 covers an ordinary instrument through page 15, with $4.00 for every page past that. A deed of trust costs $64.00 through page 35. Cancelling one costs nothing. A certified copy is $5.00, plus $2.00 for each extra page.

What else does the Sampson County office handle?

Birth, death and marriage certificates, marriage licenses, military discharges and notary records, plus notary oaths, according to the county site.

Why file a deed promptly after closing in Sampson County?

Registration fixes priority. Under section 47-18, a conveyance binds lien creditors and later buyers for value only from registration, so quick filing protects the buyer's position.

Which Scotland County office holds the land records?

Land records for Scotland County sit with its Register of Deeds, which describes itself as custodian of deeds, deeds of trust, powers of attorney, plats and other legal papers. The same staff issue birth and death certificates and marriage licenses, and they file military discharges.

A home sale there ends with the buyer's deed landing in this office. The county's page for the department keeps the research tools in one spot, so a seller can read the public trail on a parcel before any offer arrives.

What search tools does Scotland County offer for deeds and plats?

The county splits its tools by era and by purpose:

  • One index covers 1978 to the present together with every plat, and you enter it by signing in as a guest.
  • A second search holds pre-1978 documents at a new web address.
  • The Laurinburg and Scotland County GIS map often shows an owner's name and usually a book and page cite for the deed.
  • A tax foreclosure listing is reachable from the department page, where you scroll to the Scotland County entries.
  • PropertyCheck lets you save names and receive a notice when a filing appears.

For rights of way from before 1978, the office asks you to email the references. Bring book and page numbers if you are chasing an old easement across a lot.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Scotland County house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

What does Scotland County check before accepting a deed?

The recorder reviews each instrument against statutory prerequisites and the state's Document Standards. The county lists the usual ones:

  • Papers are normally originals bearing original signatures and proof of notarization.
  • A North Carolina deed or deed of trust names its drafter, a person or a law firm, on page one.
  • Fees are collected before filing, unless a statute lets the paper be recorded free.
  • A transfer of real property, other than a mortgage or deed of trust, must state the excise tax owed by the grantor.

Staff may not practice law, so they cannot help prepare a deed or discuss its legal meaning. Take drafting questions to an attorney.

Can unpaid taxes keep a deed out of the Scotland County records?

They can. The county says that since July 1, 2020, a deed moving real property is turned away unless the Scotland County tax collector has certified that no delinquent county, municipal or other collector-charged taxes are a lien on the land.

An alternative wording is allowed. The deed may carry a line saying a licensed North Carolina attorney prepared it and that any delinquent taxes will be paid to the collector by the closing attorney when closing money is disbursed. That clause is why local closings tend to route through an attorney's trust account.

Before listing, ask the collector for a payoff on each parcel. Tax foreclosures for the county appear in the listing the register of deeds links to.

What do deed recording and excise tax cost in Scotland County?

Recording charges follow the statewide schedule in section 161-10. The excise tax line comes from the Scotland County page.

Charges tied to a deed filed in Scotland County
ItemPrinted figureSource
Standard instrument, pages 1 to 15$26.00 flatSection 161-10
Standard instrument, each later page$4.00Section 161-10
Mortgage or deed of trust, pages 1 to 35$64.00 flatSection 161-10
Satisfaction or cancellationFreeSection 161-10
Plat sheet$21.00Section 161-10
Excise tax on a deed$2 per $1000, owed by the grantorScotland County page

The county page names several transfers that owe no excise tax: gifts, intestacy, a lease for a term of years, a merger or consolidation, operation of law, and transfers under a will. State statute states the rate as one dollar per $500, which works out to the same $2 per $1000 (section 105-228.30).

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Scotland County houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

What privacy rules apply to documents filed in Scotland County?

Once a paper is recorded in the real property books it becomes a public record that anyone may inspect and copy. Because the county posts images online, it warns filers not to include Social Security, taxpayer ID, driver license, passport, bank account or card numbers, or PIN codes, unless a law or court order requires it or all but the last four digits are redacted.

Anyone can ask in writing to have such data removed from an online image. The request must name the information, identify the document, and say where in the document it appears. The county says no fee is charged for a redaction request, and a person who requests a redaction without authority commits an infraction punishable by a fine up to $500 per violation.

If you are selling and spot your own account number on an old filing, send that written request through the register of deeds.

Why does recording order matter when a Scotland County house sells?

A deed or lease running more than three years binds lien creditors and later buyers for value only from the time it is registered in the county where the land sits, and priority follows the order of registration (section 47-18).

That makes same-day filing of the buyer's deed and the lender's deed of trust the normal practice. On the seller's side, a payoff should be followed by a recorded satisfaction, which carries no fee. Keep the recorded deed's book and page numbers with your files, and ask the office to correct the index if a number looks wrong.

What should I bring when I contact the Scotland County Register of Deeds?

Staff can prepare records faster when you call before visiting, which the county's own pages recommend. A short checklist keeps the call productive:

  • The owner's name as it appears on the deed, and the book and page if the GIS map gave you one.
  • The street address or parcel, if you are tracing a boundary or easement.
  • For a filing, the original signed instrument with proof of notarization and the preparer's name on page one.
  • A way to pay the recording fee, since fees are due before the paper is filed.

Questions about what a document means or whether it is valid go to an attorney, because the office cannot give legal advice. The staff can still tell you whether a paper meets the recording prerequisites and which index holds it.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

Does the Scotland County office handle marriage licenses and vital records?

Yes. Applicants complete a county form and then call 910-277-2575 to schedule an appointment. The county says a license is not valid until signed by the applicants and by staff in the office, lasts 60 days, and covers marriages in North Carolina only.

Birth and death certificates and marriage licenses can be picked up after a call ahead, or ordered by mail through an online request that the county says it processes the day received.

More questions about Scotland County, NC Register of Deeds

Can I search Scotland County deeds online?

Yes. One index covers 1978 to the present plus all plats, entered by signing in as a guest, and another covers older documents. The GIS map helps when the owner's name is unknown.

What excise tax does a Scotland County deed carry?

The county page prints $2 per $1000, owed by the grantor, matching the state rate of one dollar per $500. Gifts, intestacy and transfers under a will are among the exempt transfers it lists.

Does Scotland County need proof of paid taxes to record a deed?

Yes. Since July 1, 2020, a real property deed needs the tax collector's certificate of no delinquent taxes, or an attorney's statement that back taxes will be paid from closing funds.

Will the Scotland County register of deeds draft my deed?

No. The office is barred from practicing law and cannot help prepare documents. An attorney should draft it and be named on the first page as preparer.

How do I schedule a marriage license in Scotland County?

Fill out the county's form, then call 910-277-2575 for an appointment. The license is good for 60 days and only for marriages held in North Carolina.

Mapping staff verify every parcel change, from new subdivisions to estate files, so a deed for an unusual tract may take a little more time.

What will Albemarle charge to file a deed?

The legislature sets the price, not the county. Ordinary instruments start at $26.00 and cover 15 pages; extra pages are $4.00 each. Loan security instruments start at $64.00 and cover 35 pages. A release of a paid-off loan costs nothing.

  • Plats are $21.00 per sheet.
  • Certified copies are $5.00 for page one and $2.00 after.
  • A badly formatted document picks up a $25.00 surcharge.

Ask which payment types the counter takes before you drive over.

Who covers the deed tax when a Stanly County house sells?

The seller. The rate is one dollar for each $500.00 of price, rounding a remainder up, and the register collects it before filing. The county keeps half and sends half to the state.

Closing attorneys subtract it from proceeds, so it appears as a single line on your settlement statement.

Why does filing order matter on an Albemarle deed?

G.S. 47-18 says a deed, or a lease longer than three years, cannot bind lien creditors or paying buyers until registered where the land sits. The first to file generally ranks first.

  • Obtain a recorded release from your lender after payoff.
  • Match the grantor name on your deed to the prior deed.
  • Keep the stamped first page.

For an inherited house the deed index also shows how title reached the heirs, which helps when paperwork was left unfinished.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Stanly County houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

How does the Stanly tax bill affect a closing?

An unpaid balance holds up the collector's stamp, so the tax position of the parcel comes first. Stanly bills mail in late July or early August, a 1% discount applies to payment before September 1, and the county counts January 5 as the last safe day. After that, interest runs 2% in January, then 0.75% monthly.

The latest reappraisal took effect January 1, 2025, and the county lists the next for January 1, 2029. It also raised its yearly solid waste fee to $99 for 2025. Request a payoff figure from collections before you commit to a closing date.

How can a Stanly County owner challenge a value?

Call 704-986-3631 and ask for an informal review by a certified appraiser, which can raise, lower or keep your value. Still unhappy? File with the five member review board the commissioners appoint; the county says it normally sits in April.

That board starts from the view that the county's number is right, so bring proof: an appraisal dated to the last reappraisal, a broker's market analysis, nearby comparable sales, photos of serious defects, or a sketch if the dimensions on file are wrong. Once the board mails its ruling, you have 30 days to ask the state commission for a hearing.

Which Stanly relief programs could change a seller's figures?

Filing runs January 2 through June 1 at the county tax office. The county prints a $39,900 income ceiling for 2027 applications built on 2026 income.

  • Owners who are older or disabled may exclude $25,000 or half the home's value, whichever is higher.
  • Disabled veterans may exclude the first $45,000.
  • A deferment holds back tax above 4% or 5% of income; postponed amounts for this year and three prior years become a lien due on transfer.

Because a sale triggers repayment, request the payoff in writing.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

What other Stanly County records and permits touch a home sale?

Deed work is only one piece. The mapping office keeps the county base map and ownership data, drawn from deeds and plats filed with the register, and the base maps are built on 2023 color orthophotos. Property search runs through the county GIS site.

If you made repairs or additions before listing, Central Permitting handles building inspections, planning and zoning, and environmental health from one place. Permit requests and inspections now go through an online platform, and the county says no application is processed without a street address. Inside the City of Albemarle, Richfield or Oakboro, the town issues the address, so call the town first.

What zoning and housing rules might matter to a Stanly County owner?

The Planning and Zoning page lists county ordinances for zoning, subdivisions, watershed protection and floodplain management, plus a minimum housing ordinance with a complaint form. It also carries a short term rental application, home occupation permits, rezoning and variance forms, and an abandoned manufactured home program.

  • Planning and Zoning sits at Stanly County Commons, 1000 North First Street, Suite 20, Albemarle, phone 704-986-3660.
  • A free review committee meets on the first and third Wednesdays so owners can talk through a project with several departments before applying.
  • The county's 2040 comprehensive land use plan is posted on the same page.

A buyer planning a rental, a home business or a split of the lot will ask about these, so having the answers ready helps a sale move.

How is Stanly County Tax Administration organized?

In spring 2008 the commissioners merged the old collector and assessor offices into one department with three divisions. Real Property appraises at fair market value as of the latest reappraisal. Personal Property lists, values and audits business and personal items and prepares annual and monthly vehicle bills. The Collector's Division gathers real and personal tax and any other charges the governing body sets.

The county also bills for its municipalities, fire districts and special districts, which is why a single payoff figure from the collector covers more than the county's own levy. Mapping sits apart, at Stanly County Commons, 1000 North First Street, Suite 20, phone 704-986-3637.

Does Stanly County offer present use value for farm and forest land?

Yes. Present use value taxes qualifying land on its productive use. Agriculture needs ten acres in crops or livestock for commercial sale and an average gross income of $1,000 over the prior three years. Horticulture needs five acres with the same income test, and forestry needs twenty acres under a written management plan. Wildlife land must be twenty to one hundred acres under a conservation plan.

All tracts on one application must have identical ownership. Call 704-986-3630 for questions, and ask how a sale changes enrollment before you list rural acreage.

More questions about Stanly County, NC Register of Deeds

Does Albemarle charge more than other North Carolina counties?

No. The base amounts are set by statute for every county: $26.00 covering 15 pages of an ordinary instrument, then $4.00 per extra page.

What has to be stamped on a Stanly County deed first?

The Tax Collector must stamp it "Checked By Tax Collector" after confirming no delinquent tax, using the county's Tax Certification Form.

Who writes the check for the deed tax in Stanly County?

The seller, at the register's counter before recording. The charge is one dollar per $500.00 of price, with any remainder counted as another block.

Where do I request a birth or death certificate copy in Albemarle?

At the Register of Deeds window in the Courthouse, 201 South Second Street. The county lists weekdays from 8:30 until 5.

When does Stanly tax start accruing interest?

January 6. The charge is 2% for that month and 0.75% for every month afterward.

Stokes County by the numbers

How do I reach the Stokes County Register of Deeds?

Walk in at 1014 Main Street, Danbury, ZIP 27016, or write to P.O. Box 67. The listed lines are (336) 593-2414 for the office and (336) 593-9360 for fax.

The recording window closes a quarter hour before the office does, so a deed delivered at ten to five likely waits until the next business day.

What does this office do in a home sale?

The register keeps, indexes and preserves the county's land and vital records. Three filings tend to appear in a Stokes County sale: the seller's deed, the buyer's deed of trust if there is a loan, and the release of the seller's old loan.

Stokes County itself is young compared to its neighbor. It was split off in 1789 from the eastern half of Surry County, which means a title chain for land near the line may run into Surry's books, and those go back to 1771.

Does a Stokes County deed need tax clearance first?

It does. Tax Administration says every deed offered for recording must include its certification that no delinquent tax is owed on the real property being transferred, citing G.S. 161-31.

An unpaid bill therefore holds the deed back. The tax office shares the building and street address, so the errand is short, and it keeps weekday hours of 8:30 to 5:00.

What does a Danbury filing cost?

Statute sets the amounts: $26.00 buys a standard instrument of 15 pages, and each page beyond adds $4.00. A mortgage or deed of trust starts at $64.00 for 35 pages. Filing a loan release is free.

Add $25.00 if a document misses the formatting rules and $10.00 for each extra instrument in one filing. The statute calls the schedule complete and exclusive, due up front. The seller's deed tax is separate and is paid here too.

Why does fast filing help both sides?

North Carolina ranks competing claims by the order of registration. Until a deed is registered where the property sits, it does not defeat lien creditors or paying buyers (G.S. 47-18).

The buyer wants priority. The seller wants a clean break, because claims against the buyer that arise afterward cannot reach back. Keep a copy showing the date and time of filing.

Do installment land contracts get recorded at Danbury?

They should. Chapter 47H reaches deals where the seller holds title to a home of up to four units and the buyer pays at least five installments. Either the contract or a memorandum must be filed within five business days of signing, and the buyer has until midnight of the third business day to cancel.

  • A default notice must leave a cure period of at least 30 days.
  • Late charges stop at 4% and start only after 15 days.

If you sold this way years ago, check that the memorandum is indexed in Danbury.

What can a Stokes County seller do before recording day?

Work through this list with your closing attorney.

  • Confirm the parcel with the county GIS site and the tax website's property record card.
  • Obtain the tax certification from the office down the hall.
  • Work out the deed tax from the sale price using the $1.00 per $500.00 formula.
  • Check that any old mortgage has a recorded release.
  • Arrive before 4:45 on a weekday.

For title questions about an inherited or vacant house, speak with a North Carolina attorney, and call the register about document form.

Which other Stokes County offices share the Danbury address?

The Administration Building at 1014 Main Street houses more than one office a seller will visit. Tax Administration is there, along with Planning and Inspections at (336) 593-2444, and the Finance Department, whose mailing box is P.O. Box 20.

  • Planning and Inspections keeps weekday hours of 8:30 to 5:00 and asks that permit applications arrive by 4:30 in the afternoon to be processed the same day.
  • The Finance Department lists (336) 914-9188.
  • The Register of Deeds uses (336) 593-2414.

One trip to Danbury can therefore cover the tax certification, a permit question and the recording itself.

What planning documents should a Stokes County seller know about?

The planning page links the county's 2035 Vision Plan, titled Moving Together, along with planning board materials for meetings held during 2026. It also notes that a regional transportation organization based in Winston-Salem published a draft 2050 Metropolitan Transportation Plan for public comment through September 15, 2025.

None of that changes how a deed is recorded, but a buyer evaluating a rural parcel may ask what is planned nearby. Planning and Inspections can answer zoning and code enforcement questions at (336) 593-2444.

What changes when the owner has died?

Small estates can skip full administration. Once 30 days have passed, an heir may file an affidavit with the superior court clerk serving the decedent's home county, provided personal property net of liens is under $20,000 (or under $30,000 for a spouse who is the only heir). The affidavit must describe every tract of land owned.

Larger estates take the longer route. Either way, the deed that finally conveys the house is filed in Danbury with the tax certification, so bring the court papers.

What happens to a recorded deed of trust in a foreclosure?

A lender or trustee starts by filing a notice of hearing with the clerk of superior court. The clerk has to find a valid debt, a default and a right to foreclose. An owner can appeal that finding in 10 days by posting a bond of 1% of principal unless the judge lowers it.

After the sale is reported, upset bids must top the last one by 5% or $750 added, whichever is greater, with a deposit. A borrower who sells before the hearing usually keeps more equity, and the payoff ends with a release filed in Danbury.

What does the Stokes County tax calendar mean for a deed?

Stokes bills come due by January 5, with interest from January 6. The tax certification a deed needs reflects what the county's books show owed on the parcel at that moment, so a house sold in autumn, after bills go out, usually has an open current-year balance.

Plan to settle it at the closing table. Tax Administration can quote a figure, and the tax website lists property record cards and land and home values that confirm what the county has on file for your parcel.

Which towns and school system sit behind a Stokes County address?

The county website links to the town sites for Danbury, King and Walnut Cove, and to the Stokes County school system. A buyer comparing houses will often start there, then ask the register's office only about the paper side of the transfer.

Where a house sits matters for permits and utilities, but the deed still records at Danbury whatever town the parcel lies in. Use the county GIS site to confirm which jurisdiction a parcel falls under before you advertise it.

More questions about Stokes County, NC Register of Deeds

What are the Stokes County Register of Deeds recording hours?

The county lists recording from 8:30 to 4:45 on weekdays, with the general office open 8:30 to 5:00.

What is the mailing address for Stokes County deeds?

P.O. Box 67, Danbury, NC 27016. The street address is 1014 Main Street, Danbury.

Does a Stokes deed need tax clearance first?

Yes. Tax Administration must certify that no delinquent tax is owed on the real property before the deed is offered for recording.

Who pays the deed tax in Danbury?

The seller, at the register's window before recording, at one dollar per $500.00 of price with any remainder counted as another block.

Is a loan release free to record in Danbury?

Yes. State law sets no fee for filing a satisfaction or cancellation of a deed of trust.

Which office files deeds for Surry County land?

Send it to the Register of Deeds in Dobson. The office is at 201 East Kapp Street, with P.O. Box 303 for mail, and answers at (336) 401-8150.

Walk-in hours differ by task. Counter service runs from 8:15 am to 5:00 pm, except Tuesday, when doors open at 9:00 am. Real estate filings stop at 4:30 pm, half an hour before closing time, so a late-afternoon courier run can slip to the following day. Faxed real estate paperwork has its own line, (336) 401-8149, distinct from the vital records fax.

The county spans 532.65 square miles of land, home to an estimated 72,287 people in mid-2025. Every parcel in that area is recorded in this one office.

Does Surry County accept electronic recording?

Yes. The register's real estate page names two e-recording companies the office accepts documents from: Simplifile and Corporation Service Company.

Most title companies and closing attorneys already hold an account with one of them, which means a closing can be recorded without anyone driving to Dobson. If you are selling without an attorney, ask the person handling your closing how the deed will be submitted. The county page lists a phone number for Simplifile at (800) 460-5657 and a web address for Corporation Service Company.

  • Electronic submission goes through an approved vendor, not directly through the county website.

What are the filing fees at the Dobson desk?

Fees come from state law and do not vary by county. G.S. 161-10 sets the price of an ordinary instrument by page count and calls its fee list exclusive. Open the statute for the current schedule, and ask the Dobson office about any add-on for an oversized or nonstandard document.

A seller seldom writes this check, because the buyer's closing costs usually absorb recording. Your contract controls that point, so read it before closing day. The table gathers the office details a seller or courier needs.

Who pays the excise tax when a Surry County house sells?

You do, as the seller. The deed stamp tax, found in G.S. 105-228.30, falls on the person transferring title and must reach the register before the deed is filed.

The amount rises with the price, so ask your closer for the exact line on the settlement statement instead of working it out yourself. Receipts are shared between the county and the State. If your acreage straddles a county line, the tax goes to the county holding the larger share of the value.

Why does filing order protect a seller?

Filing is what protects the buyer's title, and your clean exit with it. Under G.S. 47-18, a deed, long lease, option or right of first refusal carries no force against lien creditors or purchasers for value until it is registered, and the earlier filing wins.

So a signing is only half of a closing. Until the clerk stamps the deed into the record, someone with a claim against you could be placed ahead of your buyer. A same-day e-recording avoids the Tuesday late opening and the 4:30 pm cutoff entirely.

Once the deed is filed, request the book and page or instrument number from your title company. You or a future owner can use that reference in the online search.

How far back do the Surry County land records go?

The records start in 1771, the year Surry County was formed from Rowan County. At that time the county covered land that later became Stokes, Forsyth and Yadkin counties.

The register's page describes the early collection as including deeds from agents of Lord Granville, state land grants, sheriff's deeds, mortgages and property divisions. Original books can be viewed or copied through the imaging system, and they also exist on microfilm and in book form. The oldest index covers 1771 to 1870, and a second index runs from 1870 to 1937.

  • The early records include land grants from the state and deeds from agents of Lord Granville.
  • Land that now sits in Stokes, Forsyth or Yadkin may appear in early Surry volumes.
  • Online search and recording standards are linked from the real estate page.

If a title problem surfaces during a sale, a title examiner usually does this research. A seller can still look up the chain of ownership to find a missing release or an old easement.

Can personal information be removed from Surry County records online?

Yes, within limits. The county explains that G.S. 132-1.10(f) allows certain personal identifiers to be redacted from the website copy of a record, and it publishes a redaction request form.

The request must be in writing, signed by the requester or an agent with power of attorney, and must name the information and the document. Items that can be covered include Social Security numbers, driver's license and passport numbers, bank account numbers and card numbers or PINs. Only the website image changes. The official record kept in the deed vault stays as it was recorded.

This is worth knowing if you recorded an old deed that contains a number you would rather not have online. Call (336) 401-8150 before sending a request.

How does Surry County compare with nearby counties for sellers?

QuickFacts puts the owner-occupied median at $177,600 for 2020 to 2024, with $55,656 as median household income. Owners occupy 73.4% of housing units. Housing stock stood at 34,405 units in mid-2025, and builders pulled 244 permits during 2025.

Set beside the other counties on this Census table, Surry sits between Tyrrell at $164,500 and Swain at $207,000, far below Union at $417,300. Because stamp tax tracks price, a Surry sale typically carries a much smaller tax line than a Union County one.

Median gross rent is $761, and adults 65 and over make up 22.9% of the population. Surry also has 90.2% of its population reporting White alone, and 14.1% reporting Hispanic or Latino origin.

What should I bring to a Surry County closing?

Bring identification, the signed deed, and payoff statements for any loan on the property. When a lender is paid off, its release is filed as a cancellation of the deed of trust, and state law charges nothing for that filing.

  • A deed that follows the recording standards linked on the county page.
  • Money or instructions covering the stamp tax.
  • Notarized authority if someone signs for you under a power of attorney.
  • The name of whoever will file the deed, by e-recording or over the counter.

Inherited homes add one step: ask the superior court clerk which estate papers must be on file before a buyer's attorney will accept the deed.

More questions about Surry County, NC Register of Deeds

Where is the Surry County deed office?

It is 201 East Kapp Street, Dobson, NC 27017, with a mailing address of P.O. Box 303 and a main phone of (336) 401-8150. Real estate filings are taken until 4:30 pm on weekdays.

Can my closing company e-record a deed in Surry County?

Yes, through Simplifile or Corporation Service Company, the two vendors the office lists. Ask your closer which one they use.

Which party owes the stamp tax on a Surry County sale?

The seller does. G.S. 105-228.30 puts the deed stamp tax on whoever transfers title, payable ahead of recording.

How much does the register charge to record an ordinary deed?

The schedule is statewide and printed in G.S. 161-10. Ask the Dobson office for the figure that fits your page count.

Does recording a deed change the property tax bill?

No. The bill follows the parcel, not the recording. Settle the current year with your closer and ask the Surry County tax office for the amount.

Who pays the deed stamps in a Swain County sale?

Owing it falls on the seller. Under G.S. 105-228.30, whoever transfers title pays the register first, and only then is the deed recorded.

The amount appears on your settlement statement, and the closer carries it to Bryson City with the deed. It scales with the price, so request the exact number instead of estimating.

How do home values in Swain County look?

Owner-occupied homes in Swain County carry a $207,000 median value in the 2020-2024 QuickFacts survey period. Owners live in 72.7% of them, and the median rent is $742. Housing units numbered 8,951 as of July 2025, and permits totaled 94 for 2025.

QuickFacts also reports that 30.6% of residents identify as American Indian and Alaska Native alone, the highest share among the four counties in the table the Census page compares. If a tract has an unusual ownership history, ask your title company early what it needs to see.

Households earn a median $52,349, and 22.0% of people are past 65. A clean chain of title at the register speeds up any closing.

What vital records and notary help does Swain County offer sellers?

A seller settling an estate often needs a death certificate, and the register issues them. The county lists four ways to ask: upload a photo of your ID on its premium site, email a photo, fax a request, or mail it with a copy of your ID. In person, bring a state ID, driver license, military ID or passport.

Under G.S. 130A-93, as the county summarizes it, those entitled to a certified copy include yourself, a spouse, a sibling, a child or step-child, a parent or step-parent, a grandparent or grandchild, and an authorized agent or attorney with proof. Requesting a record by fraud is a felony under G.S. 130A-26A.

The county tax office, in the same building, offers notary service for cash only, at $8.00 for the first signature, $9.00 for a second signer and $10.00 for more than two. The tax department closes for lunch from 1:30 to 2:00 and shuts at 4:30 pm. Confirm those times before a signing trip.

Can I search Swain County land records online?

Yes. The county provides a remote access site for land records with two modes. The full system lets you search by grantor or grantee name, instrument number, or book and page. The imaging system only retrieves deed book images when you enter a book and page.

The county warns that online records are unofficial and that the official records are kept at the register's office. For a certified copy that a court or lender will accept, ask the office itself.

  • Search by name when you do not know the book and page.
  • Use book and page for a direct image of a known deed.
  • Take any reference from the online index to the counter if you need an official copy.

How does the Swain County tax office tie in with a sale?

The tax office sits in the same Courthouse Building, with a separate mailing address of P.O. Box 2321. It splits into an assessor side, which handles values and reappraisal, and a collections side, which handles payment and enforcement. Phone numbers run through (828) 488-9273.

The county tax page says bills go out in July, fall due September 1, and begin collecting interest after January 5. G.S. 105-360 holds the interest schedule.

Swain County's last reappraisal took effect January 1, 2021, and the county tax page notes an eight-year cycle. The county also says a revaluation contractor has been working in the Alarka community. Call the assessor to learn which year applies to you. The county posts a disabled veteran exclusion form and a property tax relief application on that page.

What should my closer confirm in Swain County?

Confirm three things with your closer: that the deed matches the legal description, that the excise tax amount is on the statement, and that outstanding property tax is settled. A buyer will expect unpaid property tax to be paid off, since G.S. 105-355 makes it a charge against the parcel.

  • Ask whether the buyer's lender needs a payoff letter from a prior mortgage.
  • Ask who will carry the signed deed to the register and by what date.
  • Request the recording book and page once the deed is filed.

If the house came through an estate, start with the court clerk. G.S. 28A-25-1 describes an affidavit route for small estates, and land questions belong with an attorney.

More questions about Swain County, NC Register of Deeds

When can I visit the Swain County deed office?

Come between 8:30 am and 5:00 pm on a weekday to 101 Mitchell Street in Bryson City. License issuing ends 30 minutes earlier.

How do I search Swain County deeds online?

Use the county's remote access site, which offers a full system search by name, instrument number or book and page, plus an imaging-only mode. Those results are unofficial, so use the office for certified copies.

Which party covers the deed stamps in Swain County?

The seller does, ahead of recording, under G.S. 105-228.30. Your closer will show the figure on the statement.

What does a certified vital record copy cost in Swain County?

Certified copies are $10.00 each and uncertified copies $1.00 each, according to the county page. These fees are for birth, death and marriage records, not deed recordings.

When are Swain County property taxes due?

September 1, with interest starting after January 5 per the county. Ask the Courthouse Building tax office for your bill.

Tyrrell County is the least populated of the four counties in a Census comparison used here, with 3,537 residents in mid-2025 across 390.78 square miles of land. That works out to 8.3 people per square mile.

What does the office do?

According to the register's site, the office lets a property owner put the world on notice of an ownership interest. That public record shields later parties from unknown transactions and hidden liens.

The filing cabinet there ranges from old land grants to modern deeds, maps, leases and agreements. The same counter hands out vital certificates and marriage licenses.

A Fraud Alert Notification Service is advertised on the site. Registering an email address brings an automatic message whenever a recording looks possibly fraudulent. The seller does. The statute names the person transferring title as the one who settles the tax at the register's office, ahead of recording.

The excise tax statute sets a flat charge per $500 block of price or value, with leftovers counted as a full block. The county and the State share what comes in.

Why does recording matter after I sell a Tyrrell County house?

G.S. 47-18 withholds protection from an unregistered deed against creditors and later buyers who gave value. The deed that reaches the county office first usually ranks ahead.

If your deed is not recorded, a creditor with a claim against you, or a second buyer, could end up ahead of the purchaser. The practical answer is to make sure the deed is on its way to Columbia on closing day, whether through your closer or by your own delivery.

  • Ask when the recording will happen and how it will be submitted.
  • Keep proof of delivery if you mail the deed to P.O. Box 449.
  • Request the recording information once the register has filed it.

How are Tyrrell County property taxes paid and handled at a sale?

Interest rules sit in G.S. 105-360, and G.S. 105-355 explains the lien that follows the parcel.

Tyrrell County's payment page offers six routes: web portal, phone, mail, the tax office counter, a drop box inside the hallway before the tax department door, and a bank's bill pay. It says card payments carry either a $2.50 or a 2.95% service fee, whichever is greater, and e-check payments an added $2.00 fee. A bank's bill pay can lag by as much as seven business days, so begin early.

For the current bill, tax rate and any prepayment discount, ask the Tyrrell County tax office.

Can an heir sell a Tyrrell County house without a full estate?

Sometimes. G.S. 28A-25-1 allows an affidavit for small estates, with caps of $20,000 in personal property after liens and $30,000 for a sole-heir surviving spouse after any spousal allowance, if no personal representative petition is pending and 30 days have passed since death.

File it with the superior court clerk where the person lived. The statute has the affidavit describe every tract of land the person owned. The seller, before recording. Look for the figure on the settlement statement.

Most sellers skip the mail and let the closing firm file electronically.

Does filing order change who wins a dispute?

Under G.S. 47-18, a conveyance has no force against lien creditors or purchasers for value before it is registered, and rank follows registration time.

No. Staff cannot advise on drafting, so the attorney who prepared the deed has to correct it.

A seller with a Raleigh-area house rarely goes in person. Your closing firm files the deed, which is the step that publishes the sale.

How much does Wake County charge to record a deed?

On the register's schedule, an ordinary deed starts at $26 and a deed of trust at $64, with $4 for each page past the included count.

What counts as a standard deed in Wake County?

Missing any single item on the register's standard-document list triggers the $25 surcharge, and the list covers layout only.

  • Paper sized 8.5 by 11 or 8.5 by 14 inches.
  • Three blank inches at the top of the first page, with half-inch margins everywhere else.

  • One side only, with the instrument type centered on page one.

Pen is acceptable for filling blanks and making corrections. Documents from a title firm pass as a matter of course. A form downloaded and printed double-sided, or a scan that crowds the edge, is the sort of file that draws the extra $25.

How is the Wake County deed transfer tax stated?

The fee page lists $2 per thousand for deeds since August 1, 1991, and the help page for changing names on a deed mentions the same excise tax on a purchase price.

State law words it as a dollar per $500 and makes the transferor pay first, so the seller sees it at settlement. Ask the closing office for the number on your deed.

The fee page also lists $1 per thousand for 1969 to July 1991 and $1.10 per thousand before 1969, which matter when reading an old transfer.

What can you search through the Wake County register's index?

The county says its public records start in 1785, and the Consolidated Real Property Index lets a seller or a buyer's lawyer follow title from a desk.

Start with your own deed and compare its legal description and owner names against the contract. Next, look for the deed of trust you are paying off, and after closing look for its satisfaction, which the fee page lists at no charge.

How does the register connect to Wake County tax records?

The tax help line is 919-856-5400. Wake also bills towns and special districts, so one bill can carry several charges. The county's bill page reports 53.71 cents after a 2-cent increase adopted for Fiscal Year 2027.

Values reset on January 1, 2027, the effective date of the county's next revaluation, which sorts about 460,000 parcels into 5,400 neighborhoods.

What should a Wake County seller line up with the register and the tax office?

None of this needs a trip downtown if a closing firm is involved.

  • Your recorded deed, pulled from the online index.
  • The payoff letter for any deed of trust, followed by a recorded release at no charge.
  • A tax figure from Tax Administration, which matters most for owners who pay by escrow and never see a bill.
  • A deed laid out to the standard list.

Heirs unsure what is recorded can search the index, then phone 919-856-5460. The register suggests an attorney for questions about the deed itself.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

Which Wake County register services help heirs selling an inherited house?

The register sells certified death certificates, which heirs often need for estate paperwork. The fee page lists $10 per certified copy, with a $10 amendment charge, and for out-of-county death certificates a $14 search fee, a $10 certified copy and $15 for each additional copy. Ordering online adds a county charge of $10 per copy plus a vendor convenience fee that varies.

The same fee page lists copies of recorded documents. A certified copy of a document is $5 for page one and $2 for each page after, and the county does not charge for its trailer page. A certified copy of a map is $5.

  • Get a certified deed copy to show how the decedent held title.
  • Check the index for any open deed of trust before listing the house.
  • Ask an attorney whether probate steps must come before a deed is recorded.

The register does not decide who may sign a deed for an estate. That question belongs to the probate side and to your attorney.

Does Wake County record anything besides deeds that affects a house?

Yes. The fee page lists plats and condominium maps at $21 per page, right-of-way plans and highway maps at $21 for the first page and $5 for each page after, and UCC filings at $38 each for the UCC-1 and UCC-3, rising to $45 above two pages. The county's example prices a 13-page UCC filing at $51.

For a seller, the useful items are the maps and restrictive covenants, since both can describe limits on the parcel. The register's description says restrictive covenants and survey maps are recorded here, and its index reaches back to 1785. Ask your title or closing firm to pull any plat and covenant that applies to your subdivision.

Business owners operating from home may also file an assumed name here, which the fee page places at the $26 instrument rate.

Does the Wake County register take e-recording?

Ask the office or your closing firm how a deed will be sent and what cutoff applies. Paper goes to the Justice Center on weekdays.

For any question tied to a particular filing, call 919-856-5460 before you go.

Why does recording matter after a Wake County sale?

Until a conveyance is registered in the county where the land lies, it carries no weight against lien creditors or purchasers for value. For a Raleigh-area house, that makes the filing the buyer's protection.

File the stamped copy with your closing papers and confirm the old lender's release is recorded.

More questions about Wake County, NC Register of Deeds

Is the Wake County deed office open on Saturdays?

No. The Justice Center office keeps weekday hours only. Call 919-856-5460 about holidays.

How is Wake County's deed excise tax stated?

The county lists it as $2 per thousand on deeds since August 1, 1991; the transferor pays.

Does Wake County charge to record a payoff release?

No. Satisfactions, affidavits of satisfaction and trustee's satisfactions are listed as free.

How do I change the names on a Wake County deed?

With a new deed. The register suggests an attorney unless you are used to preparing legal papers.

How far back do Wake County deeds go online?

To 1785, per the county.

Where in Warrenton is the deeds counter?

The counter is on South Main Street at number 109. The register's site lists Monday to Friday service from 8:30 to 5, a phone at (252) 257-3265, and a post office box, number 506, with the 27589 ZIP. The job is filled at the ballot box every second year, per G.S. 161-1 provides.

Warren County was created in 1779 and carries the name of a doctor who died at Bunker Hill, the county manager's page explains. Some 20,000 people share its 443 square miles of fields, and five commissioners hold the board seats. One counter covers all of it, so a quick call can save a drive.

Anyone may read what the office holds. Lookups run on names, so a person hunting for a parcel's owner should have one; with only a street address, the FAQ redirects to the tax office at (252) 257-4158.

What does recording a deed in Warren County accomplish?

Recording shields the buyer. Under G.S. 47-18, an unrecorded transfer, or a lease longer than three years, cannot beat a lien creditor or a paying purchaser. Whoever registers first stands first.

By its own account the office exists so owners can publish their interest in real estate. It also files births that happened in Warren County, marriage licenses and notary oaths, and it files DD-214 papers for retired service members at no cost.

  • The land side takes deeds, mortgages, releases, plats and powers of attorney.
  • Wills live elsewhere, with the courthouse clerk.
  • Liens and judgments: the FAQ gives the clerk's number, (252) 257-6300.

What does filing a Warren County deed cost?

Warren County follows G.S. 161-10. Twenty-six dollars buys the first fifteen pages of an ordinary deed and every page after costs four. A mortgage or deed of trust starts at sixty-four dollars for thirty-five pages, with the same four-dollar overage. Filing a release costs nothing.

What each Warren County filing costs, per the named source
ItemPrinted amountSource
Ordinary deed$26 plus $4 per page beyond 15G.S. 161-10

DD-214 filingNoneRegister's home page

The county's own fee page and FAQ were written years ago and show other per-page and mortgage numbers than the statute does. Call before mailing a package, and use the statute figures as your starting point.

Who pays the deed stamp in Warren County?

Sellers pay. For each $500 of value, or any leftover part of $500, the stamp is one dollar, handed to the register before the deed is entered.

The county keeps half for its general fund, and the rest travels to the state monthly, less a small allowance (statute). The old office FAQ restates the rate as $2 per $1,000. The settlement statement shows the exact stamp.

What should a Warren County seller line up first?

Three items come first: matching names, a current tax account and a document that fits the office's format. The register's website carries a recording checklist and a fee page, and staff answer by phone.

  • Changing who is named takes a fresh deed. The office recommends an attorney, then the normal filing fee, plus stamp tax where a price is involved.
  • Check the tax account. Each bill is due on September 1 and starts drawing interest after January 5, per G.S. 105-360.
  • Ask the clerk if a lien or judgment sits on the file.
  • Pay with cash, check or money order, since the FAQ rules out cards.

Two short calls, one to each office, before listing.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Warren County houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

How does rural Warren County shape a sale?

Farm tracts and family land come up often in a county of this size, and such sales may add a survey, plat or easement, each filed separately. A plat is $21 a sheet by statute. Splitting acreage? Learn the register's plat format before the surveyor starts.

In the FAQ, a copy of a recorded map is five cents a page (fifty for large maps) and a deed copy is also five cents. The online search shows scanned deeds. Tax maps, parcel numbers and aerial photos come from tax mapping, not here.

Heirs who want to sell should see whether a deed was ever recorded in their names; estate papers may start at the clerk.

How far back do Warren County genealogy and vital records reach?

The county's genealogy page gives a short timeline for what the register keeps. Birth and death certificates run from 1914 to the present. Delayed birth certificates reach back to the late 1800s. Marriage indexes begin in 1867, and marriage bonds and licenses go back to the late 1800s.

  • Certificates, bonds and licenses are filed only for events that took place in Warren County.
  • NC Vital Records in Raleigh holds records for every county in the state and is the place to ask about events elsewhere.
  • Wills are not here. The page says the Warren County clerk of court maintains them.

Heirs selling a Warren County house will find the register useful for the marriage and death side of the family story, while the will itself sits with the clerk.

NC Vital Records lists its Raleigh phone line as 919.733.3526 on the county page. If an owner died in another county, the record will not be in Warren County's files, so ask the state office or the county where the death happened.

What non-land business does the Warren County office do?

Many visitors come for other reasons. A marriage license costs sixty dollars, lasts sixty days and is booked by phone. A certified marriage certificate is ten dollars and can be had once ten days have passed since the ceremony.

A certified vital record goes only to a short list: the person named, a spouse, parents, siblings, children, grandparents, a legal representative, or someone with proof of a legal need. Plain copies are open to all.

New notaries swear in at the counter without an appointment, bringing the notice from the Secretary of State, for a $10 fee per the FAQ. Births outside the county are recorded by NC Vital Records.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

Can a Warren County house with liens or repairs still sell?

Yes. Liens and back taxes come out of the price at closing and the releases get recorded. A tired house can find a buyer willing to take it as it stands.

Start the title work early so both the register's index and the clerk's judgments are checked. For a cash number on a Warren County house to set beside a listing, ask this site.

Where can a Warren County owner look up or pay a tax bill?

The county's property page for the register of deeds links to a combined tool for paying tax bills and searching property record cards. It is a county web page, so the register's staff still direct questions about assessments to the tax office at the number in the FAQ.

Keep the bill and the recorded deed together. When a closing is scheduled, the person handling it will want the account number and the book and page of the last recorded deed, and both come from those two lookups.

More questions about Warren County, NC Register of Deeds

Is releasing a Warren County mortgage free?

Yes, no fee applies to recording a satisfaction of a mortgage or deed of trust, under the state schedule.

Can Warren County staff name a parcel's owner from an address?

No. Staff search by name only, so address-only callers are sent to the tax office.

Does the Warren County deeds office file wills?

No. The clerk of superior court takes wills and estates. The register takes deeds, mortgages, plats, releases, marriage licenses and notary oaths.

Does Warren County charge to record a DD-214?

No, the office files discharge papers for retired military free.

Who answers deed questions in Warren County?

Phone (252) 257-3265, Monday to Friday, 8:30 to 5. The office is at 109 South Main Street, Warrenton.

Where does Washington County keep its deed records?

At 120 Adams Street in Plymouth, mail to Box 1007 with the 27962 ZIP. The county page gives office hours of 8:30 to 5 on weekdays, phone (252) 793-2325 and fax (252) 793-6982.

Voters fill the register's seat for a four-year term, the county says. The office exists so that owners can put their interest in land on public notice, which in turn shields later buyers from unknown transactions and secret liens. It also issues birth, death and marriage certificates and marriage licenses.

Washington County sits in the northeast of the state. By the county's description, US 64 cuts through it, Raleigh is about 120 miles west, Nags Head about 80 miles east and Greenville under 50 miles away. Plymouth, Roper and Creswell are its towns, and the Albemarle Sound shore is at Roper.

How old are the land records in Plymouth?

The oldest go back to 1799, the year Washington County was carved out of Tyrrell County. Marriage records start in 1851 and the licenses themselves in 1881.

The shelves hold old land grants, deeds, deeds of trust, maps, leases, agreements and powers of attorney. Anyone selling farmland or shoreline here should expect a long chain of title, and a title searcher will walk it back through those early books. A link on the county page opens deeds online.

North Carolina began statewide birth and death registration in 1913. Some earlier births appear in the county's files as delayed registrations filed by the person later. Older vital record requests should be in writing, with names and dates.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Washington County house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

What steps come before a Washington County deed can be filed?

Two local checkpoints apply. First, every deed passes through the GIS (mapping) office to receive a parcel identifier number. Second, the county tax collector must certify that no delinquent taxes exist, or the deed itself must carry a statement from the closing lawyer promising to send any back taxes to the collector out of the closing funds. The statement route is the usual one.

  • Name the person who prepared the deed on page one.
  • Choose letter or legal size paper, with a three-inch blank band across the top of the first page and quarter-inch margins on the remaining edges.
  • Print in black on white, nothing smaller than nine point, on one side only.
  • Label the type of instrument at the top of page one.

A paper that misses those standards is still accepted, but the register adds a $25 non-standard charge to the normal fee. The county also mentions that cancellations and satisfactions can be sent through Simplifile.

What does it cost to file in Washington County?

The county prints the uniform schedule from G.S. 161-10. An ordinary deed starts at twenty-six dollars, which covers fifteen pages, with four dollars for each page beyond. A deed of trust starts at sixty-four dollars for thirty-five pages and takes the same four-dollar surcharge per added page.

Charges printed on the Washington County register page
FilingCharge
Ordinary deed$26, plus $4 per page past 15
Indexing over twenty names$2 per extra name
Deed of trust$64, plus $4 per page past 35
Extra reference on an assignment$10 each
Map, sized 18 by 24$21
Cancellation or satisfactionFree
Stamp tax$1 per $500 or part
Certified vital record$10

Maps are routed through GIS for a parcel number and through the county review officer for approval, unless the map carries one of three stock statements: no new street, an existing building or natural feature, or a control survey.

Who covers the stamp tax on a Plymouth-area sale?

The person transferring the property. The register collects it before the deed goes on record, at one dollar per $500 or fraction of the price or value.

The county reproduces the same rate on its page, and G.S. 105-228.30 divides the money between county and state. The settlement statement will show the stamp, so no one has to calculate it in advance. If a deed has no ordinary sale price, ask the register how the stamp applies before you bring it in.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Washington County houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Does the Washington County office file contracts for deed?

It files any instrument touching land, and seller financing is a common case. Under Chapter 47H, a contract for deed on a one to four family home must be written, signed and acknowledged, and the seller has five business days to record the contract or a memorandum of it.

The buyer may cancel until midnight on the third business day. If the seller later seeks forfeiture, the written default notice must give a cure date at least thirty days after service.

Other things a Washington County seller may bring to the counter:

  • A power of attorney, if someone signs the deed for the owner.
  • A map or plat in the 18 by 24 format, after GIS review.
  • A lease or agreement, both listed among the county's record types.

Because the preparer must be named on page one, line up whoever drafts the deed before you go.

What else brings Plymouth residents to the register?

Marriage licenses are a regular errand. Any North Carolina register will issue one, and the ceremony can be held in any county, but the signed license must come back to the county that sold it. Each applicant needs a driver's license and a Social Security card, or a W-2, pay stub, insurance card or Social Security printout as proof of the number. Blood tests and physicals are no longer required.

Applicants aged 16 to 17 bring a certified birth certificate, and anyone under 18 needs a parent or guardian's consent. Those under 16 must call the office first.

Vital record copies follow a tight rule: certified ones go only to the applicant or immediate family, and in-person requests need identification. The same counter that handles those errands is the one that files your deed, so allow time on busy days.

Why does filing order matter in Washington County?

Because the earliest registration wins. G.S. 47-18 says a conveyance has no force against lien creditors or purchasers for value until registered in the county where the land lies.

  • For a deed naming more than twenty parties, call (252) 793-2325 first.
  • Ask the tax collector about open bills, since the deed needs the certification or the lawyer's statement.
  • Check whether an old loan still lacks a recorded satisfaction.

Shoreline and farm parcels often carry surveys, and any plat that comes with the sale follows the map rules above.

Can a Washington County house with title or tax problems still sell?

Yes. A closing lawyer clears unpaid taxes and liens from the price, and a buyer can take the house in its present condition. Searching the register's index is the first move for any title searcher.

To weigh a cash offer on a Washington County house against a listing, you can request a written offer on this site.

More questions about Washington County, NC Register of Deeds

Does Washington County charge to record a satisfaction?

No. The county lists cancellations and certificates of satisfaction as free, and the non-standard document fee never applies to a cancellation.

Is a parcel number needed before a Washington County deed is filed?

Yes. The county sends every deed to GIS first so a parcel identifier number can be assigned.

What does a certified birth, death or marriage copy cost in Washington County?

The county prints ten dollars for certified and twenty-five cents for uncertified. Certified copies go only to the applicant or immediate family, and faxed requests are refused.

How long does a Washington County marriage license last?

Sixty days, at a cost of sixty dollars. The county asks applicants to arrive before 4:30 p.m. because the visit takes fifteen to twenty minutes.

Whom do I phone about filing a Washington County deed?

The register of deeds at (252) 793-2325. The office is at 120 Adams Street in Plymouth, open weekdays from 8:30 to 5.

Fees

Watauga County by the numbers

Where in Boone is the Watauga County deeds office?

Inside the courthouse, Room 119, at 842 West King Street. Mail goes to the same street, Suite 9, Boone, NC 28607. The county contact page gives 828-265-8052 for land records, 828-265-8034 for vital records and 828-265-7632 for fax.

Watauga County lies in the Blue Ridge Mountains of northwestern North Carolina. It was cut from parts of Ashe, Caldwell, Wilkes and Yancey in 1849 and takes its name from the Watauga River. Boone, the seat, is home to Appalachian State University, and the Blue Ridge Parkway crosses the county.

Voters elect the register, per G.S. 161-1. Wills are filed with the clerk of court, and the county says liens and judgments on real property are checked with the clerk of superior court.

What can be searched in the Watauga County land records?

The website carries indexes and images from 1872 forward, searchable by name or by book and page. Anything recorded before February 22, 1985 lives under the old index books tab, because on that date deeds and deeds of trust were folded into one series, the Book of Records, restarting at Book 1.

Plats can be searched by book and page, subdivision, or the owner as grantor, no matter when they were recorded. North Carolina's indexing standards began in 1995, and the office keeps copies.

Nearly everything filed is public. The county names one exception: military discharges on file under 80 years. For the owner of a given parcel, the FAQ sends you to tax mapping at 828-265-8030.

The county's tax mapping department, not the register, answers parcel ownership questions. That split is typical in North Carolina: the register's index runs on names and recorded documents, while tax mapping runs on parcels and maps. Keep both numbers handy when you prepare a sale, and bring the book and page of your deed to either call.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Watauga County house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

What does the Watauga County fee page list?

The county's schedule, marked as revised October 1, 2016, tracks G.S. 161-10. A deed opens at twenty-six dollars for fifteen pages; a deed of trust opens at sixty-four dollars for thirty-five. Each added page is four dollars in both cases.

Selected lines from the Watauga County register fee page
Line itemAs printed
Deeds and instruments$26.00, then $4.00 a page after 15
Mortgages and deeds of trust$64.00, then $4.00 a page after 35
Records of satisfactionNo fee
Non-standard document$25.00 on top of the filing fee
Parties beyond twenty$2.00 each
Multiple instruments$10.00 per extra instrument
Plats$21.00 a sheet
Excise stamps$1.00 per $500.00 or fraction

A 1983 commissioner ordinance, noted on the page, requires plats offered for registration to measure 18 by 24 inches. Records supplied to help someone claim veterans' benefits are free.

Fees apply per instrument, so a closing that records a deed and a new deed of trust is billed on two lines. Releases of an old loan add nothing. The county page also notes that the schedule is posted for the public to read, so you can compare it with your closing statement.

Does Watauga County accept electronic recording?

Yes, for all land record document types. The county says more than 1,500 submitters, such as banks, law offices and mortgage companies, already send documents this way.

Three vendors are named:

  • Simplifile, 1-800-460-5657.
  • Corporation Service Company, 1-866-652-0111.
  • eRecording Partners Network, 1-888-325-3365.

Most home sales arrive electronically through the lawyer handling the closing, so sellers seldom carry paper in. Deeds, deeds of trust, satisfactions, easements and powers of attorney are all on the county's list of electronic filings.

What will the Watauga County register's staff not do for a seller?

Staff can point you to the right book and tell you whether a document is a real estate record or a vital record, but the county says they cannot run a title search, offer a legal opinion, or change a deed already recorded. Adding or deleting a name would count as practicing law, so that job goes to an attorney.

Address searches are also off the table. This office indexes documents by legal description, with boundary, lot, block and acreage details, so a street address has to go to the Tax Mapping Department at (828) 265-8030.

  • A lost deed is replaceable: a copy can be certified with the office seal, because the recording matters more than the paper.
  • Copies cost five cents a page, and a recorded subdivision plat copy is one dollar.
  • If no money changes hands, no excise stamp applies.
  • A person with private data in online records can ask in writing, at no charge, for it to be removed from the online copy under the Identity Theft Protection Act of 2005.

The office is open weekdays from 8:00 to 5:00 except holidays, and marriage licenses are by appointment, with applicants in the door by 4:30.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Watauga County houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Who covers the excise stamp on a Boone-area deed?

The seller. The stamp is a dollar for each $500 or fraction of the consideration, paid to the register before the instrument is entered. The county gets half and the Department of Revenue gets half, per G.S. 105-228.30.

The settlement statement carries the final amount. North Carolina also repealed its estate tax for deaths on or after January 1, 2013, so an inherited Watauga County house adds no estate tax step before recording.

What else does the Watauga County register's office provide?

Besides land, the fee page lists marriage licenses at $60 and certified birth, death and marriage copies at $10. Notary oaths are $10, with $2 for verifying a commission. Military discharge records are kept, and a certified copy of an armed forces discharge costs nothing.

The county menu also lists an assumed business name certificate, a redaction request form, a fraud notification system and an identity theft page. Because deeds and deeds of trust are public, the fraud notice and the redaction form are the two a homeowner is most likely to use.

  • Uncertified copies cost whatever is posted at the office.
  • Comparing a copy for certification is $5.00.
  • For birth and death certificates, call 828-265-8034.

Must a Watauga County deed be recorded, and can I write my own?

The county says to record soon after drafting, since an unrecorded deed can make a later sale or mortgage impossible to prove. The law backs it up: G.S. 47-18 denies a conveyance force against lien creditors and paying purchasers until it is registered where the land lies.

An owner may write a deed, the county notes, though an attorney is strongly advised. Adding or removing a name takes a new deed, and the register has no blank forms.

A search of the index shows how the present owner took title, which matters when property passed through heirs or a trust.

What if a Watauga County title has loose ends?

Begin with the index. Look up the owner, note the book and page of the last deed, and watch for old deeds of trust with no recorded release. Releases cost nothing to file.

Next, phone the clerk of superior court about liens and judgments and the tax office about the account. A house with flaws can still sell as it is. If you want a cash offer to compare with listing, you can request one on this site.

More questions about Watauga County, NC Register of Deeds

Where is the Watauga County Register of Deeds?

In the courthouse, Room 119, 842 West King Street, Boone. Dial 828-265-8052 for land records and 828-265-8034 for vital records.

How far back do the online land records in Watauga County go?

To 1872. Anything recorded before February 22, 1985 is under the old index books tab.

Does Watauga County charge to file a release of a deed of trust?

No. The county's fee page lists records of satisfaction at no fee.

Does the Watauga County register keep wills?

No. Wills go to the clerk of courts. Separation agreements can come from the register, while divorces are filed with the clerk.

Can a Watauga County deed be recorded online?

Yes, through Simplifile, Corporation Service Company or eRecording Partners Network. Most sellers let the closing lawyer handle it.

Where do I take a deed in Wayne County?

The Register of Deeds works from 224-226 E Walnut Street, Suite 100, in Goldsboro (ZIP 27533), phone 919-731-1449. The fax line is 919-731-1441, and the office's own web page gives 8:00 to 5:00 as general hours.

Real estate filings are taken from 8:00 to 4:45 with no appointment. Staff ask that nothing be walked in later than 4:45 p.m., so a closing that runs into the evening is better sent by wire or electronic filing.

If a funeral home or an heir needs paperwork rather than land records, the page lists a fax number, 919-731-1441, and an email option. Land and vital records share the building, but each service has its own window hours, so call 919-731-1449 before driving over with a time sensitive filing.

What is kept at the Wayne County Register of Deeds?

The office is the custodian of county land and business records: deeds, deeds of trust, satisfactions and cancellations, powers of attorney, assumed business names and separation agreements. Marriage licenses, notary commissions and DD-214 discharge recordings come from the same counter.

The archive reaches back to 1913. The online index covers most real estate papers from 1971 onward, so an older tract usually means a visit.

Funeral homes have their own routine: email registerofdeeds@waynegov.com, or drop off a request in person, and staff call when the order is ready. Wills are not accepted here. The page sends people to the Clerk of Courts at 919-722-6100.
