Is the office only a filing counter?

Yes. It records what is handed over, and North Carolina law keeps its staff from practicing law. They will not draft a deed, explain a form's effect or help fill in blanks.

So most Wayne County sales run through a lawyer or title firm that prepares the deed, searches title, gathers the tax and delivers the filing.

Owners selling without an agent can still use an attorney only for the paper work. Ask whether the attorney will handle the recording, and who pays the fees.

A seller who plans to skip a lawyer should still call the office first and ask what the counter will and will not check. Staff can say whether a packet arrived in the right form to file, though they will not say whether the document does what you want.

Can a closing office eRecord in Wayne County?

Yes. Wayne County takes every document type by eRecording, and the eRecording page says plats can now be submitted this way. The office lists approved vendors that firms must choose from first.

The vendor helps the firm complete a submitter agreement. Within two business days of processing, the Register of Deeds emails an identification number, which every electronic filing needs.

  • Choose an authorized vendor
  • Complete the submitter agreement
  • Receive the ID number by email
  • Submit deeds and deeds of trust electronically

Vendors must hold approval under G.S. 47-14(a1), says the county page. Individual sellers rarely sign up, since their title company does.

What does recording cost in Wayne County?

Recording charges from G.S. 161-10, collected by the Wayne County office

How does the seller's transfer tax work in Wayne County?

The seller owes the state deed excise tax, paid at the Goldsboro counter ahead of recording, at one dollar for each five hundred dollars (or part) of value conveyed (G.S. 105-228.30).

The settlement statement lists it. Check the figure against your contract, and ask about gifts or below market transfers.

Why record a Wayne County deed right after closing?

A deed left unregistered gives the buyer no shield from lien creditors or later purchasers for value (G.S. 47-18). Earlier registration wins.

A seller can help by clearing old liens beforehand. A paid off mortgage with no recorded satisfaction clouds the title, and lenders file releases at no charge.

  • Search the grantor index for open deeds of trust
  • Request a satisfaction from any lender you paid off
  • Confirm the legal description matches your own vesting deed

How can a Wayne County seller check the title before listing?

Run three checks before you sign a listing or an offer. They take little time and prevent most closing surprises.

  • Search the online index, which covers most real estate documents from 1971, for your name as grantee and grantor.
  • Look for deeds of trust with no matching satisfaction.
  • Match your own vesting deed against the parcel shown in the county's real estate search on the tax site.

For anything before 1971, go to the Goldsboro office and ask staff how the older books are indexed. Staff can show you where records are kept, though they cannot interpret them for you.

If a plat is involved, the office tells people to check with the Planning Department about plats and signatures before presenting them.

What should be in a Wayne County recording packet?

Your closing attorney normally assembles it, so the list below is a way to check their work rather than a task for you.

  • The signed and notarized deed, with a legal description that matches the prior deed
  • A check or account for the recording charge
  • The excise tax payment, collected on the seller's side
  • A deed of trust for the buyer's lender, recorded after the deed
  • Any satisfactions for loans paid at closing

Documents arriving by eRecording follow the same order, and the vendor's system carries the fee and tax figures. If something is rejected, the office phone is 919-731-1449.

Which other Goldsboro offices touch a Wayne County sale?

Three county offices matter. The Register of Deeds records the paper. The Tax Collector, at P.O. Box 1495, supplies the tax payoff. The Clerk of Courts, at 919-722-6100, holds wills for an estate sale.

If the house belongs to an estate, call the clerk and an attorney before looking for a buyer, because the right person to sign the deed depends on what the court has done. The register of deeds will record the deed once it is signed and acknowledged, but cannot tell you whether the signer has authority.

Marriage licenses and vital records are handled at the same Walnut Street counter, which sometimes helps an heir who needs a death certificate to complete an estate file. Funeral homes are served by email.

How do Wayne County housing numbers show up in these records?

Census QuickFacts counts 9,996 veterans in the county, so discharge recordings and veteran relief claims are routine, see Census QuickFacts. Median gross rent was $965 for 2020-2024, which shapes what a landlord seller can expect from a rental.

Owners tend to stay put, so a Wayne County house may carry decades of deed history, and a buyer's title search reads all of it. An old loan that was never released is a common loose end.

If the owner has died, the register of deeds holds the recorded chain, and the estate's attorney works from the clerk of court for the will.

More questions about Wayne County, NC Register of Deeds

Until what hour are real estate filings taken in Wayne County?

4:45 p.m. The office asks people not to bring recording packages after that time, and general hours are 8:00 to 5:00.

Will Wayne County staff draft my deed?

No. Staff may not practice law, so they cannot draft a deed or explain its effect. Hire an attorney or use a closing office.

How far back are Wayne County real estate records online?

Most real estate records are searchable from 1971 forward, while the archive itself goes back to 1913.

Is recording a loan release free in Wayne County?

Yes. State law sets no fee to record a satisfaction or cancellation of a mortgage or deed of trust.

Which Wayne County office takes a will?

To the Clerk of Courts, which the Register of Deeds page lists at 919-722-6100.

What are the address and hours of the Wilkes County Register of Deeds?

How old are Wilkes County land records?

They begin with the formation of the county in 1778. Birth and death records start in 1913, with a few earlier delayed birth entries, and marriage licenses go back to 1882.

The register lists deeds, deeds of trust, powers of attorney, assumed names, plats, separation agreements, foreclosures, notary oaths and military discharges among the papers it takes in. Digitizing is ongoing, so ask the office how far back a given book is indexed.

For a parcel with deep family ownership, older deeds can describe land by landmarks instead of lot numbers. A survey tied to the current deed saves arguments with a buyer's title examiner.

Heirs sorting an estate often start here, since births, deaths and marriages are on file alongside land records. A short visit with the death certificate and the last recorded deed can show who held title and whether a loan was ever released.

Where can I search Wilkes County deeds online?

At wilkesncrod.org, which the register of deeds opened on July 1, 2017. That is the authoritative site for recorded documents.

The tax office runs a second, narrower tool. Its Deed Search holds face pages and legal descriptions of certain deeds that the tax office scanned for its mapping staff. Signature and notary pages are usually left off, and deeds of trust, satisfactions and wills are not included.

The disclaimer tells attorneys and title examiners not to rely on it. Treat it as a quick way to find a legal description by book and page, and use the register for the real record.

The tax office tool works by book and page. Once you have those numbers from a prior deed or from the register's own site, you can pull the scanned face page and compare its legal description with your survey. Keep a printout for your attorney.

What are the Wilkes County recording charges?

Recording charges under G.S. 161-10, as collected in Wilkes County

A deed that is not registered loses to lien creditors and later buyers who paid value, and priority follows the time of registration (G.S. 47-18). Lawyers therefore record on the day funds move.

  • Get the tax balance from North Street
  • Bring the excise tax with the deed
  • Record the deed ahead of the buyer's loan

The register is elected by county voters (G.S. 161-1).

What if a Wilkes County tract has boundary questions?

State law lets a person gain title by 20 years of possession under known and visible lines and boundaries, adverse to others (G.S. 1-40). On older rural tracts, fences and farm roads may sit off the deed line.

Before listing, pull the vesting deed from the register, order a survey if lines are unclear, and tell your attorney about any neighbor who uses part of the land. A buyer's examiner will find recorded claims, so surprises cost more late.

How should a Wilkes County owner prepare before closing day?

Work backward from the recording desk. The register closes at 4:55 p.m., so a closing that wraps up at four leaves little room for a corrected page.

The county estimated that real property values rose about 75% to 80% overall as of January 1, 2025, with ranges that varied from town to town, in its revaluation release.

For recording, the price in the contract is what matters for the excise tax. The tax value does not set it. If your contract price and the county's value differ widely, your attorney can explain why before the deed is drafted.

The release also says the county reappraises more often than the eight year minimum. Check with the tax office for the schedule.

Where should a Wilkes County seller go for each document?

  • Deeds, deeds of trust, plats, powers of attorney, foreclosure papers: Register of Deeds, Court House Drive
  • Tax balances, appeals, relief applications, parcel and GIS look-ups: Tax Administration, North Street

The deed search page itself points to the register and the clerk of superior court for any authoritative use of land records. Keep the three straight and a sale usually moves without a second visit.

What other Wilkesboro records come up in a sale?

Besides deeds, the register takes foreclosure papers and powers of attorney, which matter when an owner signs by proxy or the lender has begun sale proceedings. The county also lets people look up parcels through the tax office's real property search and GIS maps.

If you want to confirm who is on the tax record, search the parcel there, then match it to the recorded deed at wilkesncrod.org. Mismatches usually trace to an unrecorded transfer or a name change.

When does the Wilkes County Register of Deeds close?

At 4:55 p.m., Monday through Friday. The doors open at 8:30 a.m. and close for holidays.

How can I search Wilkes County deeds from home?

Use wilkesncrod.org, the register's site that has been online since July 1, 2017. The tax office also has a limited deed copy tool for finding legal descriptions.

What year do Wilkes County land records start?

1778, when the county was formed. Births and deaths begin in 1913, and marriage licenses in 1882.

Do I pay to record a loan release in Wilkes County?

No. The statewide fee schedule sets no charge for a satisfaction or cancellation of a mortgage or deed of trust.

Who owes the excise tax on a Wilkes County deed?

The seller. It is paid to the register of deeds before the deed is recorded.

What is the Wilson County Register of Deeds office for?

The Register of Deeds keeps Wilson County's real property and vital records. Its county page says the office records deeds, deeds of trust, mortgage cancellations, powers of attorney, maps and many other documents.

The same office issues marriage licenses and holds the county's birth, death and marriage files, plus military discharges and notary oaths. For a house sale, only the real property side matters: the deed that moves title and the deed of trust that secures a buyer's loan both end up here. State law makes the register an elected county officer, chosen every two years by the county's voters (G.S. 161-1).

The phone line is 252-399-2935, and the county says marriage license visits and vital record amendments are scheduled by phone through that number.

What records can I search online for Wilson County?

The online search holds Wilson County's real estate indexes back to 1974, and the office says it is still scanning older documents so that their images can be viewed online. For an older chain of title, expect to ask the office for images that are not yet online.

Useful lookups before a sale include:

  • The current deed, to confirm how the owners' names appear.
  • Any deed of trust, to see whether a lender still has a lien.
  • Recorded cancellations, which show that an old loan was released.
  • Maps and plats that describe the lot lines.

Title searches for a closing are normally ordered by the closing attorney, but a quick index search lets an owner spot a stale lien early.

What must a deed carry to be recorded in Wilson County?

A deed has to carry a statement about delinquent property tax before the register accepts it. The county's deed requirements page says this rule dates from October 1, 2014 and rests on G.S. 161-31, which names Wilson County and which the commissioners implemented by resolution on December 6, 2004.

The county describes two routes. In the first, the paper is taken to the tax department's Collections Division, where a clerk confirms that no delinquent tax is owed. The attorney should have the parcel number printed on the deed or on hand. In the second, the attorney fills in the statement with his or her own name, and the deed can go straight to the register.

The county asks for separate checks, one for taxes owed and one for the Register of Deeds' recording fees. The tax department's number for questions is 252-399-2900, option 2.

What are the filing charges at the Wilson County counter?

Every register in the state charges the same amounts, Wilson County included. the statewide fee statute prices an ordinary document at $26.00 and covers 15 pages in that price. A loan security document starts at $64.00 and includes 35 pages. Extra pages on either are $4.00 apiece.

Recording fees printed in G.S. 161-10
ItemFee as printed
Ordinary instrument, 15 pages included$26.00 base, $4.00 for each page beyond

The statute calls these fees complete and exclusive, and they are collected before the document is filed. Nonstandard documents add $25.00, and each extra instrument in one document adds $10.00.

Which side pays the Wilson County deed stamp tax?

The seller does. The state levy runs $1.00 for each $500 or fraction of value passing, and the excise tax statute puts the payment on the transferor, due to the register before filing.

One half is retained by the county and the other half is sent to the state monthly. Your closing attorney calculates it and deducts it at settlement, so ask for the exact number.

Why does recording order matter in Wilson County?

Protection against outside claims starts at registration in the land's home county. G.S. 47-18 says contracts to convey, options, leases over three years and conveyances are not valid against lien creditors or purchasers for value except from the time of registration, and priority follows the order of registration.

So a seller who signs on Friday and a buyer who records the following week are both better off if the closing office records the same day. A seller who also owes tax should note that a deed with an unrecorded tax statement cannot be filed in Wilson County.

Does the Wilson County register also handle vital records?

Yes, and the office's notice board shows how its services are shifting. Certified copies of birth, death and marriage records can be ordered online, with pickup orders confirmed by a phone call, or requested by mail.

A county notice also says that from January 1, 2026, adopted people born in Wilson County can request new birth certificates directly from the register, in person only, under Senate Bill 248. Marriage license applicants print and fill out the application first, then call to book a visit, and only the couple attends. None of this affects a sale, but it explains why the front counter can be busy.

Can I order a certified copy of a deed here?

Search the online index first, since it lists real estate documents back to 1974, then request an image or a certified copy from the office. A certified copy runs $5.00 for its first page and $2.00 for each page that follows.

Deeds before the online coverage may be missing from the images, and in that case a phone call to 252-399-2935 gets a clerk looking for the book and page. Heirs often need the deed that put title in the decedent's name, so order early to avoid delay in the contract period.

What mistakes slow down a deed in Wilson County?

Most delays come from the tax statement, not the recording itself. A deed brought to the register without either of the two tax options will not be accepted for recording, so the attorney has to go back to the tax department first.

Other frequent snags:

  • One check covering both taxes and recording fees, when the county asks for separate ones.
  • A missing parcel number, which slows the clerk's delinquent tax check.
  • A deed of trust left open after payoff, which keeps showing as a lien in the index.

If you hold a house inherited from a relative, the names on the last recorded deed may differ from the heirs. Sort that out with an attorney before a buyer's lender asks.

What should a Wilson County seller do before closing?

Gather the paperwork in the order the office will ask for it. For scale, the Census Bureau, the county counts 38,463 housing units and 411 building permits in 2025, so deeds move through the office steadily.

  • Find the parcel number in the county tax records.
  • Confirm the delinquent tax statement route with the closing attorney.
  • Bring two checks, one to the tax department and one to the register.
  • Ask whether any old deed of trust still needs a recorded cancellation.

Where is a Wilson County deed filed?

With the county Register of Deeds, reachable at 252-399-2935. For a sale, the closing attorney usually files it.

Does Wilson County require a tax statement on the deed?

Yes. The county accepts a deed only if it carries one of its two delinquent tax options, either verified by a tax department clerk or completed by the attorney.

What fee applies to a general deed in Wilson County?

An ordinary document costs $26.00 with 15 pages included, and each page past that adds $4.00. Loan security papers start at $64.00.

Who owes the excise tax on a Wilson County sale?

The seller, who pays the register before the deed is filed.

What does the Yadkin County Register of Deeds handle?

This office in Yadkinville keeps the county's land records: deeds, deeds of trust, maps and related filings. State law opens those records to public inspection. The staff also copy and certify birth, death and marriage certificates, issue marriage licenses and swear in notaries.

A sale is only fully protected once the deed is on the books. Under G.S. 47-18, an unregistered conveyance loses to lien creditors and later buyers who paid value, and whoever registers first generally ranks first.

The county web page urges electronic recording for every document. Marriage licenses and notary oaths run by appointment through 336-849-7904. The register of deeds is an elected post, and the excise tax on deeds is collected at this same counter.

How does a deed get on record after a Yadkin County sale?

Usually the attorney or title company at the closing table sends it electronically. The register accepts every document type except maps by e-recording. Any firm wanting to submit must go through Simplifile, CSC or ePN and complete a submitter agreement that the provider passes to the county.

The Yadkin County tax office page has a one-line instruction for deed work: consult your attorney, then it links to the Register of Deeds. Sellers in Yadkinville, Jonesville, East Bend or on a rural road in between therefore rarely deal with the recording desk themselves.

  • Ask whether your closing firm already has an e-recording agreement with Yadkin County.
  • Find out who is writing the check for the excise tax, since the statute assigns it to the seller.
  • Keep the recording confirmation as proof of the date and time of registration.
  • Bringing paper instead? Phone the office before you drive, because no walk-in recording hours appear on the county page.

What does recording cost at the Yadkin County Register of Deeds?

A single statewide schedule applies here. G.S. 161-10 prints one schedule for the whole state, calls it complete and exclusive, and requires payment up front.

Register of Deeds charges in G.S. 161-10 that touch a house sale
DocumentAmount printed
Deed, pages 1 through 15$26.00
Mortgage, pages 1 through 35$64.00
Overflow pages on either$4.00 each
Paying off a mortgage (satisfaction)Free
Certified copy of a recorded deed$5.00 plus $2.00 per added page
Nonstandard document$25.00 added

Count the pages in your deed and exhibits before closing, because the $4.00 charge starts on the sixteenth page of a general instrument.

Who owes the excise stamp on a Yadkin County deed?

The person transferring the house. G.S. 105-228.30 puts the rate at one dollar per five hundred dollars of value. Payment is due at the register's counter ahead of the filing.

Collections are divided evenly. Half stays with the county. The state's half is remitted monthly, and the county may retain 2 percent of it. The closing statement lists the dollar figure that applies to your price.

If a house passes as a gift or between relatives, ask the office how a stated value is treated before anyone signs.

Where does the tax office fit in with the Register of Deeds?

They are separate counters. The Yadkin County Tax Department in Yadkinville lists and bills property, takes exemption applications and keeps the parcel maps. The register of deeds only records the paper. The tax office page announces a 2027 revaluation and points deed questions back to an attorney and the Register of Deeds.

For billing and payment questions, the tax office takes calls at 336-849-7903. It lists an August discount of 2 percent, plus a solid waste fee of $76.00 per household, or $38.00 with the elderly exemption. Statewide, taxes fall due September 1, and interest starts January 6 (G.S. 105-360).

Which other documents are recorded at the Yadkin County Register of Deeds?

More than deeds. Under G.S. 47-18, options, leases beyond three years and rights of first refusal must be registered before they bind a later buyer. A seller who gave a buyer an option months ago should check that it was recorded, since an unrecorded one may not hold up against a new purchaser.

A seller-financed sale is the other case worth knowing. North Carolina's Chapter 47H covers a contract for deed with five or more payments, where the seller keeps title. Written and acknowledged terms are required, the buyer gets a three-business-day cancellation window, and the seller records the contract or a memorandum within five business days. A forfeiture notice has to allow at least 30 days to cure (Chapter 47H).

  • Satisfactions of a deed of trust record for no fee under G.S. 161-10, so paying off a mortgage costs nothing at this office.
  • For a parcel split between counties, the excise tax goes to the county holding the greater value.
  • An estate sale may require a small estate affidavit to list each tract the decedent owned.

What does the Yadkin County housing picture look like?

The Census Bureau's mid-2025 estimate for Yadkin County is 38,325 people, a 3.0 percent gain over 2020 that has not quite regained the 38,406 of 2010. About 111 people live on each of its 334.94 land square miles, and there are 17,697 housing units.

Owners live in 76.9 percent of Yadkin County homes. Survey data for 2020 to 2024 show a median home value of $181,200, owner costs of $1,177 monthly with a mortgage, and rent of $766. Households earn a median $62,932, and 14.5 percent of people fall below the poverty line. Adults 65 and over are 22.4 percent of residents and 1,966 are veterans, so the age-based and veteran programs reach many owners.

Employers numbered 650 in 2023 with 8,235 jobs among them, and the average commute is 29.6 minutes. New construction is slow, with 116 building permits in 2025. Many sales involve inherited or older houses; for an estate, the clerk of superior court can say who has authority to sign.

How do Yadkin County's economy and demographics shape a home sale?

Retail sales were $338,224 thousand in 2022, or $9,018 per resident, according to the Census Bureau, a lower per-person figure than a county with a large shopping district would show. Health care and social assistance brought in receipts of $66,701 thousand and transportation and warehousing $57,494 thousand. The county had 2,727 nonemployer businesses in 2024, which fits a place with many self-employed households.

Of adults 25 and older, 86.6 percent hold a high school diploma and 17.5 percent a bachelor's degree. Home internet is common, with 87.9 percent of households subscribed to broadband, a point for buyers planning to work from home.

For a seller, the practical point is a buyer pool drawn from nearby employers and commuters. Owners facing a tax lien can look at the county's Tax Foreclosure Sales page to see how auctions are listed, and redemption remains possible before a sale is confirmed.

More questions about Yadkin County, NC Register of Deeds

Does Yadkin County charge a transfer tax on a sale?

Yes. The seller owes a deed excise tax, paid to the register at filing. The rate is one dollar for each five hundred dollars of value.

Can a Yadkin County deed be recorded electronically?

Yes, any document except a map. The attorney or title company must first sign a submitter agreement through Simplifile, CSC or ePN. For paper filings, phone 336-849-7904.

Does it cost anything to record a satisfaction of a mortgage in Yadkin County?

No. G.S. 161-10 sets no charge for a satisfaction, so the payoff paperwork is free to file.

How long does a buyer under a Yadkin County contract for deed have to cancel?

Through midnight of the third business day. After that, the seller has a five-business-day window to record.

Is a Yadkin County revaluation coming?

Yes, the county tax page says a 2027 revaluation is underway. Counties must reappraise all real estate on an eight-year cycle at the longest.
